Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture
Zhi Lü; Jun Ma; Qiangbo Tan

We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(χ(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
Brennan's Conjecture and the Universal Integral Means Spectrum
Ilia Binder; Oleg Ivrii; Istvan Prause; Stanislav Smirnov

In October 2026, OpenAI released two preprints \cite{openai-brennan,openai-kraetzer}, establishing Brennan's celebrated conjecture~\cite{brennan,brennan2} and disproving Kraetzer's more general $t^2/4$ conjecture \cite{kraetzer, kraetzer-thesis}. While validating these results, we observed that much of their argument is redundant and arrived at a drastically shorter proof of a significantly stronger statement. The goal of this note is to give a short and concise presentation of the reborn proof, sacrificing some of the context and consequences for brevity, and relegating them to a follow-up work. In this particular case the human-AI interaction was fruitful and quite satisfactory, and hoping for a similar future in other subjects, we would paraphrase Rick Blaine: {\em ``AI, we hope this is the beginning of a beautiful friendship.''}
Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Ampère Equations

We prove a Harnack inequality on Monge--Ampère gradient graphs under suitable geometric bounds, giving us interior $L^\infty$ estimates for the linearized Monge--Ampère equation. The proof combines Moser iteration on extrensic balls with a gradient estimate for the extrinsic distance function. The argument avoids the Caffarelli--Gutiérrez Harnack inequality and the engulfing and covering properties of Monge--Ampère sections.
Identifiability from Moments in Independent Component Analysis Mixture Models
Pardis Semnani; Konstantin Usevich; Elina Robeva

We study Independent Component Analysis (ICA) mixture models. These models consist of mixtures of ICA densities. An ICA density is associated with a random vector whose coordinates become mutually independent after an invertible linear transformation. ICA mixture models are nonparametric extensions of the celebrated family of Gaussian mixtures. We show that in many cases the ICA mixtures are identifiable from the collection of the observed moment tensors, that is, the mixing coefficients, linear transformations, and source moments of order up to $d$ can be identified from the moment tensors of order up to $d$ for generic parameters. We address the problem by studying the corresponding secant varieties and their algebraic properties such as dimensions and Gauss maps. In particular, for $n$-variate distributions, we establish that generically and up to the trivial scaling and permutation symmetries, when $d\geq 5$, the parameters can be recovered uniquely for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ mixture components. For $d=3,4$, we show identifiability up to a finite equivalence class for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ and $0.5 n^{d-2}/d!$ components respectively, where for $d=4$ the mixing coefficients need to be known a priori. The obtained bounds on the component numbers have the maximum possible orders in $n$, and for $d = 3$ and $d\geq 5$, they are also asymptotically sharp.
Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models

We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.
Canonical Layer Inference for Deep Gaussian Processes via Symmetry-Breaking Augmentation

Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are flexible priors for compositional regression functions, but inference for intermediate layers faces questions. The basic obstruction is an adjacent-layer symmetry: applying an invertible transformation and its inverse to two adjacent layers leaves the composed regression map unchanged. Under explicit symmetry and prior-comparability conditions, we show that the posterior may not concentrate on any prescribed intermediate-layer representation, even when the composed regression function is estimable. We then introduce an augmented $ρ$-fractional posterior that reweights layer decompositions by a non-saturating identity-deviation penalty. The augmentation changes posterior odds between symmetry-related decompositions by an exponential penalty ratio. Under proper choices of the penalty and a prior mass condition, it preserves function-level fractional posterior contraction, while shrinking the redundant layers towards the identity mapping. Thus, the likelihood does not identify a unique ``true'' set of layers; the augmentation favors identity-biased parsimonious decompositions within an equivalence class of layers; uniqueness of a selected representative is not established.
A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
Marco Delgado-Garrido; Lars Moberg Salbu; Alvaro Torras-Casas; Rocio Gonzalez-Diaz

We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.
Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems

We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic.
 To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.
A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses

We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.
A generalised and modular proof-theoretic semantics for sequent systems
Victor Barroso-Nascimento; Arghya Chakrabarty; Elaine Pimentel

Base-extension semantics explains logical consequence via derivability in atomic systems. Extending this approach across logics requires careful control of structural principles and contexts. We present a modular sequent-based framework in which support is indexed by multisets of atomic resources and the semantic clauses for connectives are guided by their left introduction rules. The framework separates additive from multiplicative behaviour and makes explicit the contributions of structural rules and restrictions on sequents. We establish soundness and completeness for classical and intuitionistic propositional logic and for multiplicative-additive fragments of classical and intuitionistic linear logic. We then investigate axiomatic extensions of intuitionistic logic through Jankov logic. Two classes of atomic bases yield sound and complete semantics. Completeness is proven using two novel and modular methods using simulation bases, one of which is constructive. These results provide a common semantic treatment of several logical systems while identifying the additional conditions needed to extend the framework beyond structural variations.
Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing elastic particles

This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $γ=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size.
 For $γ=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $γ\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ and $γ=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $γ=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
On extremal problems related to the Krzyż conjecture
Sarah May Instanes; Adrián Llinares; Dragan Vukotić

We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzyż conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzyż case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzyż problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzyż conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzyż problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.

The Wronski map is a central object of study in osculating Schubert calculus, and has been the focus of much work in real algebraic geometry over the last few decades due to its remarkable reality properties. In this work, we study it over arbitrary fields through the lens of quadratically-enriched enumerative geometry. A basic obstruction is that the Wronski map is not oriented in general, so existing approaches do not apply directly. To that end, we introduce twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of finite flat lci maps of schemes, which generalize ordinary $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees by allowing us to twist an orientation by the equation of a divisor, and $\mathbb{A}^1$-chambers, which generalize the notion of connected component of a real manifold.
 We then show that a certain weighted count of the fibers of the Wronski map depends only on the action of the absolute Galois group of the base field on the roots of the Wronski polynomial. This unifies Eremenko and Gabrielov's work on real degrees of Wronski maps, Levinson and Purbhoo's work on the character orientation of the real Wronski map, and Brazelton's work on enriched degrees of Wronski maps into one framework.
Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM

Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_α$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[Δ_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.
Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods
Nilasis Chaudhuri; Piotr B. Mucha; Tomasz Piasecki; Jiakun Yang

This paper is concerned with the conditional Hölder regularity of the temperature for the heat-conducting compressible Navier-Stokes system, where the pressure takes a complete form that includes the Stefan-radiation correction. Under minimal assumptions on the density and velocity, we prove that any weak solution automatically exhibits Hölder continuity in the temperature component. This constitutes the main result of the work and is achieved by an application of the De Giorgi method. As a consequence of this conditional regularity, we establish the global-in-time existence of a regular, unique solution to a simplified system for the compressible potential flow of a heat-conducting fluid, valid for arbitrarily large initial data.

In a GCD ring $R$, every pair of elements $a,b\in R$ admits a greatest common divisor $\text{gcd}(a,b)$ and a least common multiple $\text{lcm}(a,b)$. Motivated by a question on Mathematics Stack Exchange by Ash Seifert~\cite{Sei22}, I introduce the notion of an lcm splitting $c,d\in R$ for $a,b$ satisfying $cd\sim\text{lcm}(a,b), c\mid a, d\mid b, \text{gcd}(c,d)\sim1$. I show that adequate Bézout domains always admit lcm splittings, give examples of Bézout domains in which some pair has no lcm splitting, and make further remarks on this seemingly new property.
A duality principle for the neighbourhood of manifolds and applications to counting rational points near curves

In this paper, we establish a duality principle relating the count of rationals near a manifold to a sparse counting problem for the dual. As applications, we give a short, self-contained proof of sharp bounds for planar curves under minimal regularity conditions and similarly, sharp upper bounds for non- degenerate space curves, again under minimal curvature conditions. This work recovers and extends the works of Beresnevich, Dickinson and Velani and of Vaughan and Velani on planar curves and independently proves and extends the results of Chen, Seeger, Srivastava and Technau on space curves, while providing a structural picture well-suited for generalisations. The re- sults and methods of this work precede the emergence of highly capable AI models.
Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers

We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.
Revisiting separators in string graphs, region intersection graphs, and induced-minor-free graphs
James Davies; Paweł Rzążewski; Jack Spalding-Jamieson; Bartosz Walczak

String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced vertex separators of size $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m})$ and conjectured that this bound can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families. A key intermediate step in Lee's approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs. In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee's approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. These results have since found applications in a wide range of works.
 Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee's padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee's as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov's separator results, and many works relying on them.
 In this work, we prove that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced separators of size $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, and more generally obtain analogous $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$ bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works. Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time.
 Our proof uses a different approach from Lee's and does not rely on padded decompositions. Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs.
 We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib.
Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture

For a set $V$ of $n$ distinct positive integers, let $\mathrm{ML}(V)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $V$, \[ \mathrm{ML}(V)>\frac{1+c}{2n}. \] The proof combines a refinement of the large GCD argument of Green and Walker with a new physical spillover inequality for interval multiplicities.
Parametric Resonance in Primal-Dual Learning for Slowly Non-Stationary Constrained MDPs

Primal-dual methods for constrained Markov decision processes are analyzed under a two-timescale assumption, with non-stationarity entering through two channels. In the additive channel, where the constraint level oscillates, the dual oscillation saturates at a floor set by the moving optimum and is amplified linearly by the timescale ratio. In the parametric channel, where the constraint sensitivity oscillates, a coherent modulation carries no resonant forcing at any depth: the dual update's stiffness modulation cancels the primal update's damping modulation. Instability instead comes from a mismatch between the constraint estimate used by the primal update and the measurement used by the dual update, producing a parametric resonance at twice the pair's natural frequency. The tolerated mismatch grows with the square root of the forcing bandwidth and collapses with the square root of the dual-to-primal step-size ratio. These results hold on the tangent linear-quadratic reduction around an active saddle, for one constraint and for $K$ constraints under a common modulation and an isotropy condition. Driving both updates from the same estimate removes the resonant forcing but introduces a stationary offset equal to the estimator's bias. In a Lagrangian soft actor-critic agent, the multiplier locks onto the sub-harmonic at the timescale ratios its identified linear loop predicts and a coherent cost critic suppresses the lock-in, while a proportional (PID) term, predicted to leave the lock-in in place, suppresses most of it through the projection of the multiplier.
Feasible closed form moment matching for scenario generation through covariance rotations

Closed form moment matching constructs small scenario sets without numerical optimisation. We study two generators that match the mean, the covariance matrix, and the marginal third and fourth moments. Both place their scenarios along the columns of a covariance factor, usually the symmetric or Cholesky root. Although every valid factor reproduces the same covariance matrix, its choice can determine whether the resulting weights are nonnegative. By viewing each column as a univariate mixture component, Pearson's inequality gives the minimum probability needed to reproduce its assigned variance, skewness, and kurtosis, which leads to exact feasibility conditions whenever the relevant entrywise powers are nonsingular. The effect of the factor is governed by its entrywise fourth powers, whose sum can vary by a factor equal to the dimension. This explains why standard roots fail in high dimension. We combine these results into a rotated moment matching procedure that searches for feasible factors without altering the target moments. Applied to stock returns and synthetic data, the procedure produces valid probabilities for both generators in nearly every instance considered, and it outperforms the original constructions, whose standard factors give invalid weights in most of them. Finally, the two asset case explains when such a rotation exists. With symmetric marginals, a suitable rotation reaches Pearson's bound except in one degenerate case, whereas with skewness the factor must balance the allocation of third and fourth moments, and some attainable targets admit no feasible rotation. We also establish a sufficient condition for arbitrary correlation and equal marginal kurtosis.
Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations

We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $α\in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $α\in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.
Error analysis of a backward L2 method on graded meshes for linear and semilinear subdiffusion equations

Time-fractional linear and semilinear parabolic equations with a Caputo time derivative of order $α\in(0,1)$ are considered. Their solutions exhibit an initial singularity of type $t^σ$ for any fixed $σ\in (0,1) \cup (1,2)$. A backward L2-type discrete fractional-derivative operator of order $3-α$ is considered on nonuniform temporal meshes. Sufficient conditions for inverse monotonicity of this operator areestablished. Hence, sharp pointwise-in-time error bounds are obtained on graded temporal meshes with arbitrary degree of grading. The theoretical findings are illustrated by numerical experiments.
Dg models for derived differential operators
Jack Jeffries; Devlin Mallory; Claudia Miller; Josh Pollitz; Eamon Quinlan-Gallego

We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.
Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models

We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincaré inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.
Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
Anming Gu; Bobby Shi; Kevin Tian; Hubert Yang

We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m δ)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{ω- 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $δ$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $δ= \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $Ω(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincaré constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.
Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map

We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugallé and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted étale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.
Robust Local Fréchet Regression: Nonasymptotic Theory and Minimax Optimality

We develop robust local Fréchet regression for heavy-tailed responses in a general metric space and propose a distance-based median-of-means estimator. We derive nonasymptotic pointwise high-probability bounds separately under local second-order smoothness and local $1$-Wasserstein Hölder continuity, and show that the corresponding optimized rates match the classical pointwise rates for nonparametric regression. We also establish matching pointwise minimax lower bounds over embedded Gaussian regression subclasses. Remarkably, our results do not require an entropy condition on the response space. Simulation studies with positive-definite matrix-valued responses, together with a real-data application involving Wasserstein-valued responses, illustrate the robustness--efficiency tradeoff and practical performance of the proposed estimator.
The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments

Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$
 C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.
Asymptotic stability of a Bloch skyrmion for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation

We prove the asymptotic stability of isolated skyrmions under the flow of the two-dimensional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. We consider a micromagnetic energy functional involving the exchange energy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and the Zeeman interaction. We are interested in the stability of chiral Bloch skyrmions, which are local minimizers of this energy. We prove that data in H2 which are near in the skyrmion in a slighlty stronger than H1 sense, converge with exponential rate, in H2, to the skyrmion, up to a change of gauge.
Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential

We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.
Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
Xiaoli Li; Qianqian Lei; Ziyang Wei; Wei Biao Wu

With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.
From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling

Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions.
 First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L. Price moves during the execution window are part of that P&L, so executing more slowly reduces its variance, and because impact is concave it can also lower cost per share. Urgency comes only from alpha realized while the order is being worked. The problem is governed by the signs of two quantities: (i) the duration elasticity of impact $a$, which under a structural prior equals the impact-persistence gap $β- H$ and can take either sign; and (ii) the net urgency $ν$, the rate of alpha realization net of exposure relief. When $ν$ keeps its sign over the window, an interior optimum exists, to leading order in $T/t_f$, only when both are positive; otherwise the order should be worked at the fastest or slowest admissible pace. In the interior regime the first-order condition involves no impact coefficient, order size or volume, and the objective is flat: for a large-cap example, the window within 1% of maximal Sharpe spans more than an order of magnitude.

The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.

We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code. The constructions are the result of a computer search executing a tabu search algorithm.

Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy

With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude information networks (LAINs) must provide reliable communication, environmental sensing, and target identification to support efficient and safe airspace operation. Although integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) provides a foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing, identification must also be incorporated to meet airspace safety and regulatory requirements. Building on these, we introduce ISCAI, focusing on a backscatter communication (BackCom)-based identification mechanism in which backscatter devices serve as electronic license plates for aircraft. We present system and signal models for integrated sensing and identification (ISAI) and ISCAI, together with multifunctional receiver designs and mutual integration gains. Finally, we discuss open problems and future directions, including an information-theoretic framework, artificial intelligence-empowered system design, and reconfigurable intelligent surface-enhanced ISCAI. Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), such as Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, can provide consistent coverage for Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, particularly in rural areas where cellular coverage is lacking. These IoT nodes are used to monitor and record their surroundings, supporting various applications, including real-time applications. In such cases, transmission of the most up-to-date data is essential, making the Age of Information (AoI) a critical metric to consider. The AoI measures the elapsed time from the data generation at the source node to its reception at the destination. Moreover, the Peak AoI (PAoI), which denotes the maximum AoI in the system before an update is received, provides valuable insights into the network's performance. Therefore, this encourages us to focus on the PAoI within a large-scale and fully loaded IoT network, which is covered by LEOSATs. Using tools from stochastic geometry, this paper derives the spatial distribution of the uplink mean PAoI in a LEOSAT-enabled IoT network. To achieve that purpose, the meta distribution of the uplink conditional coverage probability is derived. Numerical results articulate how varying the number of deployed LEOSATs and their altitudes affects the coverage probability meta distribution and the spatial distribution of the mean PAoI. Additionally, by examining various scenarios with different numbers of LEOSATs and altitudes, we can derive valuable insights to determine the optimal beamwidth for LEOSATs tailored to each specific scenario to minimize the conditional mean PAoI.

Our proof overcomes this difficulty through a level-set approach: it relies on a flux identity for the eigenvalue, for which a variational interpretation re-emerges in the special case where the domain is a ball.

For a locally Gorenstein module $X\in{\rm mod}\ Λ$ we construct $\underline{χ}_X$ a subcategory of $\underline{\rm mod}$ $Λ$ and we prove that the syzygy functor is faithful and full on $\underline{χ}_X$. The results obtained in this paper provide a generalization of some geometric inequalities to the class of log-concave functions. They describe the relationships between the Quermassintegrals of functions and bodies, giving estimates for constants involved in functional Shephard-type problems.

As a further application, we show that for every uniformly bounded representation of a compact extension of an abelian topological group on any separable Banach space, there exists an equivalent invariant strictly convex norm.

We generalize the results of Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis, which lift odd mod $p$ Galois representations to geometric $p$-adic representations, to geometric lifting theorems for mod $p^n$ representations whose mod $p$ reduction is odd.

For both the convex range $m>1$ and the concave range $0<m<1$, we obtain sharp Sobolev regularity in terms of the order $m$. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.

We also consider the problem of bounding the number of empty pentagons and hexagons in terms of the number of interior and boundary points of $S$. While the hexagon bound is weak, it offers a potential step toward a superlinear lower bound. On the other hand, the two-parameter bound for pentagons, combined with the structural results on $C$-sets, yields a simple proof of an $Ω(n^{3/2})$ bound for the number of pentagons. While this is a significant improvement over previously published bounds, a recent preprint \cite{Astudillo2026} attains a better bound using completely different methods. Closed geodesics on compact semi-Riemannian manifolds

We study the existence of closed geodesics on compact quotients of Lie groups endowed with left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics. We construct a compact, geodesically complete pseudo-Riemannian manifold that admits no closed geodesics. We also establish the existence of closed geodesics in several settings, with particular focus on the Lorentzian case.
A Mixed Elliptic--Hyperbolic Monge--Ampère Problem: Modeling and a Least-Squares Solver
G. V. Carvalho; M. J. H. Anthonissen; J. H. M. ten Thije Boonkkamp; L. Kusch; W. L. IJzerman

We consider a transport problem motivated by freeform optical design of a parallel-to-far-field reflector. Numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to compute both isolated and periodic mixed-type transport solutions, yielding smooth reflector configurations.

Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.
Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling Models: Taxonomy, Classification and Open Challenges
Margarida Caleiras; Paulo Jorge Nascimento; Samuel Moniz

Over the past three decades, a large number of optimization models have been proposed for Earth observation satellite (EOS) scheduling. The main goal of this paper is to provide an overview of these models and to relate them to the characteristics of the problems they address. To do so, we first identify the main features of EOS scheduling problems and those with the most impact on the computational complexity of the model. Based on these features, we propose a new taxonomy of satellite agility and a classification of EOS scheduling problems that allows the problem under study to be clearly identified. We then propose a classification of the optimization models into five categories, based on their time and event representations, and describe representative formulations of each category in a unified notation, together with their extensions, discussing the respective advantages and limitations. The trade-offs between the alternative representations are analyzed, showing that discrete-time formulations allow time-dependent parameters, such as transition times and image quality, to be pre-computed, which preserves the linearity of the model but makes its size depend on the adopted discretization, whereas continuous-time formulations treat these parameters as functions of the start times, which introduces nonlinearities unless simplifying assumptions are adopted. Primal-dual forward-reflected splitting with linesearch for distributed min-max problems under local Lipschitz smoothness
Felipe Atenas; Minh N. Dao; Matthew K. Tam; David Torregrosa-Belén

We consider a network of finitely many agents aiming to cooperatively solve a convex-concave min-max problem combining nonsmooth terms with a smooth saddle function whose partial gradients are only locally Lipschitz continuous. Without requiring prior knowledge of the local Lipschitz moduli of the partial gradients, we propose a distributed proximal-reflected-gradient algorithm which incorporates a distributed backtracking procedure to adjust the stepsizes at each iteration. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.
Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions

We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.
mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras

We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.
Weighted spatial averages with missing observations: Convergence and accuracy of delta-method variance approximations

Lydia Boubendir; Peter Constantin; Hezekiah Grayer; Zhongtian Hu

We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,α}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. For the biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces, we construct a nonconforming finite element method that requires neither stabilization nor the Piola transform. Stability of Hyperplane Projections of the Regular Simplex and $L_p$-Projection Bodies of balls in $\ell_q^n(\mathbb{R})$

We prove stability estimates for extremal hyperplane projections of the regular simplex. We further generalize the analogous stability estimates for $\ell_q$-balls by the first named author and the monotonicity theorem for normalized ratios by Barthe and Naor to the $L_p$-setting. To this end, we derive closed formulas for the support functions of their $L_p$-projection bodies, complementing those obtained by the second named author. Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. Huihui An; Zaili Yan; Hui Zhang; Shaoxiang Zhang

We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.
Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings

For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.
Jianfeng Hou; Caiyun Hu; Hezhi Wang

We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of every fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $δ(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. The constant is best possible. This settles the remaining cases $\ell=5,7,\ldots,71$ and completes the determination of the thresholds for all odd cycles. The proof combines the condensation approach of Bryant et al. with a sharp weighted-triangle fractional decomposition theorem. Its key step is a rescaling of the dual edge weights that allows us to apply a quantitative discharging estimate from the breakthrough of Delcourt and Postle on Nash--Williams' triangle decomposition conjecture.
More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line

We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.
A Smaller Subspace is All You Need: Efficient ISAC Beamforming via Dimensionality Reduction
Ruiqi Liu; Yuanshuo Gang; Tianqi Mao; Qingqing Wu

Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a critical technology for the sixth generation (6G) wireless networks. Under monostatic sensing mode, achieving a balance between communication and sensing performance via optimal beamforming is a critical research problem. In multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems, such beamforming problems are of substantial computational complexity due to the large number of antennas. Existing methods exploit exact subspaces of lower dimensions to speed up the beamforming process where the complexity is proportional to the number of communication users and sensing targets instead of antennas. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the beamforming problem can be solved in an even lower-dimensional subspace with only a small sensing performance loss. Numerical results compare the sensing performance and computational complexity of ISAC beamforming problem in the exact subspace and smaller subspaces.
On MRD constacyclic codes over inseparable field extensions

In this paper, we construct MRD constacyclic codes of length $p$ over an inseparable field extension $L/K$, where $K$ has characteristic $p$. In particular, these codes cannot be obtained from known constructions.
Are Single-Leader-Multi-Follower Problems Particular Cases of Bilevel Optimization?
Didier Aussel; David Salas; Martin Schmidt

For more than 20 years, single-leader multi-follower (SLMF) problems have been treated as a more difficult class of problems in comparison to bilevel optimization. In this work we challenge this common belief, studying whether SLMF problems can be reformulated as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. We consider both optimistic and pessimistic formulations. For the optimistic case the answer is positive: We derive an equivalent bilevel problem by representing the followers' equilibria as fixed points of the solution mapping of a single optimization problem. For pessimistic problems, the situation is different. We show that every optimistic trilevel problem admits an equivalent pessimistic SLMF formulation with two followers. Conversely, for every pessimistic SLMF problem verifying a mild attainability assumption we establish an equivalent optimistic trilevel reformulation. The reformulations are easy, readily tractable, and they preserve convex and linear data. Thus, unless $\text{NP}=Σ_2^p$, we deduce as byproduct that multiple followers induce an unexpected complexity gap between optimistic and pessimistic approaches, which is not the case when considering one follower alone.

Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.
Fast matrix-vector products in tensor-train format via structured sketching
Alberto Bucci; Stefan Güttel; John W. Pearson

We propose a randomized, streamable algorithm that computes a tensor-train approximation of a matrix-vector product without ever forming the full intermediate tensor. We develop three contraction strategies for streaming tensor-train approximation (STTA): sequential, fused, and pre-sketched. We focus on the regime of large operator mode sizes and show that pre-sketching can provide significant speed-ups when a lower-rank approximation of the input is sought, by pre-computing all sketch-related contractions with the operator. The pre-sketched strategy can also accelerate successive randomized compression (SRC), although to a lesser extent since its second sweep depends on the input vector and cannot be pre-computed. We compare the three strategies in terms of computational cost and memory, and demonstrate their performance on synthetic and application-driven examples where rank reduction is relevant.
Trilinear Forms for ${\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ via conjugacy classes

It is well known that for a finite group \(G\), the number of elements in ${\rm Irr}(G)$ the set of irreducible representations up to isomorphism is the same as the number of elements in ${\rm Conj}(G)$ the set of conjugacy classes in $G$ although there is no natural bijection between these two sets. For $G={\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the finite field with $q$ elements, we give a bijection between ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Conj}(G)$, which behaves well with the tensor product of irreducible representations on one side and the product of conjugacy classes on the other. In particular, we relate the dimension of the trilinear forms with the multiplicity of the identity element in the triple product of the corresponding conjugacy classes.
Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the complex plane

This paper continues our previous work \cite{Miy6} on an extension of the Li--Mochizuki theorem concerning the existence and uniqueness of complete diagonal harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles over open Riemann surfaces. We consider the extended Hitchin equation associated with general subharmonic weight functions on the canonical bundle, not necessarily induced by holomorphic $r$-differentials. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for arbitrary subharmonic weight functions, without additional regularity assumptions on them. We also prove that, on the complex plane, such a complete solution exists whenever the weight function is not identically $-\infty$. Furthermore, if $(\varphi_ε)_{ε>0}$ is a family of smooth subharmonic weight functions decreasing to such a weight function $\varphi$ as $ε\searrow0$, the associated family of smooth complete solutions $(h_ε)_{ε>0}$ with $\det(h_ε)=1$ converges monotonically to the unique complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$ and satisfying $\det(h)=1$.
Minimum-Area Enclosing Rectangles and the First Neumann Eigenvalue of Planar Convex Domains
Xiaolong Li; Jin Sun; Kui Wang

Let $Ω$ be a bounded convex domain in the plane and let $R$ be a minimum-area rectangle containing $\overlineΩ$. We prove that if the ratio of the shorter side of $R$ to its longer side is at most $ρ\approx 0.443485$, then the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue of $Ω$ is bounded from below by that of $R$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $Ω$ coincides with the interior of $R$. The proof is based on a flux identity for the means of a test function over vertical sections of $Ω$, combined with weighted estimates involving the distributional second derivatives of the boundary functions. Finally, we show that the threshold $ρ\approx0.443485$ is nearly optimal by constructing, for every ratio in $(0.457994,1/2)$, trapezoids that are arbitrarily close to their minimum-area enclosing rectangle and for which the inequality fails.
Kumiko Nishioka; Taka-aki Tanaka; Yusuke Tanuma

This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications.
 In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemerédi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$.
 As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Hančl, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and Väänänen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.
Fluctuations of the planar random walk sausage

We establish fluctuation results for the volume of random walk sausage $R_n^{A}$ associated to a finite set $A\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$, where the underlying random walk $S$ has finite second moments. Precisely, we establish that the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and are described by the renormalized self intersection local time of planar Brownian motion, as in the cases of the range of random walks and the Wiener sausage. For any $N\ge1$, we also establish an asymptotic expansion of the expected volume of the form \begin{equation*}
 \mathbb{E}[R_n^{A}]=n\sum_{k=1}^N c(k,A,S)/(\log n)^k+O\left(n/(\log n)^{N+1}\right), \end{equation*} where the constants $c(k,A,S)$ depend only on the order $k$, the set $A$ and the distribution of $S$, and can be computed explicitly in terms of complete exponential Bell polynomials.

For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.
Cayley access models for matrix functions: reachable class and cost

We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials.
 We propose the Cayley transform, parameterized by $σ\in \mathbb{R}$ and $γ> 0$, as an alternative to the standard quantum access model. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally. This transformation converts Hermitian matrices to unitaries, allowing generalized quantum signal processing to apply Laurent polynomials bounded on the unit circle.
 We compare three access models (block encoding, matrix exponential, and Cayley encoding) in terms of query complexity and of the cost of their circuit realization. When the difficulty of $f$ is localized in the spectrum, the Cayley encoding reduces the required degree by a factor of three to four, and it represents the shifted resolvent exactly at degree one. For spectral projectors, the standard models cannot reach the target accuracy at fixed degree, because their approximants cannot concentrate resolution near the discontinuity.
 Realizing the Cayley encoding from a block encoding requires solving a shifted linear system, whose cost offsets its query-complexity gain over the standard models. For structured matrices arising in practice, however, low-depth circuits for the encoding can be constructed directly, and the gain is preserved at the circuit level.
Accelerated Born series for high-frequency strong scattering by weakly non-radial media

We present a practical method for accelerating the modified Born series for high-frequency Helmholtz scattering in one, two, and three dimensions. We consider bounded, nonnegative, compactly supported media, allowing small departures from radial symmetry in two and three dimensions. The method selects a single complex relaxation parameter using an approximation of the scattering operator's spectrum. Starting from precomputed eigenvalues for a constant reference medium, we estimate their evolution towards the prescribed radial profile. A leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation reduces this spectral propagation to scalar nonlinear equations, followed by a first-order correction for the nonradial part of the medium. The estimated eigenvalues, together with a bound on the omitted spectrum, define a convex minimax problem for selecting the relaxation parameter. This spectral preparation is independent of the source and can therefore be reused for multiple scattering problems in the same medium. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence in strongly scattering cases where the scattering operator has spectral radius greater than one. Comparisons with direct integral-equation and finite-difference solvers assess accuracy, residual convergence, and computation time, and show computational savings at comparable accuracy in selected examples.
The nearest neighbor interchange proximity measure for the tree-basedness of rooted binary phylogenetic networks

Tree-based networks are a broad graph class in phylogenetics which posit a model of evolution composed of tree-like processes and hybridization events. Hence, for any non-tree-based phylogenetic network, it is meaningful to study the magnitude of violation of the tree-based model assumptions. For rooted networks, we introduce the proximity measure delta_rNNI, defined by the minimum number of rooted nearest neighbor interchanges (NNIs) required to transform a network into a tree-based network. For binary networks, we prove that delta_rNNI is pairwise distinct from all previously known proximity measures in the literature and that no approximation guarantees between delta_rNNI and other known proximity measures holds. In addition, we characterize a family of networks for which a linear time lower bound on delta_rNNI is tight. Moreover, we analyze upper bounds and give an exact solution algorithm to compute delta_rNNI.

Let $Λ= \mathcal G_A (\mathbb F_q)$ be a minimal simply connected split Kac-Moody group of compact-hyperbolic type, and set $Γ=Λ/Z(Λ)$. We prove that $Γ$ is charfinite when $q\geq 11$, or when its Weyl group is $3$-spherical and $q\geq 4$. Here are a few consequences: the only characters of $Γ$ are the trivial and regular characters, every invariant random subgroup is supported on $\{e\}$ and $Γ$ and these are the only uniformly recurrent subgroups, and every nontrivial unitary $Γ$-representation weakly contains the regular representation. Our approach relies on a recent result due to Caprace and Thom, showing that the topological completions $G_+$ and $G_-$ associated to $Γ$ have the Howe-Moore property. We prove a criterion of charmenability for irreducible lattices with trivial amenable radical in products of Howe-Moore groups acting geometrically on proper hyperbolic spaces. The criterion requires the visual boundaries to be Poisson boundaries of suitable random walks and the corresponding lattice actions to be essentially free.
Entropy estimates and volume rigidity for graphs with positive Bakry-Émery curvature
Yanlong Ding; Shiping Liu; Chiyu Zhou

We establish a volume bound for weighted graphs with positive Bakry--Émery curvature through entropy estimates for the heat flow and characterize the equality case. As a consequence, if a connected unweighted graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfies the Bakry--Émery curvature--dimension condition $CD(2,\infty)$ with respect to the unnormalized Laplacian, then $$
 |V|\le 2^d, $$ where $d$ denotes the maximum degree. Equality holds if and only if $G$ is a hypercube. We also establish an analogous volume rigidity result for the normalized Laplacian.
Long-time existence of the Laplacian flow with Weyl tensor
Chuanhuan Li; Yi Li; Kai Zheng

We establish integral extension criteria for the Laplacian flow of closed $G_2$-structures on compact $7$-dimensional manifolds $M$. Assuming a uniform lower bound for the scalar curvature, we prove that a finite-time solution extends smoothly whenever the spatial $L^p$ norm of the $77$-dimensional Weyl component $W_{77}$ remains uniformly bounded for some $p\ge 7/2$. We also obtain a mixed space--time extension criterion under the condition \[ W_{77}\in L^q(0,T;L^p(M,g(t))), \qquad \frac{7}{2}<p<\infty,\quad 1\le q<\infty,\quad \frac{1}{q}+\frac{7}{p}\le 2. \] In particular, finite space-time $L^4$ integrability of $W_{77}$ is sufficient for extension.
Alberto Foresti; Giulio Franzese; Pietro Michiardi

Information-theoretic measures, such as Mutual Information (MI), play a crucial role in understanding non-linear relationships between random variables and are widely used across scientific disciplines. Yet, their use on real-world discrete data remains challenging. Existing methods typically rely on embedding discrete data into a continuous space and apply neural estimators originally designed for continuous distributions. This process requires careful engineering for both the embedding model and estimator architecture, but suffers from issues related to high data dimensionality. In this work, we introduce InfoSEDD, a discrete diffusion-based approach that bridges information-theoretic estimation and generative modeling such that they can be used to compute Kullback-Leibler divergences. Backed by Continuous Time Markov Chains theory principles, the design of InfoSEDD is lightweight and scalable and allows seamless integration with pretrained models. We showcase the versatility of our approach through applications on motif discovery in genetic promoter data, semantic-aware model selection in text summarization, and entropy estimation in Ising models. Finally, we construct consistency tests on real-world textual and genomics data. Our experiments demonstrate that InfoSEDD outperforms alternatives that rely on the "embedding trick". Our results position InfoSEDD as a robust and scalable tool for information-theoretic analysis of discrete data.
A Generating Polynomial for Convex Subsets of Posets

For any finite poset we define a generating polynomial counting upsets, downsets, and their intersection. We investigate the behaviour of this polynomial with respect to poset operations and show that it distinguishes certain posets constructed with the operations of ordinal sum and disjoint union, including Series-Parallel posets as a special case. Lastly, we comment on connections to the causal set approach to quantum gravity.
Testing Treatment Effect Heterogeneity with Functional Outcomes
Yongzhen Feng; Jie Li; Xiaojun Song

Assessing treatment-effect heterogeneity is important in causal inference, particularly for functional outcomes where effects may vary over time and the common effect is unknown. We propose a nonparametric procedure that assesses treatment-effect homogeneity through a testable marginal implication. By comparing within-arm difference distributions, the construction removes the unknown common functional effect without estimating it. We measure departures between these distributions through an integrated squared discrepancy of their characteristic functionals. A full-support Gaussian integrating measure yields an explicit bounded-kernel representation and identifies equality of the difference laws without requiring moment conditions on the outcomes. We construct an unbiased generalized U-statistic that accounts for dependence among overlapping differences, derive its null, fixed-alternative, and local-alternative limits, and develop a centered multiplier bootstrap for inference. The framework extends to multiple treatment arms with a shared control. For computation, a random-direction approximation combined with a nine-state recursion reduces the cost to linear order in the sample size for fixed numerical settings. Simulation studies assess the finite-sample performance of the proposed procedure relative to several benchmark methods. An application to the Irish gas smart-metering trial illustrates its use for assessing heterogeneity in functional treatment responses.
Nonlocal-to-local variational limits of energies on partitions
Roberto Alicandro; Giuliana Fusco; Chiara Leone

We study, through a $Γ$-convergence procedure, the asymptotic behaviour of a general class of nonlocal energies defined on functions taking values in a finite set $Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_N\}\subset\mathbb R^m$. These energies are written in terms of double integrals accounting for pairwise interactions in an open set $Ω$, weighted by a kernel $K_\varepsilon$. If the latter is controlled from above and below by suitable non-negative radial kernels with unit mass concentrating at the origin, then, up to subsequences, the $Γ$-limit has domain $BV(Ω;Y)$ and is given by a local surface energy. We show that the locality of the $Γ$-limit is not guaranteed if the concentration of mass fails. For a class of reference energies, we obtain a more explicit representation of the limit energy, also for non-radial kernels, recovering the limits of isotropic and anisotropic fractional perimeters. We also prove a homogenization result for periodic kernels.
Convergence rate of stochastic gradient descent under Łojasiewicz type condition and polynomially controlled noise

Stochastic gradient methods are widely used for solving optimization problems in many scientific fields. Recently, their popularity has risen due to the increase in machine learning's prominence. Their convergence is often studied under the convexity assumption, which is too restrictive in modern applications. In this paper, we investigate the almost sure convergence rate and expectation under a Łojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition. This framework includes both bounded and decaying noise, as well as noise with controlled polynomial growth. The obtained results extend existing convergence by allowing a broader class of noise sequences and explicitly capturing the effect of their asymptotic behavior on the convergence rate and applicability.
Spinors, Doppelgängers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy

We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelgänger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace
Ivan Kaygorodov; Abror Khudoyberdiyev; Zarina Shermatova

The Schrödinger--Witt algebras are infinite-dimensional Lie algebras of local dynamical symmetries of the free Schrödinger equation; they contain the Witt algebra of conformal transformations of the time line and appear in non-equilibrium statistical physics and in non-relativistic conformal field theory. We describe all quasi-derivations of the original and the twisted Schrödinger--Witt algebras. We prove that every quasi-derivation is the sum of a derivation, a trivial $\frac12$-derivation, a linear map with values in the center, and a finite linear combination of maps from three new families of quasi-derivations. As corollaries, we describe all $δ$-derivations, all $δ$-biderivations and all transposed $δ$-Poisson structures of the Schrödinger--Witt algebras. Finally, we prove that every quasi-derivation of the (original or twisted) extended Schrödinger--Witt algebra is the sum of an inner derivation and a multiple of the identity map. As a consequence, there are no nontrivial $δ$-derivations (for $δ\notin \{\frac12,1\}$), $δ$-biderivations (for $δ\neq1$), and transposed $δ$-Poisson structures on these algebras.
Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
Xuezhi Chen; Changxing Miao; Jiye Yuan; Tengfei Zhao

For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2πiz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.
Ambient Chow Rings of Debarre--Voisin Fourfolds and the Beauville--Voisin Conjecture

We prove the Beauville--Voisin conjecture for a very general Debarre--Voisin hyperkähler fourfold \(Y\subset\Gr(6,10)\) associated with a trivector \(σ\) on a ten-dimensional complex vector space \(V_{10}\). Namely, the cycle class map is injective on the subalgebra of the Chow ring generated by divisor classes and the Chern classes of the tangent bundle.
Finite power image families and automorphism actions in linear groups

Let $k/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finitely generated field extension. We characterize the subgroups $G\leq GL_n(k)$ for which the power images $P_m(G)=\{g^m:g\in G\}$ form a finite family: this holds precisely when $G=N\rtimes F$, where $F$ is finite and $N$ is a uniquely divisible subgroup consisting of unipotent matrices.
