In this article we prove the existence of continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces generated by Orlicz functions. The class under consideration contains sequence spaces of Orlicz-Sobolev type, including certain special cases that have played an important role in a number of applications regarding problems arising in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, as well as Nakano's class of Lebesgue sequence spaces with variable exponents. In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Our results are complementary to those already available in the literature. We illustrate them with several concrete examples.
Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
Yanlong Fan; Fengjie Luo; Yiqiu Mao; Quan Wang

We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. The oscillatory density and velocity decay like \((1+t)^{-1}\); the density converges at the same rate to a stratified profile, its horizontal mean faster. For small data, the limit profile is the decreasing vertical rearrangement of the initial density, the unique potential-energy minimizer among rearrangements, independent of rotation, viscosity, and initial velocity. Kinetic plus available potential energy is dissipated exactly by viscosity and decays like \((1+t)^{-2}\), and each fluid particle settles where the limit density equals its own. These rates are optimal for every rotation rate. The linearized problem has real, slowly decaying normal modes, viscously overdamped high-vertical-wavenumber internal gravity waves, whose small solutions show the \(H^r\) density rates \((1+t)^{-(1-r/4)}\), \(0\le r<4\), pressure rate \((1+t)^{-1}\), and energy rate \((1+t)^{-2}\) cannot be improved uniformly for small data. Key difficulties are the loss of a horizontal derivative in the vertical velocity, the failure of \(H^1(\mathbb T^2)\subset L^\infty\), and rotation-induced coupling of divergent and vortical motion, controlled at top order by a positive power of the initial low-order energy. If the stratification is unstable somewhere, every horizontal mode is linearly unstable with real growth rates and the equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable; rotation strictly lowers each growth rate, with an explicit Taylor-number bound depending on the horizontal wavelength, but leaves their supremum unchanged.
Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes

In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.
Capacity Bounds for Optical Interference Channels Subject to Average Power Constraints

Accurate information-theoretic analysis of multiuser wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) optical links is complicated by Kerr nonlinearity and chromatic dispersion. Existing capacity bounds for first-order regular perturbative (RP) channel models have relied on per-symbol peak power constraints to simplify the underlying extremal analysis. In this paper, we replace these peak constraints with the more practically relevant average input power constraints and study the resulting RP WDM interference channel. Unlike the peak-constrained formulation, an exact finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) analysis under average power leads in general to a nonconvex, high-dimensional optimization problem with no closed-form solution. We show that the problem admits a tractable characterization in the high-SNR regime. Using a genie-aided argument, we derive closed-form single-user high-SNR capacity bounds for the RP interference channel and identify constant-amplitude interferer signaling as extremal. Furthermore, under an empirically validated non-negativity condition on the dominant RP kernels and within a truncated first-order RP model, we establish a finite-SNR extremality result, yielding a single-user capacity characterization within the RP model under average power constraints. Building on these single-user corner points, we construct an all-helpsone achievable region via time sharing, which strictly improves upon treating nonlinear interference as noise. Numerical results and split-step Fourier simulations of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation channel confirm that the qualitative conclusions persist over practical launch powers. The results provide new insight into extremal signaling and multiuser trade-offs for nonlinear WDM systems within the RP approximation.
The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus

We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.
Coherent-State Integrals Beyond the Domain of Operator Products

Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain $e^{μa^2}e^{λa^{\dagger2}}$ of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.
On the sum of eccentric subgraph numbers of the vertices of a connected graph

Let $G$ be a connected graph. The eccentric subgraph number $ε(v)$ of a vertex $v$ of $G$ is defined as $ε(v)=\min\{f_G(v,u): u\in V(G)\}$, where $f_G(v,u)$ is the number of connected subgraphs of $G$ containing both $v$ and $u$. The eccentric subgraph index $ES(G)$ of $G$ is defined as $ES(G)=\displaystyle\sum_{v\in V(G)}ε(v).$ In this paper, we obtain the unicyclic graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed girth. The graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices is also obtained. We then characterize the trees that maximize the eccentric subgraph index over trees on $n$ vertices with fixed diameter. Among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed number of pendant vertices, the graph which maximizes the eccentric subgraph index is also characterized.
Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet

Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.
The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve

Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$. Finally, we establish $\mathrm{RIGP}$ over the variety-excluding fields of Szachniewicz and the author, when the excluded variety is a locally closed subvariety of an abelian variety.
On Completely Positive and Semidefinite Programs for Moment Bounds on Maximum of Random Quadratics
Buse Unluturk; Divya Padmanabhan; Karthik Natarajan

Completely positive programs are known to provide an exact representation to several NP-hard optimization problems. In this work, we look at the maximum of random quadratic functions and compute the maximum expected value over ambiguity sets defined with moment and support information. We propose exact completely positive programs and semidefinite programs when the random variables are Bernoulli, nonnegative and unrestricted in support. Our experimental study demonstrates the utility of these formulations.
Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes

We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.
Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion

The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.
Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
Mingxiang Li; Quoc Anh Ngo; Xingwang Xu

This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.
Invariable Generation of Groups of Homeomorphisms

We provide a sufficient condition for a group of homeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff space to be non-invariably generated, generalizing previous results proved using the dynamics of a group's action. We exhibit new applications among Scott-Röver-Nekrashevych groups and among groups of tree automorphism of with (almost) locally prescribed actions.
The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons

We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Ampère potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.
C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
Arbaz Khan; David Mora; Alberth Silgado; Harpal Singh

This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.

We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$. More generally, in odd dimensions, a convex body with $C^\infty$ semialgebraic boundary is an ellipsoid whenever its section volume function satisfies a joint algebraic relation.
Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces

We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.
Time-Inconsistent Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy
Xiaochen Chen; Guohui Guan; Zongxia Liang; Xiaodong Luo

This paper studies infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend distribution for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion under observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting leads to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier policy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The policy retains surplus below the prevailing regime's threshold and distributes any excess immediately. Numerical experiments examine how shareholder patience and economic conditions affect dividend decisions. Over the parameter ranges considered, greater discount-rate dispersion at a fixed initial average rate raises both barriers, while switching speed can generate nonmonotone responses and reverse their ordering.
Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials

Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[ G^{\HC,k}_φ(u,v) =\int_X \bigl(Δ_φ^{(k)}u\bigr) \bigl(Δ_φ^{(k)}v\bigr) \,ω_φ^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[ φ\longmapsto 2\sqrt{\frac{ω_φ^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}}{ω^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,ω^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_Xω^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.
Sharp radial--angular mixed norm Fourier extension and global stability on spheres

We study the sharp Fourier extension inequality from $L^2(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ to the radial--angular mixed space $L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}$. Our work is motivated by and builds upon the foundational analysis of Carneiro, Oliveira e Silva and Sousa \cite{COS}, who initiated the sharp mixed-norm spherical restriction problem from the viewpoint of spherical-harmonic decomposition. Their reduction revealed that the extremal problem is governed by a competition among the individual harmonic modes, and their results established degree-zero extremizers in several important ranges of exponents, including even integer exponents and the endpoint case. The present paper addresses this question by establishing a complete modal ordering result. Building on their spherical-harmonic reduction, the sharp-constant problem is reduced to the weighted Bessel moments \[ I_{ν,k}(q) := \int_0^\infty |J_{ν+k}(r)|^q r^{2ν+1-νq}\,dr, \qquad ν:=\frac d2-1. \] For every integer $d\ge2$ and every finite admissible exponent $q>2d/(d-1)$, we prove \[ I_{ν,k}(q)<I_{ν,0}(q), \qquad k\ge1, \] and hence constants are the unique nonzero extremizers of the sharp mixed-norm extension inequality. In dimensions $d\ge3$ we prove the stronger strict ordering \[ I_{ν,0}(q)>I_{ν,1}(q)>I_{ν,2}(q)>\cdots. \] We resolve this difficulty by combining exact Hankel asymptotics with a finite remainder comparison. The modal ordering also yields the optimal quadratic global stability inequality. For every finite admissible $q$, \[ C_{d,q}^2\|f\|_2^2 -\|\widehat{fσ}\|_{L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}}^2 \ge Γ_{d,q}\|f-P_0f\|_2^2, \] with the best possible coefficient. When $d\ge3$, this coefficient is explicitly \[ Γ_{d,q} =(2π)^d \left[ I_{ν,0}(q)^{2/q}-I_{ν,1}(q)^{2/q} \right]. \]
The Big Match under translation-invariant charges

We study two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which a stream of stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant, and by Mertens and Neyman each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, whose uniform value is $1/2$, every strategy of Player 1 is worthless: for every strategy of Player 1 and every $δ>0$, Player 2 has a pure reply, and there is a translation-invariant charge under which Player 1's payoff is less than $δ$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value with respect to all translation-invariant charges. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge. We pose questions on robust guarantees in general stochastic games and on optimality with respect to a fixed translation-invariant charge.
Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis

Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk. A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates. These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.
What Inverse Problems Can Be Solved Using Neural Networks?
A. S. Leonov; D. V. Lukyanenko

The relationship between classical methods for solving inverse problems and neural network methods is examined. An answer is provided to the question of what inverse problems can be solved using neural networks. The answer is that neural network algorithms can solve only conditionally well-posed problems (well-posed according to Tikhonov). The reason is that the design of standard neural network algorithms violates the well-known Bakushinsky veto from the theory of ill-posed problems. It requires that any method theoretically guaranteeing a stable solution to an ill-posed problem must depend explicitly on the error level of data. The article highlights the distinction between the concept of regularization (RA) in the theory of ill-posed problems and regularization as understood in neural network training, where Bakushinsky's veto is violated. Due to this violation, any changes to the neural network architecture, regularization during training, or training dataset augmentation cannot alter the answer specified above. It is theoretically demonstrated that an ill-posed inverse problem can be solved only by using a parametric set of neural networks that explicitly depend on the known error levels (as parameters) of data. Accordingly, as an alternative to standard neural network algorithms, \neural network based regularization algorithms (NNBRAs) are proposed to solve ill-posed inverse problems. One approach to their construction involves using a regularized dataset. Such a dataset can be generated from perturbed inverse-problem data using a specific base RA explicitly depended on the error level of the data. Test solving the simplest finite-dimensional ill-posed inverse problem demonstrate that the accuracy of the NNBRA approximate solutions is comparable to that of the base RA. At the same time, errors of conventional neural network methods may be unacceptable.
Bei Kang; Lu-Yao Wang; Ke Wu; Wei-Zhong Zhao

By means of $W$-representation, we investigate the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble and present a compact expression for Catalan polynomials. For a special Nekrasov partition function associated with the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble, we show that it can be expressed as a exponential form of the special Catalan polynomials. Furthermore, we make a rule to calculate the Catalan polynomials by means of Feynman diagrams and present another expression for Catalan polynomials. We also establish the connection between certain Catalan polynomials and knot theory.
Sharp $L^q$ estimate of adjoint problem and Pucci conjecture

Let $L$ be a linear second-order elliptic operator satisfying a nondegeneracy condition. We establish sharp $L^q$ estimates for solutions of the adjoint problem associated with $L$ and, by duality, derive sharp $L^p$ estimates for solutions of $Lu = f$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Carlo Pucci.
Isometries of Unit Spheres of SFS-Spaces and a Geometric Approach to Tingley's Problem
Karimbergen Kudaybergenov; Mukhtar Ibragimov; Allabay Arziev

We investigate surjective isometries between the unit spheres of facially symmetric spaces and their interaction with the underlying facial structure. It is shown that such isometries preserve the essential geometric relations associated with symmetric faces, orthogonality, and geometric tripotents. In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries. As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.
Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
Eviatar B. Procaccia; Haoyu Wang; Yuan Zhang

In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $λ$, where the critical value equals $λ_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $λ_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<λ<λ_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $λ_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $λ_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.
Sharp Constants, Threshold, and Failure of Uncertainty Principles on Non-trivial Flat Finsler Manifolds

By uncertainty principles we mean the generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg (CKN) inequality and the Heisenberg--Pauli--Weyl (HPW) uncertainty principle, with the latter being an endpoint case and the Hardy inequality a further limiting case. We study these \(L^p\)-type inequalities \((1<p<n)\) on \(n\)-dimensional non-trivial flat Finsler manifolds, which arise from Hilbert's fourth problem. These manifolds are forward complete but not backward complete, projectively flat, with zero flag curvature, and have infinite reversibility, making them highly asymmetric. They are the simplest non-Riemannian, non-Minkowskian solutions to Hilbert's fourth problem, providing a natural framework in which classical inequalities exhibit new behavior. For the full class, we establish a sharp threshold at the parameter value \(s=2\): the generalized CKN inequality and the HPW uncertainty principle hold for \(s>2\) but fail completely for \(s\le2\). When the generating Minkowski norm is reversible (while the Finsler metric itself remains irreversible with infinite reversibility), we determine the sharp constants for \(s>2\), which were previously unknown. These constants are approached in the limit by compactly supported radial functions. As a corollary, our results cover Berwald's metric space and resolve the open questions on its sharp constants. These findings reveal that the threshold phenomenon is structural for the entire class and is a genuinely non-Riemannian feature with no analogue in the Riemannian flat case.
The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
Sihao Ma; Xiaolin Danny Shi; Zhouli Xu; Albert Jinghui Yang; Shangjie Zhang

We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $μ$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.
On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli

Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^γ$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
On the Isomorphism of Semicircular Algebras

Building on OpenAI's proof of isomorphism of free group factors, we give a self-contained proof of a corresponding result for $C^{*}$-algebras generated by free semicircular systems: the isomorphism class of a $C^{*}$-algebra generated by a semicircular $n$-tuple does not depend on $n\in\{2,3,\dots,+\infty\}$. Similarly, reduced free products of $n$ copies of the Jiang--Su algebra are isomorphic for different $n$ in this range. While reduced free group $C^{*}$-algebras of different ranks are not isomorphic (by a result of Pimsner--Voiculescu), we show that they have strong free absorption properties. At the heart of the proof is an automorphism approximation property for inclusions of $C^{*}$- and $W^{*}$-algebras; a relative version of that property was previously used to derive free complementation results.
Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation

We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,μ)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$. At these parameters, finite Taylor estimates give three sign changes of the return displacement. Scalar order, analyticity along transverse itineraries, and half-period reflection then establish at least seven distinct isolated periodic orbits on the phase cylinder.
A short open space curve of unit width
Tinko Sebastian Bartels; Dennis Kevin Choy; Ruixiang Wu; Tongxin Li

In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.

Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. For a Fourier-Mukai transform whose kernel is a family of Gieseker stable sheaves, we shall give a condition for the preservation of Gieseker stability of sheaves.

Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex $L$-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order $1/L$. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components $n$. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying $0<η\lesssim 1/(L(1 + \log(nK)))$, where $K$ is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit $1/n$ factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.
Birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms
We shall study birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface with Picard number 1 induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms.
A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain

We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $ρ$. A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with low regularity potential

We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Dirac Points in High-Contrast Dielectric Honeycomb Structures
Yi Huang; Bowen Li; Ping Liu

We study Dirac points for a two-dimensional scalar Helmholtz equation in a periodic dielectric medium with two penetrable inclusions per honeycomb cell. In a joint small-inclusion and high-contrast regime, we reduce the Bloch eigenvalue problem to a two-dimensional interaction matrix and derive a two-term asymptotic expansion for the two relevant eigenvalues, uniformly for quasi-momenta separated from the reciprocal lattice. At a vertex K of the Brillouin zone, rotation and inversion-conjugation symmetries force these eigenvalues to coincide. Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference

Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices

We show that limit-periodic Jacobi matrices in the weak exponential class $EC(η)$ have purely absolutely continuous spectral type when $η$ is sufficiently large, depending only on the $R$-boundedness constant. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.
Fractional elementary symmetric functions and Hessian estimates in the plane

We prove an endpoint Pucci maximum principle for domains in $\mathbb R^2$, formulated using a generalization of elementary symmetric polynomials to noninteger orders. As a result, we sharpen an earlier result of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin, and deduce a new Sobolev inequality for $q$-Hessians where $1 < q < 2$. The fractional elementary symmetric functions we use are derived through fractional differentiation. Their signed singular value extension coincides with the Burkholder functional introduced by Burkholder and gives us access to a local Burkholder inequality due to Astala, Iwaniec, Prause and Saksman, leading to a different proof of the Pucci maximum principle from the one in that used quasiconformal maps. We include an elementary real-variable proof of this local Burkholder inequality, obtained by combining a few known techniques from existing literature.
Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation

In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.
Reduction for flag-transitive symmetric 2-designs with gcd(k, λ) = p
Ziwei Lu; Yu Sun; Shenglin Zhou

We study symmetric 2-(v, k, λ) designs admitting a flag-transitive point-primitive subgroup G of automorphisms, where gcd(k, λ) = p and p is a prime. In this paper, we show that G is of affine or almost simple type.
Bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, affine lengths, and Theta operators

We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions. Assuming the Theta coinvariant conjecture implies the Schur-positivity of our refinement.
Poincaré compactifications of pullbacks of parallel vector fields under counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture

Let $F: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polynomial map with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant. It is known that the global invertibility of $F$ is equivalent to the pullback of a parallel vector field being parallel. In this paper, we construct the phase portraits on the Poincaré disc of the pullbacks of the canonical annular, radial, and strip vector fields under non-injective maps $F$ that have recently appeared in the literature. Our arguments use local and global properties of vector fields as well as local and global properties of functions, thereby connecting techniques from dynamical systems and singularity theory.
Katy Blumer; Da-Cheng Juan; Jon Kleinberg; Ravi Kumar; Cyrus Rashtchian; Andrew Tomkins

In this paper we study the behavior of transformer networks generating text over long periods of time. We show that even a three-token, single-layer attention-only transformer can fail to converge. We then study a rich class of transformers with arbitrary finite depth, layer normalization, MLPs, RoPE encodings, and an arbitrary mix of local and global layers. Every transformer in this class has a softmax temperature threshold above which its empirical cache distribution converges to a unique limit, independent of initial conditions. We show further that, while each transformer has a temperature threshold, the supremum of this set is infinite, so there is no global minimal temperature that forces all transformers to converge.
On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems

In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2. Consequently, we obtain another proof of the Arnold corank problem in dimension 3, which was recently proved by Fernandes, Jelonek, and the author of this article. We also prove that the corank is constant in a continuous family of holomorphic functions with isolated singularities and constant Milnor number. We also approach a conjecture recently posed by Budur, Fernández de Bobadilla, Lê, and Nguyen (2022), which states that if two germs of holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms are homotopy equivalent. We prove that a (much) weaker version of this conjecture, which states that if two holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms have the same Euler characteristic, is equivalent to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture for right topological equivalence. Some other results are also presented here. For instance, the multiplicity $> 2$ of generalized semi-Bireskorn-Pham hypersurfaces is an invariant for the right topological equivalence.
Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature

We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $κ$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $β^2<α_c(κ)$. Here $κα_c(κ)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $β<β_{\max}(κ)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.
Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces

We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category. In particular, $\mathcal{S_I}(L(p, q))^*$ corresponds with cyclic traces on $\mathcal{I}$ satisfying a property reminiscent of the modified trace condition.

The problem is discretized using $H^1$-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size $h$ decreasing faster than $k^{-3/2}$ such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to $k$. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, \emph{Multiscale Model. Simul.}, 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.
On Local Inference for Functionals of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems

We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at $P_0$. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded $β$-source condition for some $β$>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.
Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems
José Luis Bravo Trinidad; Renhao Tian; Yulin Zhao

We study positive limit cycles of the Abel equation $$\dot{x}=A(t)x^{3}+B(t)x^{2},$$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2π$-periodic functions. By developing a half-period convexity method, we establish a new criterion ensuring that the equation has at most one positive limit cycle. Moreover, if such a limit cycle exists, it is hyperbolic. As applications, we consider two classes of planar polynomial systems that can be reduced to Abel equations. For a subfamily of cubic rigid systems, we prove that there is at most one limit cycle, thereby giving a partial answer to the first problem in Gasull's list of 33 open problems. For quadratic systems, we derive a new uniqueness criterion for limit cycles surrounding the origin and provide explicit parameter regions under which the criterion is satisfied.
Algebraic overtwistedness of contact $(+1)$-surgeries via augmented Floer theories
Russell Avdek; Youlin Li; Zhengyi Zhou

We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $Λ\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},ξ_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(Λ)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. In dimension three, this produces new examples of tight algebraically overtwisted contact manifolds, vastly extending the authors' previous results: If a Legendrian knot in $(\mathbb{S}^3,ξ_{\mathrm{std}})$ admits an exact, oriented Lagrangian filling that is not a disk, then contact $(+1/k)$-surgery on it is algebraically overtwisted and tight for every positive integer $k$. Our proofs use versions of symplectic cohomology and wrapped Floer cohomology defined by augmentations of a chain-level contact homology algebra.
Nondegeneracy and asymptotic behavior of type I blow-up for semilinear heat equations with general nonlinearities
Yohei Fujishima; Ryoto Ichiya; Norisuke Ioku

We study the local asymptotic behavior of nonnegative type I blow-up solutions to semilinear heat equations with nonlinearities that need not be scale invariant. Using a quasi-similarity transformation adapted to the associated ordinary differential equation, we establish locally uniform convergence to a constant profile on the parabolic spatial scale near every interior blow-up point. Under a quantitative assumption on the nonlinearity at infinity, our results cover regularly varying nonlinearities in the Sobolev subcritical and critical ranges and, in one and two space dimensions, rapidly growing nonlinearities including double exponentials. A key ingredient in this analysis is a positive lower bound for the normalized solution at interior blow-up points. In fact, under weaker assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove this bound in arbitrary space dimension without assuming radial symmetry.

A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving $A_i\vec{x}_i= λ_i\vec{x}_i$ where $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $N \gg 1$ and (usually) $λ_i$ is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of $A_i$. Often, the matrices $A_i$ come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter $p \rightarrow A(p)$, that is $A_i = A(p_i)$, so the matrices $A_i$ change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter $p$ or the matrix $A(p)$ as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.
Simulation Based Inference of a Simple Neural Network Structure

Neurophysiologists are nowadays able to record from a large number of extracellular electrodes and to extract, from the raw data, the sequences of action potentials or spikes generated by many neurons. Unfortunately these ''many neurons'' still represent only a tiny fraction of the neuronal population that constitutes the network. Using association statistics such as the estimation of the cross-correlation functions, they are trying to infer the structure of the network formed by the recorded neurons. But this inference is compromised by the tremendous under-sampling of the neuronal population. We propose to focus instead on simple spike train statistics, like the empirical spikes frequency, or the interspike interval distribution. Their sampling distributions can be estimated by simulations, and, given a few observed spike train statistics, they provide enough information to infer the structure of the underlying network. We show that, on a ''toy model'', our method gives significantly better results than the sub-network reconstruction method with regards to the inference of the connection probability of the original network.

The shape of a number field $K$ of degree $n\geq2$ is the similarity class of the lattice obtained by projecting $\mathscr{O}_K$ orthogonally away from the rational line in Minkowski space. It defines a point in the space of shapes of rank-$(n-1)$ lattices, $\mathscr{S}_{n-1}:=\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$, where $\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$ is the group of orthogonal similitudes. Let $G$ be a fixed nontrivial finite abelian group, and let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ vary over tamely ramified Galois extensions with Galois group isomorphic to $G$. We study the variation of the shapes of such number fields in $\mathscr S_{n-1}$, where $n=|G|$.

The model coupling parameters are the hopping parameter $κ^2>0$ and the field interaction coupling $α>0$. Besides the finiteness property of the free energy, for sufficiently small values of the model coupling parameters $κ^2$ and $α$, we show the model satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and construct the underlying physical quantum mechanical Hilbert space, and, using a polymer expansion, we show correlations also remain bounded in the thermodynamic limit. In recent work (arXiv:2610.10341), the authors introduced a framework for studying the vanishing viscosity limit for sequences of weak solutions of the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations to planar shocks of the compressible Euler equations. In this paper, we introduce these methods and apply them to the multi-dimensional viscous Burgers' equation. As an application, we study the rate of convergence to the inviscid shock in the vanishing viscosity limit.

The noisy torn paper channel additionally introduces bit substitution errors to each fragment. Recovering the message therefore requires accounting for both bit errors and uncertainty about the fragment order. We establish a capacity upper bound for the noisy torn paper channel that matches the achievable rate of Ravi, Vahid, and Shomorony and resolves their conjecture. We construct computable a posteriori error estimators for parametric families of nonlinear elliptic problems by measuring the residual of a variational formulation in the dual norm of a closed subspace of the test space. A single abstract theorem shows that the resulting estimator is bounded above and below by the error in the trial norm, i.e., it is a variationally correct loss function. Two instances are covered. Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. We study the linearization, with respect to zeroth-order perturbations, of the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of a formally self-adjoint elliptic operator $P=-Δ_g+Q$ on a compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n\geq 2$ with boundary, where $Q$ is of order at most one. We study the $α$-Ricci flow $(g(t),α(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $α$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[α] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[α]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([α])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([α])$ is the primitive length of $[α]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tildeα(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $α^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $α^*$ direction. If $[α]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tildeα(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$.
Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles

We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions. We distinguish the $\mathbb{R}^4$'s using end Floer homology.
Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
Mykhailo Hontarenko; Wojciech Tarnowski; Sergey Denisov; Karol Życzkowski

Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.

We study the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of spaces with locally expanding self-covering maps and, more generally, limit spaces of contracting self-similar groups. We show that the conformal dimension is characterized by combinatorial moduli associated with the Schreier graphs of these groups. We compare these moduli with contraction coefficients of self-similar group actions and with algebras of functions on the limit spaces satisfying asymptotic $p$-energy conditions. We also give conditions on the group when the conformal dimension is equal to the infimum of visual metrics on the self-similarity complex.
Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane

The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $π$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.
An analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible classes and radicality for finite irreducible Coxeter groups
Constantin Cedillo Vayson de Pradenne; Matthew Gherman; Enoch Guo; Colin La

Let $G$ be a finite group, $M$ a $G$-module, and $F$ a field. A continuous group homomorphism $i : Γ_L=\text{Gal}(L_{\text{sep}}/L) \rightarrow G$ yields a homomorphism $i^* : H^d(G,M) \rightarrow H^d(L,M)$ for every $d\in \mathbb{N}$. An element $u \in H^d(G,M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $u\in\ker(i^*)$ for every $i$ and every field extension $L/F$. If $M=\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$ with a trivial $G$-action, an element $u$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if $u^k$ is negligible over $F$ for some $k\geq1$. The (eventually) negligible elements over $F$ form an ideal of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, called the (eventually) negligible ideal. We prove an analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible elements. An element $u\in H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if and only if the restriction of $u$ to the cohomology of each elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ is eventually negligible over $F$. Paired with applications of a Gysin-type long exact sequence, we identify generators of the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of dihedral groups, cyclic $2$-groups, and generalized quaternion groups. We prove that the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of every finite irreducible Coxeter group is radical. The result was previously known for Weyl groups; we prove it for the remaining non-Weyl types $I_2(m)$, $H_3$, and $H_4$.
Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
Luis Pabon; Johannes Köhler; Revant Kasichainula; Marco Pavone

Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].
Graph binomial coefficients and a positivity conjecture of Guo and Krattenthaler

We investigate Conjecture 7.4 of Guo and Krattenthaler \cite{GK}, which predicts that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial \[ P_n(q) = \frac{(1-q)^2}{(1-q^{10n-1})(1-q^{15n-1})}\qbin{30n}{5n} \] has non-negative coefficients, except for $q^1$ and $q^{125n^2-25n+3}$, which equal $-1$. We study this problem through three main perspectives: First, by linking the boundary coefficients to the second differences of the partition function, we settle the first and last $25n+1$ coefficients via a novel partition injection. Second, by introducing a ``defect'' generalization of Andrews' classical lemma, we reduce the conjecture to an almost-unimodality property and employ a uniform saddle-point analysis to prove it analytically for all large $n \ge 2\cdot 10^{29}$. Finally, we connect these quotients to graph binomial coefficients, providing a natural orbit-counting interpretation via Burnside's lemma on directed cycles and paths.
Eremenko's conjecture on higher-order Briot--Bouquet equations

The Briot--Bouquet theorem describes the meromorphic solutions of autonomous first-order algebraic differential equations. We prove Eremenko's conjecture extending it to all orders: if $f$ is meromorphic in $\mathbb{C}$ and $P(f,f^{(n)})=0$ for a nonzero polynomial $P$, then $f$ is rational, elliptic, a rational function of $e^{cz}$ with $c\neq 0$, or satisfies $f^{(n)}=af+b$. In particular, every meromorphic solution with $P$ irreducible of degree at least two belongs to the Weierstrass class. Solutions with poles were classified by Eremenko, Liao and Ng. We settle the remaining entire case with a rigidity theorem for polynomial compositions: if $h$ is nonconstant entire and $D^nR(h)=S(h)$, where $D=d/dz$ and $°R=°S\ge 2$, then $h(z)=Ae^{bz}+Be^{-bz}+C$. No growth assumption is needed. The proof turns the cancellation of leading terms into a contraction of indicator diagrams and obtains incompatible zero counts near an exposed edge. As an arithmetic application, an algebraic Laurent expansion at one algebraic point and an algebraic value at another force a solution to lie in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(z)$. Hence any two distinct derivatives of a function in Mahler's class (transcendental meromorphic functions with algebraic Laurent coefficients at every algebraic point) are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.
Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds

Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.
With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined

In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.
Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times

We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $ν>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+ν+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.
On generalized embeddability of a non-elliptic self-map
Manuel D. Contreras; Santiago D\'ıaz-Madrigal; Pavel Gumenyuk

We study the structure of the centralizer of a non-elliptic holomorphic self-map of the unit disc and its relation with continuous dynamical structures. We prove that if the identity is not isolated in the centralizer of a non-elliptic self-map $φ\in \mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb D)$, then $φ$ is univalent and its centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup of holomorphic self-maps. This result provides a general criterion for the existence of continuous dynamics arising from discrete iteration. Our approach is based on the theory of holomorphic models and on simultaneous linearization techniques for commuting self-maps. In particular, we exploit recent developments on simultaneous linearization for parabolic self-maps with positive hyperbolic step. As a consequence, we obtain new sufficient conditions for the embeddability of holomorphic self-maps into continuous semigroups.
On the Mathematical Structure of Helical Shear in Anelastic Continua
Souhayl Sadik; Giuseppe Saccomandi; Luigi Vergori

We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kröner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenböck material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.

We propose that mathematics is done largely as a means of both coping with and celebrating our physicality in the natural world. Inspired by David Abram's "Becoming Animal", we suggest that -- in opposition to the popular image of an otherworldy Platonic realm-- the spiritual component of doing mathematics is grounded on and in the Earth. We explore this as a means of questioning the widespread adoption of AI in the workflows of research mathematics.
Alexey Fakhrutdinov; Platon Khamatov; Oleg R. Musin

We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$.
