For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.
Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products

We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl. Math., 2013]. Furthermore, we characterize the divisor lattices admitting alternating Hamilton paths and cycles.
Reverse Translation and Convolution Estimates in the Framework of the Mehler-Fock Transform
U. K. Mandal; Akhilesh Prasad; Sudhanshu Ranjan

In this paper, reverse translation and convolution estimates in the frame of $μ^{th}$ order Mehler-Fock transform are obtained. Continuity properties of these operators on the test function space $\mathfrak{H}_{l,r,n}$ have been discussed. Moreover, Sobolev space $S_{r,p}^{N,α}$ has been introduced and again continuity properties of these operators in this Sobolev space have been discussed.
Standard identities for polynomial vector fields

Let $W_n$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields in $n$ variables over a field of characteristic zero, and let $s_k$ denote the alternating sum of compositions of $k$ vector fields. The identity $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ has been asserted for arbitrary $n$. We give an explicit counterexample in dimension five, verified by an exact integer computation of a $34$-commutator. Together with the known vanishing of $s_{35}$, this shows that $35$ is the least degree of a standard identity on $W_5$. We then prove that $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ for every even $n\geq2$. The proof uses Lie algebra homology with coefficients in the polynomial algebra modulo constants and a lemma on invariant tensors. We describe the computation and provide the source code and verification results.
Topological entropy of saturated sets for Lorenz attractors
Zheng Huang; Xueting Tian; Xiaodong Wang; Xutong Zhao

We study the topological entropy of saturated sets for continuous flows, with emphasis on singular hyperbolic dynamics. For a $C^r$-generic ($r \geq 2$) vector field $X$ carrying a geometric Lorenz attractor $Λ$, we prove that for every nonempty compact connected set $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(Φ,Λ)$ and every open set $U \subseteq M$ with $U \cap Λ\neq \emptyset$, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(Φ,G_{\mathcal{K}}(Φ) \cap \operatorname{Trans}(Φ,Λ) \cap U)=\inf_{μ\in \mathcal{K}} h_μ(ϕ_1)$, where $Φ=(ϕ_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is the flow induced by $X$ and $\operatorname{Trans}(Φ,Λ)$ denotes the set of points whose positive orbits are dense in $Λ$. The same formula holds $C^1$-generically for singular hyperbolic attractors. In contrast with the uniformly hyperbolic case, we also prove that, for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^r(M^3)$, geometric Lorenz attractors admit a positive-entropy invariant measure with no generic points. An analogous conclusion holds for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^1(M)$ whose non-trivial singular hyperbolic attractors contain singularities and satisfy $\dim E^{cu}=2$. These examples show that the discrete-time saturated entropy theory does not extend directly to singular flows.
Excess inertia of finite metric spaces

This paper classifies the possible inertias that are realized by an excess matrix of a finite metric space with at most nine points. For the classification, we make use of relationships between finite metric spaces and non-obtuse and acute sets in classical geometry. As an application, we prove that the small-scale limit of the magnitude function of any six-point metric space is at least one whenever this limit exists.
Extensions of Operator Systems, Hyperrigidity and Quantum Double Suspension
Vibhor Bhatt; Satyajit Guin; Palash Sharma

We introduce a class of extensions of unital operator systems satisfying a certain Toeplitz type property. We show that these extensions induce corresponding extensions of the $C^*$-algebras they generate. We prove that hyperrigidity is preserved under these extensions, yielding new examples through iteration. We introduce the quantum double suspension of operator systems as a special class of these extensions and show that its iterates yield the Hong-Szymański quantum double suspensions at the $C^*$-algebra level, encompassing, in particular, the Vaksman-Soibelman quantum spheres. We construct hyperrigid operator systems underlying these quantum spheres. As a further application, we show that every counterexample to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture gives rise to a sequence of counterexamples. We identify the $C^*$-envelopes of these extensions and use this identification to obtain a $K$-theoretic condition ensuring that each such sequence contains infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic counterexamples. We also observe that the validity of the conjecture in the commutative setting is linked to its validity for an infinite family of noncommutative operator systems obtained through successive extensions. Finally, we compute the propagation number, an invariant of operator systems introduced by Connes and van Suijlekom, for these extensions.
Density of polynomials whose Aron--Berner extensions attain their norms

We establish a polynomial analogue of Lindenstrauss' theorem in full generality. More precisely, we prove that, for every real or complex Banach space X and every positive integer n, the n-homogeneous scalar-valued polynomials whose Aron-Berner extensions to the bidual X** attain their norms form a dense subset of the space of continuous n-homogeneous polynomials on X. This resolves a problem posed by Aron, Garcia and Maestre in 2003, extending their result for quadratic polynomials to arbitrary degrees without imposing any structural assumptions on the underlying Banach space. We further establish the corresponding theorem for vector-valued polynomials with arbitrary Banach space codomains. Our approach relies on a new perturbation scheme based on averaged linear contractions, which provides simultaneous control of the multilinear variables and yields norm attainment through iterated limits in the bidual.
The one percent property for free groups
Emmanuel Breuillard; Ferdinand Jacobé de Naurois

We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $δ>0$ such that for every probability measure $μ$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $μ$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $μ$-mass at least $δ$.
Stability Analysis of Bounded Solutions to 2-D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in L^2_uloc Spaces

This paper examines the stability analysis of two-dimensional incompressible fluids in $L^2_{uloc}$ spaces. Extending the classical stability framework for Euler equations in Yudovich-type settings, we establish the convergence of Navier-Stokes solutions toward Euler solutions as viscosity $ν\to 0$, under the weakened assumptions $u^ν_0 \in L^\infty$ and $ω^ν_0 \in L^\infty$ without imposing decay conditions at infinity. We first derive a priori estimates for the Navier-Stokes equations in $L^\infty$ spaces. Then, using harmonic analysis tools including Littlewood-Paley decomposition and Bony's paraproduct calculus, we prove the $L^\infty$-convergence of the velocity field and $L^2_{uloc}$-convergence of the vorticity as $ν\to 0$.
Actions of central Morita monoidal groupoids, and seven term exact sequences of all types

We introduce a strict monoidal groupoid associated with a given commutative ring $K$. It acts on the Clifford extension systems of $K$-central algebras which are graded by a group $G$, as well as on the generalized collective characters, both of type $ϕ\in$ Hom$(G,$ Aut$(K))$. These actions partition the two sets above with respect to graded Morita equivalence. By that we establish a seven term exact sequence of type $ϕ$, which boils down to the celebrated Chase-Harrison-Rosenberg sequence when $ϕ$ is Galois.
On the Convexity of the Upper Bild

We give a proof of the convexity of the upper bild of a quaternionic matrix, a theorem of So and Thompson. After reduction to $2\times2$ matrices, we introduce real coordinates on a sphere and obtain two representations of the upper bild over the closed unit ball, involving a convex function and a concave function. Minimizing the first and maximizing the second over parameters with a fixed real part yield a convex lower boundary function and a concave upper boundary function, from which convexity follows.
Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps

Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,ω}(f^n)=C_{f,ω,i}\,λ_i(f)^n+O(η^n), \] for every $\sqrt{λ_{i-1}(f)λ_{i+1}(f)}<η<λ_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.
Computational framework NetBiF predicts and classifies steady-state bifurcations in biochemical systems via reaction network structure
Al Jay Lan J. Alamin; Bryan S. Hernandez

Dynamics of biochemical systems are dictated by the stoichiometry and kinetics of reaction networks. These systems may admit positive steady states that could undergo qualitative change in response to varying rate parameters. These changes are called steady-state bifurcations, and they correspond to biologically meaningful processes. Classical bifurcation analysis relies on exact kinetics and rate parameters, which are often unknown or difficult to measure for complex systems. To address this, structural bifurcation analysis (SBA) was introduced to predict bifurcations using only the system's associated reaction network. In this work, the computational package NetBiF (Network Bifurcation Finder) is introduced to implement SBA. NetBiF is applied across diverse biochemical systems, including fundamental metabolic pathways, signaling and gene regulatory networks, and a large-scale carbon cycle model, to predict steady-state bifurcations. Crucially, for biochemical systems governed by power law kinetics, the implementation of NetBiF also classifies the steady-state bifurcations as saddle-node, transcritical, or pitchfork via a structural analog of Sotomayor's theorem. To this end, explicit formulations for the bifurcation criteria were derived for these biochemical systems. Determining and classifying bifurcation behaviors provide insight into biochemical systems' abilities to adapt to changing and fluctuating conditions. Collectively, the study presents NetBiF as a scalable, structure-based, and consistent computational tool to implement SBA. Our findings enable researchers to systematically study dynamical behaviors of biochemical systems through their reaction network structures without requiring explicit kinetic information.
Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
Zi-Xiao Huang; Ma-Ke Yuan; Yang Zhou

We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric Rényi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric Rényi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.

It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.
Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schrödinger Operator on a Compact Graph

We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schrödinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative
An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $γ: \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $Ω$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(γ(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ of $T_γM$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $Ω$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabré et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^Ω\subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^Ω:= \mathscr{W}^Ω\cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ via a foliation in the case $Ω$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.
Nicolas Monod; Omer Tamuz; Lizzy Teryoshin

We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.
On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials

We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;χ,ψ)$ and $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $χ_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;χ_{163},χ_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.

We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$. This leads to a correspondence with partial ovoids of the elliptic quadric $Q^-(5,q)$. Using a construction of Cossidente and Pavese, we obtain a non-additive symmetric $2$-code in $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ of cardinality $q^4+2q^3$, improving the previously known general lower bound. We also give an explicit matrix description of this family. Lastly, we present a block-based construction for symmetric $2$-codes that extends the three-dimensional improvement to all odd dimensions. In particular, for every odd $n\geq3$ and every prime power $q>2$, we obtain \begin{equation*} A_q^{\rm sym}(n,2) \ge q^{(n^2-1)/2}+q^{(n^2-3)/2}+q^{(n^2-9)/2}, \end{equation*} which is strictly larger than the maximum cardinality of an additive symmetric $2$-code with the same parameters. This yields the first infinite family (as the matrix dimension $n$ varies) of non-additive symmetric $2$-codes whose size is larger than the largest achievable size of an additive code with the same parameters; before this, such a gap had only been established for $n=3$.
A new approach for estimating the number of spikes in high-dimensional Gaussian models
Hugo Jeannin; Pascal Vallet; Florent Bouchard; Guillaume Ginolhac; Audrey Giremus

In this paper, we study the estimation of the signal subspace dimension $k$ in a $p$-variate signal-plus-noise complex Gaussian model, when the noise covariance matrix is assumed to be diagonal or Toeplitz. We consider the high-dimensional asymptotic regime in which both the data dimension $p$ and the available sample size $n$ diverge to infinity at the same rate, while we also allow $k$ to diverge at a slower speed. In this context, the classical estimates of the literature, consistent in the high-dimensional regime, often rely on the a priori knowledge of an upper bound $k_*$ of $k$, which can be misspecified in practice. Our proposed approach relies on building estimates of the tracial moments of the noise covariance matrix using the $p-k_*$ smallest eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix (SCM), which are in turn used to build a threshold above which the $k$ largest eigenvalues are isolated. The resulting estimate of $k$ is proved to be consistent in the high-dimensional regime, even for the misspecified situations where $k_* < k$. Numerical experiments in different challenging scenarios illustrate the improvement of the proposed approach over the aforementioned methods.
A Smoothed Augmented Lagrangian Method for Mathematical Programs with Vertical Complementarity Constraints
Jia Wang; Andreas Themelis; Panagiotis Patrinos

We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties. This construction yields a smooth unconstrained subproblem within the ALM framework that can be efficiently solved by many fast optimization algorithms. In the limiting setting, we establish global convergence to Mordukhovich- and Clarke-stationary points. For the convergence rate, we show that, under appropriate assumptions, the smoothed ALM achieves Q-linear convergence. We further provide a worst-case iteration complexity analysis for computing an approximate stationary point of the original problem or of an associated feasibility problem. Preliminary numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
How to Train Your Intercept: A Comparison of Intercept Update Strategies in Coordinate Descent

Coordinate descent solvers for regularized generalized linear models (GLMs) differ in how they update the intercept. This seemingly routine choice can substantially affect convergence when the response is imbalanced. For direct coordinate descent on the original GLM loss, we compare a conservative step based on worst-case curvature, a safeguarded Newton step based on current curvature, and repeated Newton steps that solve the intercept subproblem. The conservative update can leave much of the interaction between the intercept and the coefficients unresolved, producing a slowdown when that interaction controls convergence. A single Newton step avoids this attenuation and, in our experiments, follows nearly the same outer trajectory as exact minimization while requiring fewer inner steps. Simulated and real-data experiments, including comparisons across six production solvers and a controlled intervention within skglm, support this explanation. We also show how the same mechanism appears in quadratic-approximation methods and extends to multinomial models with rare classes. We recommend a safeguarded Newton update for direct coordinate descent and full intercept optimization within frozen local quadratic surrogates.
Orthonormal Strichartz estimates over fractal time
Guoxia Feng; Jinbong Lee; Sanghyuk Lee

We study Strichartz estimates for orthonormal families of initial data when time is integrated against an $α$-dimensional Frostman measure $μ$, $0<α\le1$, with coefficients measured in $\ell^β$. For the fractional Schrödinger, wave and Klein--Gordon equations, we obtain orthogonality gains in the admissible region and necessary conditions on $β$. For the fractional Schrödinger equation the exponents are sharp up to an endpoint; the optimality of the threshold $β=q/2$ requires $μ$ to be Ahlfors regular. For the Schrödinger equation in dimensions $d\ge2$, we prove a Lorentz endpoint estimate and, if $d>2α$, the critical exponent $β=q/2$ at every pair $2\le q,r<\infty$ with \[\frac d2(\frac12-\frac1r)\ge\fracαq, \quad r>\frac{dq}{d-α};\] on $r=\infty$ we obtain a restricted weak-type estimate. Since the constants depend on $μ$ only through its Frostman constant, Lebesgue measure yields global-in-time critical estimates in this range when $d\ge3$. The proofs combine Frostman fractional integration, a spectral near--far argument at the endpoint, and asymmetric Hilbert--Schmidt bounds with orthogonal frequency-block summation. We also obtain further estimates in the low-dimensional cases $d=1$ (fractional Schrödinger) and $d=2$ (wave and Klein--Gordon) with $α>1/2$, and formulate the consequences for densities of freely evolving states.

Let $2<p<\infty$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F$ of a noncommutative $L_p$-space contains a subspace completely isomorphic to $\ell_p$, $C_p$, $R_p$, or $C_p\cap R_p$ and completely complemented in $F$. This answers the question of Junge and Xu on the existence of completely symmetric basic sequences.

We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.
Non-Potential Congestion Games with a Continuum of Players
Alix Dupont; Quentin Petit; Adrien Séguret

We study a class of congestion games with a continuum of heterogeneous players and a finite set of resources, without assuming the existence of a potential function. Players differ in their individual characteristics and may contribute differently to congestion, which is represented through general aggregate features of the population choosing each resource. We characterize the conditions under which such a game admits a potential and show that this structure generally fails when players have heterogeneous impacts on congestion. To analyze the non-potential case, we introduce the concept of Stochastic Variational Nash Equilibrium, in which players observe idiosyncratic cost shocks before selecting a resource. We show that equilibrium choices are pure conditional on players' characteristics and shock realizations, whereas the induced aggregate allocation is probabilistic. Under Gumbel-distributed shocks, the equilibrium is equivalent to a continuum-player logit Quantal Response Equilibrium. Using a fixed-point formulation and the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem, we establish existence for every positive noise level and recover a pure Nash equilibrium in the zero-noise limit. Under a coordinate-wise monotonicity condition on aggregate interaction costs, we further prove uniqueness and convergence of the regularized allocations to the pure equilibrium. An application to electric vehicle charging illustrates how heterogeneous energy demands jointly affect station choice, congestion, and market shares.
Distribution tail of the distance to infinity in supercritical bond percolation

We give an estimate for the distribution tail of the passage time between $0$ and $\infty$ in first-passage percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$, when the weight distribution is bounded and has a supercritical atom at $0$. A special case involves the number of disjoint cutsets between $0$ and $\infty$ in supercritical bond percolation. Besides, we show that the rate function for the upper-tail deviations of the point-to-point passage time is asymptotically polynomial near $0$.
Lifted Restricted Isometry Property and Fast Algorithm for Spectral Compressed Sensing With Near-Optimal Sample Complexity
Xunmeng Wu; Jian-Feng Cai; Zongben Xu; Zai Yang

This paper studies the spectral compressed sensing problem, which aims to recover an $r$-spectrally-sparse signal of length $N$ from linear compressive measurements. We reformulate the problem as the recovery of a low-rank Hankel matrix. Motivated by this formulation, we propose a Lifted Restricted Isometry Property (LRIP) for the measurement matrix and show that Gaussian measurement matrices satisfy LRIP under certain conditions. Unlike classical RIP, LRIP imposes a rank constraint in the lifted matrix domain while taking measurements in the signal domain through the adjoint Hankel operator. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem efficiently, we introduce a Fast Iterative Hard Thresholding (FIHT) algorithm. Based on LRIP, we show that FIHT converges linearly to the true signal with high probability using $\mathcal{O}(r \ln r \ln^2 N)$ scaled Gaussian measurements, which is near-optimal up to log factors and improves the state-of-the-art order of $r^2$ for nonconvex Hankel methods. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the superiority of FIHT as compared to state-of-the-art convex methods in terms of phase transitions, computational time, and robustness to noise.
The Gauss--Newton Method for Phase Retrieval from Coded Diffraction Patterns

We study the minimum-norm Gauss--Newton method for phase retrieval from random coded diffraction patterns with additive intensity noise. For bounded symmetric masks satisfying the standard complex moment conditions, we establish convergence guarantees with quadratic error recursions in both the resampled and fixed-data settings. In the resampled setting, $O(\log^2 n)$ masks per independent block suffice to obtain a spectral initializer within a constant-relative-radius neighborhood and to establish a local quadratic error recursion with an additive noise term. Consequently, in the noiseless case, the method achieves relative accuracy $ε$ using $O(\log\log(1/ε)\log^2 n)$ masks. In the fixed-data setting, $O(\log^6(en))$ masks suffice for spectral initialization within a neighborhood whose relative radius is proportional to $\log^{-5/2}(nL)$. Within this neighborhood, the method satisfies a linear contraction bound and eventually a quadratic error recursion. In particular, in the noiseless case, the method initially converges linearly and enters a quadratic convergence phase after $O(\log n)$ iterations, without acquiring additional masks. Numerical experiments on synthetic signals and a natural image demonstrate the method's efficiency relative to state-of-the-art algorithms.
Inclusion-wise extremal knapsack problems are (mostly) hard to approximate
Fabio Ciccarelli; Fabio Furini; Ulrich Pferschy; Elena Rener

We study two inclusion-wise extremal variants of the 0-1 Knapsack Problem (KP). Given $n$ items with integer weights and nonnegative costs or profits, the Minimum-Cost Maximal Knapsack Packing Problem seeks a minimum-cost packing for capacity $c$ to which no item can be added, while the Maximum-Profit Minimal Knapsack Cover Problem seeks a maximum-profit cover for threshold $d$ from which no item can be removed. Both problems are weakly $\mathrm{NP}$-hard and pseudo-polynomially solvable, as is the classical KP, but their approximability is fundamentally different: unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, with positive values neither problem admits a polynomial-time $2^{p(n)}$-approximation for any polynomial $p$; allowing zero values rules out every multiplicative factor. Even with unit costs for packing and unit profits for covering, neither admits an $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, whereas a trivial $n$-approximation exists. We identify restrictions that restore approximability. If every item weighs at least a fixed fraction of the capacity, respectively of the threshold, both problems can be solved exactly in polynomial time. For the cover problem, if each weight $w_i$ satisfies $w_i-1\geδ(d-1)$, we give an approximation scheme for arbitrary profits whose running time is polynomial in $n$, $1/\varepsilon$, and $1/δ$. If values equal weights, a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) was already known for the packing problem; we give an FPTAS for the cover problem, improving on the previously known factor $2$. If value-to-weight ratios differ by at most a factor $κ$, we obtain a $(1+\varepsilon)κ$-approximation for both problems.
Generalized Topological Structures Induced by $H^{*}$-Open Sets and Their Separation Properties
Neeraj Kumar Tomar; Komal Priya; Amit Ujlayan

In this paper, we investigate the family of $H^{*}$-open sets from the perspective of generalized topology and examine the structural and separation properties arising from it. For a topological space $(\mathbb{X},τ)$, the family of all $H^{*}$-open subsets of $\mathbb{X}$ is considered as a natural candidate for an $H^{*}$-generated generalized topology. We establish conditions under which this family forms a strong generalized topology and identify additional assumptions that allow the resulting structure to be treated as an ordinary topology. This distinction provides a systematic framework for studying $H^{*}$-open sets without imposing finite-intersection properties in advance. Within this framework, we investigate the corresponding $H^{*}$-interior and $H^{*}$-closure operators and analyze separation properties determined by the $H^{*}$-open structure. When the $H^{*}$-generated family forms a topology, the resulting associated space is used to relate generalized $H^{*}$-separation properties to their classical topological counterparts. We further examine compactness-type properties, subspace behaviour, and preservation under suitable mappings. Examples are included to illustrate how the structure generated by $H^{*}$-open sets may exhibit separation behaviour different from that of the original topology. The results provide a unified setting for connecting $H^{*}$-open-set theory with generalized topological structures and offer a basis for further investigation of separation and covering properties in this framework.
Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations

In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.
Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem

We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δ$ in domain $D_{ε,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $ε$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $ρ$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $ε\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $κ>0$, the eigenvalues of $-Δ$ in $D_{ε,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schrödinger operator $-Δ+κρ$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.
The $2$-co-lacunary subsequence principle for arbitrary noncommutative $L_1$-spaces

For every von Neumann algebra \(\M\), we prove that each bounded sequence in the Haagerup space \(L_1(\M)=\M_*\) admits either a norm-convergent subsequence or a \(2\)-co-lacunary subsequence. This answers an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina \cite[Remark~3.11]{ParcetRandrianantoanina2006} and removes both hyperfiniteness and semifiniteness.
Sobolev Minimizers for Critical Vectorial $p$-Laplacian Problems

We study minimizers of the optimal Sobolev quotients for the critical embeddings $D^{1,p}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)$ and $W^{1,p}(Ω;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(Ω;\mathbb R^m)$. In the whole space, we classify all minimizers as $\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol c\,U_{δ,x_0}$, where $\boldsymbol c\neq\boldsymbol0$ and $U_{δ,x_0}$ is an Aubin--Talenti bubble. On bounded domains and for $λ>0$, we equip $W^{1,p}(Ω;\mathbb R^m)$ with $ \|\boldsymbol u\|_λ^p :=\int_Ω \bigl(|D\boldsymbol u|^p+λ|\boldsymbol u|^p\bigr) $. Using scalar attainment results, we establish existence and synchronization of vectorial minimizers. At resonance, we consider the pure Neumann problem $ -\boldsymbolΔ_p\boldsymbol u =|\boldsymbol u|^{p^*-2}\boldsymbol u\ \text{in }Ω. $ For the associated quotient, we prove existence and global $C^1(\overlineΩ)$ regularity of minimizers. Finally, we prove synchronization of radial solutions and deduce symmetry breaking on balls.
Local Hadamard well-posedness of the 2D primitive equations without thermal diffusion under strict stratification
Fengjie Luo; Quan Wang; Zhengdong Du

We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with anisotropic viscosity and no thermal diffusion. For doubly periodic perturbations of a hydrostatic equilibrium with an affine temperature profile, we establish local Hadamard well-posedness in Sobolev spaces under strict stratification. The initial horizontal velocity and temperature have sufficient regularity and vanishing vertical means, but need not be small. The estimates close at the same Sobolev order for these variables despite the horizontal derivative loss in the diagnostic vertical velocity. Stratification-weighted energy estimates and a horizontal compensation argument avoid an additional temperature derivative while retaining the full vertical dependence and the vertically homogeneous velocity component determined by periodic compatibility. A one-sided comparison places higher-order norms of the more regular solution only in terms involving lower-order differences. This structure allows the Bona--Smith method to yield continuous dependence in the original Sobolev topology. We obtain a unique maximal strong solution in the strictly stratified class, together with continuous dependence of the diagnostic vertical velocity and pressure in their natural Sobolev spaces and lower semicontinuity of the maximal lifespan.
Colored Turán densities and finite directed templates
Nannan Chen; Ander Lamaison; Heng Li; Hong Liu

Classical Turán theory relates the asymptotic extremal problem for an ordinary forbidden graph to its chromatic number. This principle fails when a forbidden copy must respect prescribed vertex colors, as occurs naturally in multipartite extremal problems and in embeddings with prescribed clusters. We study properly vertex-colored graphs whose hosts have a prescribed density between every pair of color classes, with containment interpreted through color-preserving homomorphisms. Our main theorem gives a finite directed reduction: for every fixed $m$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently many-colored $d$-dense host admits a colored homomorphism from an $m$-layer half-blowup $D[m]$ of a finite digraph $D$ with density at least $d-\varepsilon$, where $D$ may be chosen with $\lceil\varepsilon^{-1}\rceil$ vertices. Consequently, the colored Turán density of every non-empty finite forbidden family equals the homomorphism Turán density of its associated acyclic orientations. We then determine the complete finite value set: these densities are exactly the Lagrangians of finite loopless digraphs, and hence are rational. The main technical input is a low-resolution sampling method that preserves all pairwise bipartite degree profiles on a large subfamily of color classes while keeping the sample size independent of the number of retained classes.
Gregory F. Lawler; Fredrik Viklund; Yilin Wang; Catherine Wolfram

We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $ρ$, where $ρ$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $ρ$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ for all $κ\geqslant 0$. As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.
The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II

We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $φ[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.
Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3

We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-Künneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.
Simultaneous energy and entropy stability of volume-penalisation immersed-boundary methods for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations
Abbas Ballout; Albert Jiménez-Ramos; Gonzalo Rubio; Esteban Ferrer

Immersed-boundary methods avoid body-fitted meshes, but the energy or entropy stability of the underlying flow discretisation does not automatically extend to the immersed treatment. This manuscript analyses the volume-penalised compressible Navier--Stokes equations for both energy and entropy stability, on the continuous and semi-discrete levels, and integrates the isolated source exactly in time. The source is formulated as a one-parameter family indexed by $θ$, whose momentum component relaxes the fluid velocity towards the prescribed solid velocity; $θ$ sets how much of the resulting kinetic-energy loss leaves the domain rather than being converted to internal energy. The two stability requirements impose opposing bounds on $θ$, with dissipation of the relative total energy requiring $θ\geq0$ and stability of the mathematical entropy requiring $θ\leq1$. Where penalisation acts, both conditions are therefore satisfied if and only if $0\leqθ\leq1$, and the symmetric value $θ=1/2$ divides the kinetic-energy loss equally between the domain and the internal energy. We conclude that any entropy-stable split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method remains semi-discretely entropy stable once the source is added at the collocation nodes, for stationary and prescribed moving bodies alike.
Rarity Determines Minimax Rates of Semantic Entropy From Weak Pairwise Judgments With a Known Channel

The semantic entropy of a language model is the entropy of the meanings of its sampled answers. The meanings are never observed, and the entropy is estimated from the verdicts of a pairwise equivalence judge. Given the meanings of $n$ answers, a known channel declares each pair equivalent independently, with probability $q+Δ$ within a meaning and $q$ across meanings. At most $K$ meanings occur, and $q$ is bounded away from $0$ and $1$. For a weak judge, with $nΔ^2\to0$, the global minimax rate is set by distributions near a vertex of the simplex and overstates the difficulty elsewhere. We show that the difficulty is set by how many meanings can be rare. Over distributions with at most $s$ meanings below a fixed probability $τ<1/(K-s)$, the minimax squared risk is of order $N^{-1/s}$ for $s\ge2$, $N^{-1}\log^2(e+N)$ for $s=1$ and $N^{-1}$ for $s=0$, capped at one, where $N=n^KΔ^{2K-2}$. The matching lower bounds hold on every fixed polynomial window $nΔ^2\le n^{-κ}$. One estimator attains these rates without knowing $s$ or $τ$: it averages products of centered verdicts along all spanning trees of every $k$-set of answers, projects the resulting power sums onto the valid moment set and inverts them. The case $s=K-1$ gives the global rate $N^{-1/(K-1)}$ and the consistency threshold: with $Δ=n^{-γ}$ the entropy is uniformly consistently estimable exactly when $γ<K/(2K-2)$. On polynomial windows, the same estimator attains the sharp local minimax constant on shrinking neighborhoods of interior points with distinct probabilities. Restricting the average to stars multiplies the constant by $K^{K-3}$.
Control Realization of Schrödinger Bridges over Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems via Maximum-Entropy Distribution Steering

This paper shows how a Schrodinger bridge (SB) structure emerges from maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) distribution steering of discrete-time nonlinear systems. We also establish that the resulting bridge can be realized by an optimal control policy. We consider general state and input costs, non-Gaussian endpoint distributions, and input constraints. Assuming the existence of a feasible policy with finite objective value, we show that the state-path measure under a MaxEnt optimal control policy is the unique SB. The reference measure of this SB is induced by an optimal policy of the corresponding terminal-unconstrained problem. Moreover, we give an equivalent characterization of the optimal state-path measure using a killed reference and its normalized Feynman--Kac measure, thereby interpreting the state cost as killing. We then characterize the finite-cost feasibility by the existence of an endpoint coupling having finite Kullback--Leibler divergence from the reference endpoint distribution. For compactly supported marginals with bounded target density, we derive reachability-based sufficient conditions guaranteeing this feasibility. We further provide specializations to fully actuated control-affine and reachable linear systems.
Two-Dimensional Torus Action on the Quadric Threefold and GW-DT-GV Correspondence

We compute Gromov--Witten (GW) and Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants (including descendant invariants) for local CY $4$-folds over a smooth quadric threefold $Q$, up to degree $4$. We use the virtual localization formula with respect to a two-dimensional torus action to compute DT invariants. Combining these results with the computation of the J-function of the variety $Q$, we confirm the correspondence between DT and Gopakumar--Vafa invariants suggested by Cao--Maulik--Toda in genus zero. Based on these results, we predict a genus one BPS invariant on $Q$.

In this paper, we first construct infinitesimal equivariant analytic torsion forms for Kähler fibrations. We then compare them with Ma's equivariant analytic torsion forms, modulo $\partial$- and $\overline{\partial}$-exact forms, in terms of equivariant Bott--Chern currents and the $I$-genus. Our comparison formula extends that of Bismut and Goette to families.
A generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values via Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation

We establish a generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values using Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation formula. As an application, we prove a restricted sum formula in which the parity of each component of the index is prescribed. We also derive a generating function identity for finite multiple zeta values $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(\{1,2\}^n)$ and symmetric multiple zeta values $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{S}}(\{1,2\}^n)$, thereby proving Kaneko's conjecture for finite multiple zeta values and its symmetric analogue.

Let $\X$ be a variety of groups. A group $G$ is $\CSX$ if its maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal. We prove that the amalgamated free product of two $\CSX$-groups with a malnormal amalgam and without any involutions is again $\CSX$. Using this, we describe conditions under which the HNN-extension of a $\CSX$-group is $\CSX$.
Latency-Aware Uplink NOMA-MEC with PASS: A Feasibility-First Resource Allocation Framework
Sepehr Abolhasani; Saba Asaad; S. Mohammad Razavizadeh; Jiguang He

Meeting hard task-completion deadlines for many simultaneously offloading users is the binding challenge in mobile-edge computing (MEC). As the user count grows, the transmit power required to satisfy every deadline within per-user budgets rises until no feasible allocation exists. We take a \emph{feasibility-first} view of this $K$-user problem in an uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) MEC system served by a pinching-antenna system (PASS), whose radiating points establish strong line-of-sight (LoS) links that lower the received-power requirement. We formulate a latency-constrained joint optimization of transmit powers, CPU frequencies, and antenna configuration. We then derive a \emph{closed-form least-power feasibility test}: the componentwise-least allocation meeting every deadline. It certifies feasibility with the largest attainable margin to the power budgets and defines a practical \emph{quality-of-service (QoS)-feasibility outage} metric, the probability that no allocation meets all deadlines within budget. We solve the problem with a three-block alternating-optimization algorithm that is provably monotone-convergent and has polynomial complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme sustains deadline feasibility at user loads where equal-power, orthogonal multiple access (OMA), and single-antenna baselines fail or degrade sharply, each by a mechanism predicted directly from the system model, whereas the proposed design degrades gracefully. Stress tests further show that feasibility is sustained under order-of-magnitude budget reductions, and that the pinching-antenna array itself enables constrained-budget operation. The result is a scalable, closed-form-initialized design for deadline-feasible offloading.
Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres

Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.
Existence of solution for Schrödinger-Newton system with vanishing magnetic potential
Liying Shan; Wei Shuai; Ping Yang; Jianghua Ye

In this paper, we study the following Schrödinger-Newton system with a vanishing magnetic potential and an electric potential \begin{equation}\label{0.1} \left\{ \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25} \begin{array}{ll} (-i\nabla +A(x))^2u+V(x)u=Φu, \ & x\in\mathbb{R}^3,\\ -ΔΦ=|u|^2, \ & x\in\mathbb{R}^3, \end{array} \right. \end{equation} where $i$ is the imaginary unit, $A:\mathbb{R}^3\to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a continuous magnetic potential, and $V:\mathbb{R}^3\to \mathbb{R}$ is a continuous electric potential. Using this fact together with a global compactness lemma, a barycenter function, and Brouwer degree theory, we prove that under suitable conditions on $A$ and $V$, system admits either a ground state solution or a high energy solution. Interestingly, whether a ground state solution exists is significantly affected by the magnetic potential $A$ and the electric potential $V$. Furthermore, we provide sufficient conditions that guarantee the existence of a ground state solution, as well as conditions under which no ground state solution exists and a high energy solution appears instead.
Space-Time Parallel Direct Numerical Simulation of Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
Thomas Saupe; Thibaut Lunet; Mathis Bode; Robert Speck; Sebastian Götschel; Daniel Ruprecht

Rayleigh-Bénard convection (RBC) is a model for turbulent flow and challenging to simulate by direct numerical simulation (DNS). Adequate resolution of all relevant length scales requires very fine grids in space and stability restrictions can dictate small step sizes. In this paper, we investigate the use of parallel spectral deferred correction (SDC) as a high-order time-stepping method to reduce wall-clock times of direct numerical simulation of RBC. Performance results on JUSUF (CPUs) and JUPITER (GPUs) with two different codes show parallel SDC can offer some concurrency along the temporal axis plus larger maximum stable time steps. Taken together, this allows for a reduction of wall-clock time required for simulations over one free-fall time by having to compute fewer steps and being able to mitigate the higher cost per time step through temporal parallelization.
Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Systems and Orthonormal Fermionic Ground States in $\mathbb R$
Bin Chen; Yujin Guo; Yong Luo; Juncheng Wei

We study the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger system \[ -u_i''-2\Big(\sum_{k=1}^N u_k^2\Big)^{p-1}u_i=μ_i u_i \quad \mbox{in } \ \mathbb R,\ \ i=1,2,\cdots,N, \tag{S} \] where $u=(u_1,\cdots,u_N)\in H^1(\mathbb{R})^N$, $μ_1\leqμ_2\leq\cdots\leqμ_N<0$, $1<p<3$ and $N\geq 2$ are arbitrary. We then investigate a fermionic variational problem $J_N(p)$ with $N\ge2$, whose minimizers correspond to ground states of the system $(S)$ under orthonormal constraints. More precisely, we prove that there exists a sufficiently small $δ_N>0$ such that $J_N(p)$ is attained for any $p\in(2-δ_N,2)$, whereas $J_N(p)$ is not attained for any $p\in[2,2+δ_N)$. Block diagonal preconditioners for arrow-shaped multiple saddle-point linear systems

We consider multiple saddle-point linear systems with block-arrow structure. We analyze exact and inexact Schur complement based block diagonal preconditioner, by characterizing the eigenvalues of the preconditioned matrices in terms of the zeros of specific rational functions. Numerical results onto large tests coming from liquid crystal modeling and PDE-constrained optimization validate the obtained eigenvalue bounds

We construct a stationary weakly harmonic map from a domain in \R^5 into a compact Kähler surface for which a tangent map is weakly harmonic but nonstationary. The target manifold is the blow-up of \CP^1\times\CP^1 at four points lying in one fiber and arranged at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. The nonstationarity of the tangent map arises from the break down of the tetrahedral symmetry in the defect measure concentrated on the vertices.
Chordal Codes: Code Construction and Efficient Gaussian-Elimination Decoding
Yulin Chen; Laigang Guo; Tong Li; Mingyang Zhu

Maximum-likelihood decoding of linear codes over erasure channels can be considered as solving a linear system of a column submatrix of the parity-check matrix. In practice, Gaussian elimination is usually applied, and its computational cost depends on the structure of the matrix, especially the sparsity and the fill-in generated during the elimination. The \emph{chordal graph}, or \emph{triangulated graph}, first introduced by C. Berge, has a so-called \emph{perfect elimination ordering}, indicating that if the primal graph of a matrix is a chordal graph, then there exists a perfect elimination ordering such that a special class of fill-in under Gaussian elimination following this ordering will be avoided. In this paper, we introduce \emph{chordal codes}, i.e., codes equipped with parity-check matrices such that the primal graphs of the parity-check matrices are chordal. We prove that, for a chordal code, the decoding submatrix associated with any erasure pattern retains a chordal primal graph. So, the complexity of chordal elimination (Gaussian elimination following the perfect elimination ordering applied to the chordal code decoding) will be smaller than decoding a random code by Gaussian elimination. Also, we provide an upper bound on the complexity of chordal elimination.
Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades

The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $κ_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $κ_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $κ_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $μ_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $κ_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty} \| κ_T-|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$ Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty}S[κ_T]=0 \, , $$ without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[κ_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.
On integrability of local utility maximizing strategies

In stochastic control problems involving optimal portfolio choice, one often seeks an optimizer of some local criterion (dynamic programming value function) generated by some global criterion (e.g., expected utility). The local optimizer then typically acts as a stochastic integrand with respect to some multivariate stochastic process (e.g., asset prices). This paper takes a closer look at local criteria in the form of ``local expected utility''. Since the existence of the local optimizer can be established under very mild conditions, it is crucial to understand under what circumstances the local optimizer has good integrability properties. It is shown that the reasonable asymptotic elasticity condition of Kramkov and Schachermayer (1999) applied to the local utility function plays a key role in this context.
Routing Optimality for Demand Graphs of Matching Number at Most Two

We prove that network coding and fractional routing have the same capacity region in undirected networks whose demand graph has matching number at most two, that is, when no three demand edges have pairwise disjoint endpoints. The metric-packing reduction of Liu et al. reduces this problem to a distance-weighted communication inequality on the fixed graph $Γ_{3,3}$. We first prove two entropy inequalities for sessions between designated terminal pairs on $Γ_{3,3}$. We then extend this result to sessions with arbitrary endpoints to obtain the distance-weighted communication bound required by the reduction. The proof combines conditional entropy inequalities with two graph contractions and an information inequality for deterministic interaction. Combining this inequality with the existing reduction establishes routing optimality for this class of demand graphs.
Geometry and barycenters in large $\CAT(κ)$ spaces
Yassine Boukhateb; Victor-Emmanuel Brunel; Austin J. Stromme

We study the geometry and resulting properties of Fréchet functions and barycenters in metric spaces with curvature bounded above by a positive constant in the sense of Alexandrov. Existing results typically rely on the assumption that the support is small enough that the squared distance, and thus the Fréchet function, is strongly geodesically convex. We work in the sharper regime where existence and uniqueness of the barycenter are guaranteed, but where convexity typically fails. We develop new geometric properties of these spaces, including a quantitative four-point inequality and a geodesic stability result. Using these tools, we establish new finite sample error bounds for two statistical estimators: the empirical barycenter and the iterated barycenter, as well as new results on sparse representations and approximations of barycenters.
Non-Contiguous Channel Allocation in Multi-Beam Satellites: Formulations, Upper Bounds and Cooperative Matheuristics

Demand for wireless communication is growing, and commercial satellite services are expanding with it, increasing pressure on a finite radio spectrum. Allocation efficiency directly limits how many users a satellite can serve. We study how to assign frequency sub-channels to the carriers of a multi-beam satellite, maximising the total priority of admitted carriers while keeping each within its interference tolerance. Earlier work on this interference-limited channel allocation problem placed each carrier in a single continuous frequency block. Removing this restriction can admit more carriers, but a direct integer programming model cannot solve the largest test problems in practical time, so new methods are needed. We prove the problem computationally hard, reformulate it around how carriers share sub-channels, and derive three bounds on the optimum. We develop heuristics, including matheuristics combining local search with optimisation models, and an orchestrated portfolio that schedules them, recombines their solutions and stops early once its result is proven optimal or no longer improves. On 24 problems with up to 500 carriers, the best heuristics come within about 1% of the best known solution on average. The portfolio matches or exceeds the best heuristic for each problem on 23 of 24 with equal weights and 22 with priority weights, and is up to about 5% better on larger, more congested problems. It requires about a quarter of the time to run every heuristic and keep the best, and under half that of its heuristics run in a fixed order, which return slightly worse solutions on average.
The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
Yueying Lou; Youle Xu; Qichun Wang

Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.
Provable Method of Moments for Cryo-EM
Amnon Balanov; Tamir Bendory; Dan Edidin; Josh Katz; Shay Kreymer; Nir Sharon

We study the recovery of a three-dimensional volume in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) from noisy tomographic projections acquired at unknown viewing rotations, drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. We show that, in a spherical-shell representation satisfying an explicit shell-separation condition, the first three moments generically determine the underlying real volume up to its intrinsic global $\mathrm{O}(3)$ ambiguity. The proof is constructive and yields a frequency-marching procedure that successively recovers the volume. Consequently, consistent recovery in the high-noise regime has sample complexity $n=ω(σ^6)$, where $n$ is the number of observations and $σ^2$ is the noise variance. Numerical experiments validate the constructive recovery scheme under finite sampling and additive noise, and indicate that direct third-moment optimization can succeed beyond the structural assumptions required by the constructive proof.
The logarithmic exponent of the Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
We prove that $r(4,t) \ge \frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}$. This improves the lower bound of Mattheus and Verstraëte (Ann. of Math., 2024) by a factor of $(\log t)^{2-o(1)}$.
Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition

We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition. The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.
Multiplicity One for Five Strongly Tempered Spherical Varieties

Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We prove multiplicity one for every irreducible smooth admissible representation in the split forms of Wan-Zhang Models 6-10. Combining the Gelfand-Kazhdan method with nilpotent-wavefront restrictions on Bernstein-finite equivariant distributions, we establish the required symmetries through rational orbit analysis, parabolic descent, stabilizer characters, and conormal arguments. The type-$D_6$ analysis treats both the vector-similitude group of Model 9 and the semispin form arising in the exceptional $E_7$ model. For Model 10, the distribution theorem gives a product bound for periods; the individual multiplicity bound follows from Langlands classification and a vanishing theorem for standard modules induced from nongeneric tempered data on the maximal $E_6$ Levi.

Extending the notions of Kneser graphs and Schrijver graphs, we define the $G$-stable Kneser graph $KG(G,k)$ (where $k\geq 2$ and $G$ is a graph on $n\geq 2k$ vertices) as the graph whose vertices are the $k$-element independent sets in $G$ and whose edges join pairs of disjoint independent sets. Dynamics of low energy wave packets in the one-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet

Spin wave theory plays a central role in the analysis of low-energy properties of the quantum ferromagnetic Heisenberg model. In this work, we present a first step towards a rigorous justification of this approximation in the context of quantum dynamics in one dimension. Our main result establishes this idea rigorously for a class of spin wave packets. We focus on spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ systems, and consider wave packets composed of two magnons. Moduli descriptions of v-sheaf local models

A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
Jiale Chen; Min He; Maofa Wang

The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code RM(1,9) is 242

What is the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,9) ? This is a long-standing open problem in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we resolve this problem, and prove that the covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242. We exclude nonlinearity 244 by obtaining a cubic Boolean function achieving a sharp Walsh $\ell^1$ bound. To exclude nonlinearity 243, we deduce the inequality ${\Vert W_g\Vert }_{1}+2|W_g(0)|\le 10368$, and then reduce either to a spectrum bounded by 24 or to the same expression to be at least 10496.

For every even Galois representation in a family of prime conductor $\ell$, we prove that if $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is maximal such that \[\ell \equiv 1 \bmod 3^k\] then the even mod $3$ deformation ring $R_S \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_3} \mathbb{F}_3$ of level $S=\{\ell,3\}$ does not have a quotient isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_3[T]/(T^{2+3^{k-1}})$. As a corollary, we deduce that the global even deformation rings $R_S$ are finite and flat in the category of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-modules.

For every integer $d\geq 3$ and real number $Q\in \left(d,\frac{d(d-1)+2}{2}\right]$, we construct a $Q$-Ahlfors regular metric measure manifold $(M,\mathbf{d},μ)$ of topological dimension $d$ and analytic dimension $2$ that satisfies a Poincaré inequality. We prove that, under suitable assumptions, the space of order continuous orthogonally additive operators between Riesz spaces is a Riesz space. As a consequence, we give a negative answer to an open problem posed by Mykhaylyuk and Popov concerning the order continuity of the modulus of an order continuous orthogonally additive operator. We also show that, under an appropriate condition on the domain, every order continuous orthogonally additive operator is order bounded, obtaining an orthogonally additive analogue of the corresponding result for linear operators. Moreover, we establish the order boundedness result in ZF for atomic Riesz spaces and in ZF with dependent choice (DC) for Dedekind complete Riesz spaces. Finally, we characterize when every orthogonally additive operator is an abstract Uryson operator.
Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control

This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. We also propose the enforcement of differential constraints via pseudospectral operators, and the primal and dual equivalence of this approach to state augmentation is established for control-rate limits. The numerical developments include the formulation and solution of heterogeneous multiphase optimal control problems, parameterized non-affine time mappings, composition of affine scaling and equilibration methods, and a hybrid derivative strategy to combine linear pseudospectral operators with numerical derivatives for nonlinear functions. These methods are implemented in the RAPTOR (Rapid Algorithm for Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimization and Robustification) transcription framework and assessed through feature-oriented benchmarks: a one-dimensional landing problem, a planar orbit-raising scenario, an atmospheric entry problem, and a multiphase reusable launch vehicle problem with simultaneous booster-recovery and upper-stage-insertion trajectories.
Counting triangles in graphs without suspensions of paths

For a graph $H$, the suspension $\widehat H$ of $H$ is a graph obtained from $H$ by joining a new vertex to every vertex of $H$. The generalized Turán number $\textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat H)$ is the maximum number of triangles in an $n$-vertex $\widehat H$-free graph. For fixed $k \ge 4$, Mubayi and Mukherjee conjectured that \[ \textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat P_k) =\left\lfloor\frac{k-2}{2}\right\rfloor\frac{n^2}{8}+o(n^2), \] as $n \to \infty$, where $P_k$ is the path on $k$ vertices. They verified the conjecture for $k=4,5,6$. In this paper, we determine the asymptotic value of $\textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat P_k)$ for every $k\ge 4$ via a unified approach and thus prove the conjecture of Mubayi and Mukherjee.
Learning Hamiltonians from Trajectory Data with Kernel Methods
Jianyu Hu; David Martin de Diego; Juan-Pablo Ortega; Miguel Vaquero

We study the recovery of a Hamiltonian from discrete trajectory observations using structure-preserving kernel methods. When exact-flow data are fitted through a symplectic one-step scheme, the fixed-step learning target is generally not the physical Hamiltonian itself, but a scheme-dependent inverse modified Hamiltonian. For the implicit midpoint and $p$-implicit symplectic Euler methods, we establish the existence of analytic inverse targets and show that their discrepancies from the physical Hamiltonian are second and first order in the observation step, respectively. Within an RKHS framework, we derive finite-sample reconstruction bounds for random trajectories, allowing dependence among observations from the same trajectory, and separate the error into estimation, approximation, and integrator-induced components. We further establish stability under noisy trajectory observations and develop a multistride Richardson correction that systematically raises the order of the integrator-induced error without requiring additional trajectories. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scheme-dependent orders, the effect of Richardson correction, and the applicability of the method across several Hamiltonian systems.
How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?

Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.
Minimal norm control problems for linear mean-field control systems
Manfen An; Rui Gao; Yanqing Wang

This paper studies controllability and minimal norm control problems (NP problems) for mean-field stochastic differential equation (MF-SDE) systems. We first establish an equivalent rank criterion for terminal controllability, namely, that the diffusion matrices $D$ and $D+\bar D$ are both of full row rank.
