We then derive an explicit Riccati-based representation of the minimal norm control by applying a parameterization technique. A key step is to identify the value $P(0)$ of an associated Riccati solution with the controllability Gramian of a controllable auxiliary system, which yields the parameter required in the construction. The resulting representation provides a basis for the future development and analysis of numerical methods for NP problems.
Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes

We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.
Aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera of Kähler varieties
Jiawei Feng; Yi Li; Sheng Rao

We study several aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera in Kähler families over a smooth curve. First, for a relatively flat coherent sheaf, we characterize local constancy of fiberwise cohomology dimension by equivalent conditions in terms of extension, base change, torsion freeness of higher direct images, and the vanishing of jumping classes. Then, combining this criterion with the Kähler minimal model program, we prove invariance of plurigenera for Kähler families of threefolds whose central fiber has canonical singularities, and for smooth Kähler families of maximal Albanese dimension. We also establish deformation invariance of log plurigenera when the central fiber is projective, and is of log general type. We prove the invariance of higher cohomological plurigenera assuming that the canonical bundle of the total space is semipositive. Finally, we extend Z.~Li--Z.~Wang's deformation invariance result for generalized polarized pairs with abundant nef parts from projective families to Moishezon families.
$L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
Nikolay Barashkov; Giacomo Di Gesù; Petri Laarne

We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $Φ^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $Φ^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schrödinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $Φ^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $β^2<2π$. For $Φ^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $β^2<4π$, and for $Φ^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.

For a Bruhat interval $[x,y]$ in an arbitrary Coxeter group which is a lattice, we give a type-uniform construction of a convex polytope whose complete face lattice realizes $[x,y]$. This gives a polytopal realization of the coincidence between classical Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for lattice Bruhat intervals and Stanley's toric $g$-polynomials. Consequently, the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial of a lattice Bruhat interval cannot have internal zeros, satisfies a multiplicative strengthening of monotonicity, and obeys the generalized upper bound theorem for polytopes. For lattice Bruhat intervals in finite Weyl groups, we explain the relation with the toric geometry of Richardson varieties and derive formulas for their local and global intersection cohomology, as well as a Boolean criterion for rational smoothness. We conjecture that the coefficients of these Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials form an $M$-sequence.
Learned Score-Based Turbo Message Passing for Channel Recovery From Spatially Compressed Measurements

Hybrid beamforming (HBF) reduces the hardware cost of massive MIMO base stations, but its channel acquisition requires recovering the full spatial-domain channel from highly compressed beam-domain observations. This paper proposes a learned score-based turbo message passing (L-STMP) framework for uplink HBF channel recovery under extreme spatial compression. By deeply unfolding the turbo message-passing loop and introducing trainable calibration parameters and learnable score priors in each layer, L-STMP liberates STMP from the idealized compression-matrix requirements of right-rotational invariance, and reduces inference complexity to only several unfolded layers. In addition, to preserve dominant channel components that random discrete Fourier transform (DFT) selection may miss, we introduce precoding matrix indicator (PMI)-assisted beam selection as a low-overhead directional prior. Simulation results demonstrate that L-STMP consistently outperforms existing baselines and obtains substantial reconstruction gains under PMI-assisted compression in channel reconstruction.
Asymptotic Lech Bounds and Bertini Flags

For a $d$-dimensional Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak{m})$, with $d>0$, let $c_{\infty}(R)$ be the limit, as $N\to\infty$, of the suprema of $e_R(I)/(d!\ell_R(R/I))$ over ideals $I$ with $\sqrt{I}=\mathfrak{m}$ and $\ell_R(R/I)>N$. We prove that if $R$ is complete, reduced, equidimensional, and Cohen--Macaulay on the punctured spectrum, with $d\geq2$ and infinite residue field, then every nonzerodivisor $x\in\mathfrak{m}$ satisfies \[ c_{\infty}(R)\leq \max\left\{c_{\infty}(R/xR), \sup_{\mathfrak{p}\ne\mathfrak{m}}e(R_{\mathfrak{p}})\right\}. \] As an application, we prove the asymptotic Lech conjecture of Huneke, Ma, Quy, and Smirnov in arbitrary characteristic: $c_{\infty}(R)=1$ whenever $\widehat{R}$ has isolated singularities. This also settles the conjecture of Ma and Smirnov that the Lech--Mumford constant $c_{\mathrm{LM}}(R)$ is attained when $\widehat{R}$ has isolated singularities and $c_{\mathrm{LM}}(R)>1$. For reduced equidimensional Cohen--Macaulay standard graded algebras of dimension $\geq2$ over infinite perfect fields, we prove attainment and rationality of $c_{\mathrm{LM}}$ for the completed vertex local rings of sufficiently high Veronese subrings. In characteristic zero, a refinement of our method produces nonisolated klt affine cones in every dimension $d\geq3$, with $d-2$-dimensional singular loci, whose completed vertex local rings have $c_{\infty}=1$ and arbitrarily large $c_{\mathrm{LM}}$.
The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods

We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,θ)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The algebraic theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. Moreover the algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^θ)^\circ(F)$ and $G^θ$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, as in the work of Blanc and Delorme on open periods, we obtain explicit bounding polynomials for the singularities of the intertwining period. Such bounds are a key ingredient of a new proof of the cuspidal case of a conjecture of D. Prasad on quaternionic symplectic models.
Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
R. Campoamor-Stursberg; A. Marrani; M. Rausch de Traubenberg

Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.
Cutoff profiles and boundary effects in the Togashi-Kaneko model of autocatalytic reactions with weak mutations

We determine explicit bulk and worst-case total variation cutoff profiles for the configuration law of a two-species Togashi--Kaneko model with a fixed population of $n$ particles and weak mutations. Boundary initial conditions introduce an additional logarithmic growth phase and change both the leading mixing-time coefficient and the limiting cutoff profile. Let $κ_1,κ_2>0$ be the autocatalytic rate constants and put $λ_*=κ_1κ_2/(κ_1+κ_2)$. For deterministic initial configurations whose density converges to $m\in(0,1)$, the total variation distance to equilibrium at time $t_n(s)=\frac{\log n}{2λ_*}+\frac{s}{λ_*}$ converges to $\mathcal G(r(m)e^{-s})$ for every fixed $s\in\mathbb R$, where $\mathcal G(r)=d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal N(r,1),\mathcal N(0,1))$, $r(m)>0$ is explicit, and $\mathcal N(a,b^2)$ denotes the Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and variance $b^2$. For the worst-case distance $\mathscr D_n(t)$ over all initial configurations, we prove $\mathscr D_n(T_n+s/λ_*)\to\mathcal P(s)$, where $T_n=\left(\frac{1}{\min\{κ_1,κ_2\}}+\frac{1}{2λ_*}\right)\log n$.The profile $\mathcal P$ is the total variation distance between the equilibrium Gaussian and a Gaussian mixture whose random displacement is determined by a gamma-distributed amplitude arising from early growth at the boundary. Unlike the bulk profile, $\mathcal P$ depends on the mutation parameters. Both cutoffs have windows of constant order, and we identify the asymptotically worst boundary configurations.

We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).
Ground states of a logarithmic Schrödinger equation with a power perturbation in $\mathbb{R}^N$: existence, uniqueness and nondegeneracy

The objective of this paper is to study the existence and uniqueness of positive ground state solutions of the following Schrödinger problem \[ -Δu=u\log u^2+μ\abs{u}^{p-1}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb {R}^N, \] where $N\ge2$, $1<p<2^*-1$ and $μ>0.$ We prove that there exists a positive ground state solution for every $μ>0$ and every such solution is smooth, radially symmetric with respect to some point, strictly decreasing in the radial variable. Moreover, as $μ\downarrow0,$ the positive ground state solutions centered at the origin will converge, uniformly over the ground-state set, to $U_0(x)=\exp(\frac{(N-\abs{x}^2)}{2})$ in the logarithmic Orlicz--Sobolev space and in $C^{2,α}(\R^N)$ for every $α\in(0,1),$ respectively. Furthermore, for sufficiently small $μ,$ we also prove that the positive ground state solutions are unique up to translations and the kernel space of the real scalar linearized operator can be spanned by the translation derivatives. The proof combines minimization on the Nehari manifold with uniform compactness and an exterior coefficient estimate that prevents normalized difference and kernel sequences from vanishing locally.
The sobriety for locally compact dcpos

In this paper, we focus on an open problem whether every locally compact dcpo is sober for the Scott topology. Specifically, we obtain two sufficient conditions for answering this problem. The main results are (1) every meet continuous locally compact coherent dcpo is sober with respect to the Scott topology; (2) the Scott space of every locally compact second countable dcpo is a sober space.
POD-accelerated high-order multiscale method with corrected-basis reconstruction for transient multi-continuum problems
Jiayuan Peng; Hao Dong; Jiale Linghu

Multi-continuum models provide an effective macroscopic description of transient flow in fractured and highly heterogeneous porous media by introducing several interacting state variables at each macroscale location. Although high-order multiscale (HOMS) methods reduce the cost of resolving microscopic heterogeneities while recovering local oscillatory features, repeated solution of the coupled homogenized system and repeated high-order reconstruction remain expensive in long-time and large-scale three-dimensional simulations. This work develops a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) accelerated HOMS framework for transient multi-continuum problems. A vector-valued POD space is constructed from snapshots of the coupled homogenized solution, and the resulting block system is projected onto a low-dimensional space. Two recovery strategies are considered. The first reconstructs the reduced homogenized fields and performs full HOMS assembly at every output time. The second applies the spatial part of the multiscale recovery operator to retained POD modes offline and evaluates the online solution by direct linear combinations of corrected bases and time-derivative bases. An error estimate between the fully discrete homogenized solution and its POD-reduced approximation is established for the coupled system. A recovered POD-HOMS estimate is then obtained by combining the HOMS consistency error with POD truncation errors propagated through value, gradient, inter-continuum exchange, second-derivative, and time-derivative recovery terms. Numerical experiments for two- and three-dimensional heterogeneous configurations show that the reduced solutions retain the accuracy and local oscillatory behavior of the corresponding HOMS solution while substantially decreasing computational cost.
Portfolio Selection by Joint Estimation-Robustness Optimization with the Return and Risk Constraints
Yingxiao Wang; Lingchen Kong; Selin D. Ahipasaoglu; Houduo Qi

In answering the main criticism of the classical robust optimization that the size of the uncertainty set has to be determined beforehand, a recently proposed Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework treats the size of the uncertainty set as a variable and maximizes it subject to some robust conditions over the uncertainty set. This paper studies its effect on portfolio selection when both the robust return and risk constraints are built into Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework. Although this framework does not directly pursuit any optimality of portfolio return or risk, we report a surprising result that Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework actually selects efficient portfolios. This is proved by reformulating the robust risk constraint as a tractable form through the S-procedure. Moreover, a closed-form formula was derived when there is only the budget constraint. An efficient algorithm is proposed when more constraints are added. Numerical experiments illustrate the validity of the reported results. This research paves the way for Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework to be applied to the portfolio selection problem with return and risk related robust constraints.
Vanishing viscosity limit of the stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus
Xinghong Pan; Chuankai Zhao; Jianfeng Zhao

In this paper, we establish vanishing viscosity limit of the 2D stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus with a fixed width. The flow is subjected to a large perturbation of a rotation of rigid body at one boundary and stays at rest at another boundary. Due to this different boundary condition setting, the boundary layer effects are different near the interior and exterior boundaries, which result in different thickness of boundary layer and different leading order boundary layer equations. We will construct an approximate solution to this 2D Navier-Stokes equations by using higher order asymptotic approximation and show the validity of the boundary layer expansion. The leading order of the Euler solution is the Taylor-Couette flow $\left(Ar+B\frac{1}{r}\right)e_θ$ for some suitable constant $A$ and $B$, which is determined by using the principle of the Prandtl-Batchelor theory. The perturbation of the tangential velocity becomes large as the annulus expands, which causes heavy difficulties when we show the convergence of the approximate solution. Variously weighted energy estimates up to third-order derivatives of the error solution are constructed to close the energy of the nonlinear system.
Cone restriction via direction-restricted two-ends Furstenberg estimates

We investigate a direct two-ends approach to restriction for the truncated cone in $\R^n$, which gives the diagonal restriction range \[ p>2+\frac{4(7n+15)}{11n^2-n-24},\qquad n\ge10. \] This improves the range obtained by applying the result of Wang--Wu and then slicing.
Dimensions and maximal-dimensional components of higher commuting varieties of symmetric pairs

Let $\mathfrak p$ be the $(-1)$-eigenspace of a complex semisimple symmetric pair. For every $r\ge2$, we prove $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))\le \lfloor r\dim\mathfrak p/2\rfloor$ and show that every irreducible component is isotropic for a natural family of alternating forms. For a nonzero Hermitian pair with $\mathfrak g$ simple and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p^-\oplus\mathfrak p^+$, put $d=\dim\mathfrak p^+$ and $\ell=\operatorname{rk}(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)$. Then \[ \dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=rd,\qquad \dim C_r(\mathfrak p)=\max\{rd,\,2d+(r-1)\ell\}. \] In this case we also determine the maximal-dimensional components of $C_r(\mathfrak p)$; for $r\ge3$, the only maximal-dimensional nilpotent components are $(\mathfrak p^+)^r$ and $(\mathfrak p^-)^r$. For arbitrary symmetric pairs, $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=ra+m$ for all large $r$, where $a$ is the largest dimension of an abelian subspace of $\mathfrak p$ consisting of nilpotent elements and $m$ is the dimension of the variety of such subspaces. Applications give dimension and component formulas for equivariant punctual Quot schemes under explicit framing conditions, and bounds for punctual Gorenstein loci refined by socle parity.
Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via Rényi Divergence
Amedeo Roberto Esposito; Adrien Vandenbroucque; Michael Gastpar

We investigate whether Rényi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by Rényi divergence of order $0<α<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of Rényi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to Rényi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.
Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Pentablock

The pentablock is a domain in $\mathbb C^3$ arising in the study of the $μ$-synthesis problem and is defined by \[ \mathcal P = \left\{ (a_{21},\operatorname{tr}(A),\det(A)): A=[a_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^2\in M_2(\mathbb C),\ \|A\|<1 \right\}. \] We introduce the Hardy space $H^2(\mathcal P)$ associated with the canonical measure $μ$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathcal P$. We identify $H^2(\mathcal P)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathcal P,μ)$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We establish a new description of $\mathcal P$ and its closure and obtain a uniqueness set. In particular, we prove that $\mathcal P$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $Ψ(\overline{\mathbb D}^3)$, where \[ Ψ(ξ,λ_1,λ_2) = \left( \frac{ξ(λ_1-λ_2)}{2}, λ_1+λ_2, λ_1λ_2 \right) \] is the parametrization map for $\mathcal P$. We also show that $H^2(\mathcal P)$ embeds isometrically as a closed subspace of $H^2(\mathbb D^3)$. We then obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathcal P)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathcal P$-isometries and their minimal $\mathcal P$-unitary extensions. As consequences, we determine the commutant of the coordinate multipliers, characterize the compact Toeplitz operators and show that the coordinate multipliers have no nontrivial joint reducing subspaces. Finally, we characterize $\mathcal P$-unitaries as images of commuting triples of unitaries under $Ψ$ and present a class of $\mathcal P$-contractions from triples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set.
A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin

We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler--Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also establish the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, proving that they never change sign.
Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
Hang Du; Brice Huang; Sidhanth Mohanty; Amit Rajaraman

We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β< 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.
Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
Zhiwen Liu; Stephen S. -T. Yau; Hao Zuo

We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.
Semi-Lagrangian Approximation of Master Equations with Individual Noise on Finite Graphs

We develop and analyze a fully discrete semi-Lagrangian method for vector master equations associated with mean field games (MFGs) with individual noise on finite graphs. The method discretizes both the characteristic evolution in time and the population variable on the probability simplex. A central challenge is the degeneracy of the transport coefficients near the boundary of the open simplex, where no boundary condition is prescribed. To overcome this difficulty in the analysis, we introduce an interior localization based on exact density characteristics, which keeps numerical arrivals within compact regions of uniform coefficient control. Combined with a closure argument for the coupled numerical recursion, this localization yields local solvability of the updates and quantitative error bounds on compact subsets of the open simplex. Under additional $C^2$-regularity of the exact solution and suitable space--time mesh coupling, these bounds imply first-order accuracy. Furthermore, the density and value trajectories generated by the numerical master feedback converge to the corresponding MFG characteristics at the same rate. In the potential setting, the associated reconstructed density--flux pair is admissible and asymptotically optimal for the planning problem, with an action gap quadratic in the feedback error. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates, feedback responses to population redistribution, and the effects of graph topology.

Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $q$ be a prime power. We prove that there exists a real constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that if $ \# M_n(\mathbb{F}_q) > C_k$ then every element in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is a sum of two $k$th powers, proving Larsen's conjecture.
H-PDLP: GPU-Accelerated Linear Programming via Generalized PDHG and Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding

GPU-based first-order methods are emerging as an approach for solving large-scale linear programming (LP) problems. We present H-PDLP, a GPU first-order LP solver based on a generalized primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method for a homogeneous self-dual embedding of the LP, and study its numerical performance. The solver applies the restarted reflected Halpern iteration to the generalized PDHG operator, with the embedding encoding both primal-dual optimal solutions and certificates of primal or dual infeasibility. We derive a compact embedding for LPs with two-sided constraint and variable bounds in which the bounds enter through box cones, and we show that the resulting box-cone projections reduce to one-dimensional root-finding problems, so that each iteration remains matrix-free and well suited to GPUs. On the theoretical side, we establish conditions under which the iterates remain uniformly bounded away from the trivial zero solution of the embedding and derive complexity guarantees for the method. We also introduce MIPLIBInfeas, a reproducible benchmark of 229 infeasible and 105 unbounded LPs derived from MIPLIB 2017. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on both feasible LPs and infeasible or unbounded LPs. The source code for H-PDLP is publicly available at https://github.com/MIT-Lu-Lab/H-PDLP.
Constant Rank Theorems under Intermediate Ricci Curvature

We prove two constant rank theorems for the Ricci tensor in two geometric settings: manifolds with harmonic curvature and gradient Ricci solitons. In both cases, if the $k$-intermediate Ricci curvature satisfies $\Ric_k\geq0$ for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$, then the Ricci tensor has constant rank and its nullity distribution is parallel. In the complete case, the universal cover splits isometrically along the Ricci-null directions. We also show that the range $1\leq k\leq n-2$ is sharp: in every dimension $n\geq4$, nonnegative Ricci curvature alone does not imply the constant rank property in either setting.
Least-Squares Finite Element Methods with Weakly Imposed Boundary Conditions: Norm and Error Equivalences, Over-Penalization, and Fully Discontinuous Discretizations

Weakly imposed boundary conditions in first-order system least-squares methods go back to Jespersen (1977), but two questions have remained open for decades: the right weights, especially for the Neumann residual, whose natural norm $H^{-1/2}$ suggests $h_F$, and norm and error equivalences, especially for indefinite equations. We answer both for general, possibly indefinite, second-order elliptic equations with non-homogeneous mixed boundary conditions. First, for the weights $h_F^{-1}$ on the Dirichlet and $1$ on the Neumann residual, we prove norm and error equivalences with mesh-independent constants for every discrete pair: the error in a mesh-dependent norm is equivalent to the square root of the functional plus a Dirichlet data term. The least-squares solution converges optimally in $H(\mathrm{div};Ω)\times H^{1}(Ω)$, and the functional is a reliable and efficient error estimator, with a recovered flux also for approximations from other methods, even ones violating the boundary conditions. The key idea is to apply the stability of the boundary value problem to pairs that are discrete only in their Dirichlet traces, whose $H^{1/2}$ norm an inverse inequality bounds by the weighted penalty. Second, these weights are the right ones: weaker powers, including $h_F$ on the Neumann boundary, destroy the norm equivalence, and stronger weights are admissible, since the penalty multiplies zero at a comparison function meeting the projected data. Third, for the fully discontinuous counterpart, a pure penalty method with both jumps weighted by $h_F^{-1}$, the error equivalence holds for every discrete pair, also for exact fluxes with normal traces not square integrable on interior faces.
A Minimum Exact Disjunctive Basis for Two-Robot Solvability Profiles
Tsukasa Ninomiya; Shota Naito; Naoki Kitamura; Yuichi Sudo; Koichi Wada

We completely characterize the solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movements. The four standard capability models and the schedulers considered here have a known quotient order Q of thirteen computational classes. A task's solvability profile is the set of classes in which it is solvable, and is necessarily an upset of Q. We prove that every upset is realizable and construct a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen concrete tasks. The basis contains one task for each principal upset. For every antichain of Q, the disjunction of the corresponding tasks has profile exactly equal to the union of their profiles. This exactness is not implied by the individual profiles: an algorithm may satisfy different disjuncts in different executions. We establish it by constructing, for every algorithm in each maximal class outside the target union, a single admissible fair execution violating all selected predicates simultaneously. Consequently, the realizable profiles form the entire finite distributive lattice Up(Q): there are exactly 54 profiles, counted by the antichain polynomial 1 + 13z + 24z^2 + 16z^3, and each has a canonical disjunctive representation using at most three principal tasks. We also identify six tasks whose solvability signatures recover every inclusion and incomparability in Q, and prove that six is minimum even among arbitrary separating tasks. Their profiles are precisely the principal upsets generated by the join-irreducible elements of Q. In contrast, any task family generating every profile by exact disjunctions must contain all thirteen principal profiles. Thus our exact disjunctive basis has minimum size and is unique at the profile level.
On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
Drazen Adamovic; Xuanzhong Dai; Kaiwen Sun

We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.
A matching lower bound for the sextic large sieve and structured prime moments

We study the contrast between the large-sieve norm and the second moment of structured prime coefficients for sextic residue characters over the Eisenstein integers. For squarefree row and column ideals of norms at most A and B, we prove a lower bound of order (AB)^(-epsilon) times (A + B + A^(5/6) B^(1/3) + A^(1/3) B^(5/6)), matching de Faveri's upper bound throughout the full parameter range. In particular, the squared full-cutoff norm at balance is at least Q^(7/6 - epsilon). The proof uses the uniform unmarked character moments of OpenAI's September 2026 manuscript, a Gauss second moment uniform in moving prime exclusions, and a centered comparison that transports a squarefree-row signal between column scales. With the additional unmarked inverse moment and buffered zero detector from the same source, we derive a low-height zero-density estimate and bound the second moment of a fixed smooth prime sum by Q^((37 - 10 sqrt(6))/6 + epsilon). We also treat bounded convolutions of independently weighted large primes. An appendix retains the first version's unbalanced lower bound and its exponent 17/16, without using the additional plain or inverse moment estimates.
Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds

In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact Kähler manifolds.
Global existence of the $s$-Schrödinger maps in $n \geq 5$

We study the $s$-Schrödinger map equation \[ \begin{cases} \partial_t u = -u \wedge (-Δ)^s u \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}\\ u: \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^2\\ u(x,0) = u_0. \end{cases} \] For $s \in (1/2,1)$ and $n \geq 5$ we prove that for small initial data $u_0$ in the critical Besov space one can obtain a global solution.
Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic

A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $α,β$ with $αβ=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.
textGrain watermarking is harder to detect: can sum-tests still do it optimally?

Watermarking embeds an imperceptible signal in text from large language models that is statistically detectable with a secret key. The recent textGrain watermark (Li et. al. (2026b)) calibrates this signal against the model's sampling entropy through an explicit entropy budget, combining the stochasticity of Red-Green and the unbiasedness of Gumbel-max watermarks, and its accompanying report proposes a detector that sums pivotal statistics. We study when, and how efficiently, textGrain can be detected after human edits, modeled as a sparse mixture in which a fraction $\varepsilon_n\asymp n^{-p}$ of positions retain the watermark and token uncertainty decays as $n^{-q}$. First, entropy calibration comes at a cost: the minimax detection boundary of textGrain is $p+q=1/2$, so its detectable region is strictly smaller than that of Gumbel-max and maximal-coupling watermarks, whose boundary is $2p+q=1$. This cost stems from textGrain's construction rather than from entropy calibration itself: an unbiased scheme with the same entropy loss remains detectable where textGrain is not. Second, perhaps surprisingly, this loss makes the sum detector optimal at the boundary when the number of transport columns is fixed, unlike for Gumbel-max. When the number of columns grows and the entropy budget does not vanish, the detectable region expands while that of the sum detector does not. Third, for a fixed edit fraction, we characterize the optimal exponential rate of type II error decay and show that the sum detector falls strictly short of it at every fixed alternative. Finally, we propose a weighted multiscale binomial scan, valid in finite samples and needing no knowledge of the next-token distributions, entropy budget, or edit fraction; it attains every detection boundary above and the optimal exponent.
Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$

Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $α,β$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $λ\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+λ$ if and only if $α,β\in k$ or $f(β)-f(α)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.
The local structure of refined class groups in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory

We give an explicit local description of ray class refinements in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory. For distinct primes $p\geq5$ and $\ell$, and even $2\leq k\leq p-3$, we prove that the $ω^{1-k}$-component of the $p$-primary ray class group of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$, with squarefree modulus supported above $\ell$, is nonzero if and only if $p\mid\ell(1-\ell^k)B_k$. In the cyclotomic tower, we determine the local modules and their correction modulo the diagonal global Tate module, obtaining an explicit determinant formula. Their Frobenius Euler factors, combined with the Mazur--Wiles theorem, yield a ray class form of the Iwasawa main conjecture for nonexceptional odd characters. We also obtain exact class number valuation comparisons at every layer, including those before stabilization, recover Finat's formula for $\ell=2$, and deduce refined $μ$-vanishing from Ferrero--Washington. The cyclotomic character explains the Wieferich exception, while existing Eisenstein congruence theorems connect the divisibility criteria with prime-level Ramanujan-style congruences.
A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories

By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $τ$-locally free modules.
Berezin Ranges of Composition Operators on $H^2$
Paul Bourdon; Trieu Le; Derek Thompson

We explore properties of the Berezin range $B(C_ϕ)$ of a composition operator $C_ϕ$ on the Hardy space $H^2$, including constraints on its location in the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$, topological properties, shape, symmetry, and convexity. For example, we show that $B(C_ϕ) \subseteq \{z\in \mathbb{C}: \Re(z) > 0 \ \text{and}\ |z| \le 1 + |ϕ(0)|\}$, that $B(C_ϕ)$ is closed if and only if $C_ϕ$ is the identity operator, and that $B(C_ϕ)$ containa all its boundary points except for $0$ if $C_ϕ$ is compact. Addressing questions raised by Cowen and Felder, we show that $C_ϕ$ can be a (nondegenerate) disk and characterize when $B(C_ϕ)$ is convex if $ϕ$ is linear.
Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
Shixin Wang; Shikang Yu; Tao Feng

A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $θ$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto xθ(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.

We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schrödinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schrödinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schrödinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.
Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
Jose D. Hoyos; Zehui Lu; Shaoshuai Mou

We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.
John Byrne; Colby Sherwood; Ioannis Tsokanos; Brian Wilmarth

After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.
Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
Rulong Xie; Hailian Wang; Lei Yang

In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.
Strong convergence rate of the implicit midpoint method for stochastic KdV equations
Junjie Li; Xinyan Niu; Chun Li

We establish a strong convergence rate for the implicit midpoint method applied to the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with additive noise, addressing a question that has remained open since the work of Debussche and Printems. To control nonlinear error growth, we obtain exponential integrability estimates for the exact and comparison solutions using the coercivity of a classical KdV invariant. We then derive local error bounds from estimates for the comparison solutions and control error accumulation through an $L^2$ error propagation identity that isolates a martingale increment. Under $H_0^{9/2}$ regularity assumptions on the noise and the deterministic initial data, we prove that, on every fixed finite time interval, the maximum $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ error at the time points is $O(h)$ in $L^p(Ω)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$. Notably, the exponential integrability and the convergence rate hold for every damping coefficient $λ\ge0$, including the undamped case $λ=0$. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted first-order convergence.
Guoli Ding; Jake Weber; Weihao Xia

When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$. Second, we establish how to grow $H$ inside $G$ while preserving twin-freeness and certain forms of connectivity. Third, we establish {\it finite test theorems} for various graph classes, proving that agreement with the recursively generated graphs for a few initial iterations forces agreement at all subsequent iterations. Consequently, such an infinite graph family can be completely determined by finitely many of its initial generations. As an application, we characterize $\{\mathbb L_1,\mathbb L_3\}$-free graphs, where $\mathbb L_1$ is the claw and $\mathbb L_3$ is another forbidden graph for line graphs. Our structural results reduce this problem to a finite verification, which is completed through computer-assisted computation.
Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines

Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $Φ\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circΦ=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.
Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities

In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $μ_1(ρ)$ and angular viscosity $μ_2(ρ)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.
Nonhomogeneous Subordinators and Lévy Copulas for Reliability Analysis of Time-Dependent Degradation Processes

Many systems in engineering applications may experience complex multi-dimensional degradation processes involving random jumps. Analyzing the reliability of such degradation processes presents significant challenges. Previously developed models have utilized multi-dimensional Lévy subordinators and Lévy copulas to describe these processes, with reliability functions expressed through characteristic functions and Laplace transforms (Shu et al., 2015, 2016, Shi et al., 2020, Shi and Feng, 2024). However, these models are restricted to stationary linear paths and homogeneous Lévy subordinators. In real-world scenarios, increments in a degradation process are often time-dependent and nonhomogeneous. To address this limitation of previous studies, this work extends existing degradation models by introducing nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators, which are designed to capture time-varying complexities inherent in degradation processes. Unlike conventional degradation models that often assume a constant rate of jumps, nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators aim to provide a more flexible representation of degradation behaviors that evolve under varying external conditions and internal system dynamics. Additionally, the joint behaviors of multiple degradation processes are characterized using Lévy copulas, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of system reliability. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the applicability of these models in lifetime analysis.
Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees

Inference-time alignment steers diffusion models toward downstream objectives without costly fine-tuning, but existing methods typically optimize expected cost (or reward) without explicitly controlling tail risk. In this work, we propose a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) under trajectory-level Kullback-Leibler regularization. We characterize the optimal path distribution and reverse transitions as functions of the CVaR threshold, reducing the alignment problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem over the threshold. We show that this one-dimensional optimization problem can be nonconvex in general, establish sufficient conditions for convexity, and introduce quadratic regularization to enable efficient derivative-free ternary search. Under suitable assumptions, we provide finite-sample guarantees for threshold optimization and value estimation, and combine them into a terminal total-variation bound relative to the regularized target under exact resampling. Experiments on synthetic data and image generation using Stable Diffusion demonstrate improved tail performance over risk-neutral baselines while maintaining competitive average cost.
On the existence problem for a double mean field equation and its application to prescribed curvature problems
Jiayu Li; Lei Liu; Yanjun Liu; Mingyuan Zhu

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemann surface with smooth boundary $\partial M$. Let $K(x)>0$, $h(x)> 0$ or $h(x)\equiv 0$ be two smooth functions on $M$ and $\partial M$ respectively. In this paper, we consider the following double mean field type equation with a nonlinear Neumann boundary condition related to a prescribed curvature problem \begin{equation}\label{equation:01} \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|} =2ρ\frac{Ke^u}{\int_MKe^u\,dv_g}, & \text{in }M,\\[1.2em] \displaystyle \partial_νu =2ρ'\frac{he^{u/2}}{\int_{\partial M}he^{u/2}\,ds_g}, & \text{on }\partial M, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $ρ> 0,\ ρ'\geq 0$ and $ρ+ρ'=2π$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial M$. When $h\equiv 0$, the second equation changes to $\partial_νu=0$ on $\partial M$. By introducing a boundary integration constant, we obtain a sufficient condition under which \eqref{equation:01} admits a solution. As a geometric application, we solve the prescribed curvature equation for both the Gauss curvature and the geodesic curvature in the case that $M$ is topologically a disk. When $(M,g)$ is the standard hemisphere $\mathbb S^2_+$, let $p\in \partial \mathbb S^2_+$ be a maximum point of $$ Φ(q)=h(q)+\sqrt{h(q)^2+K(q)}, \qquad q\in\partial \mathbb S^2_+. $$ Suppose \begin{equation*} K_ν(p)+2Φ(p)(-Δ_{\partial \mathbb S^2_+})^{1/2}h(p)<0. \end{equation*} Then the prescribed curvature problem \begin{align*} -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|}=2Ke^u, \text{in }\mathbb S^2_+,\ \ \partial_νu=2he^{u/2}, \text{on }\partial \mathbb S^2_+. \end{align*} admits a smooth solution.
Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
Dengming Xu; Chengming Duan; Yong Jin; Yuhao Ning

Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.
An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
Yi Lu; Rongrong Chi; Wei Ren

In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.
A Structure-Preserving Effective Linear Approximation of the Quantum Boltzmann Collision Operator
Shuang Hu; Bo Lin; Zhenning Cai

We construct a structure-preserving effective linear approximation of the quantum Boltzmann collision operator for Bose and Fermi gases in the normal phase. For variable hard-sphere kernels, the resulting Fourier spectral evaluation costs $O(N_v^4\log N_v)$, with $N_v$ velocity nodes per direction and no angular quadrature factor. The continuous operator conserves mass, momentum and energy and satisfies a linearized $H$-theorem. We also use the operator at local quantum equilibrium as an approximate collision Jacobian in a modified Newton solver that retains the full nonlinear residual. Numerical tests show smaller errors than the quantum BGK model in homogeneous relaxation and fewer full collision evaluations for steady Couette and Fourier flows than the same Newton solver using a quantum BGK Jacobian.
Targeted Entropy-Stable Nonlinear Artificial Dissipation for High-Order Spectral-Element Summation-By-Parts Discretizations
Zelalem Arega Worku; Alex Bercik; David C. Del Rey Fernández; David W. Zingg

Artificial dissipation improves the robustness of high-order methods for under-resolved flows, but can compromise accuracy and suppress physically relevant structures if its strength and spatial distribution are not appropriately controlled. We present a sensor-activated nonlinear artificial-dissipation framework, inspired by the residual correction method, for continuous and discontinuous summation-by-parts discretizations. In contrast to many existing spectral-element dissipation operators that either reduce the formal order of accuracy or target only the highest polynomial modes, the proposed framework permits design- and higher-order dissipation with explicit control over its magnitude, spatial distribution, activation, and convergence rate under mesh refinement. This modular construction also recovers several existing methods through appropriate choices of its components. The dissipation preserves discrete conservation and semidiscrete entropy stability whenever the base method satisfies these properties. It is dimensionally consistent, element local, and discretization agnostic, as the added term is constructed independently of the base spatial residual. For smooth solutions under suitable mesh assumptions, we establish parameter choices that retain the formal accuracy of the base discretization. Numerical experiments with summation-by-parts discretizations of the Burgers and Euler equations demonstrate substantially improved robustness for under-resolved flows and flows with shock waves while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, using the same parameter choices across several test problems. Overall, these results show that targeted dissipation can improve the robustness of high-order methods without excessive damping of resolved flow structures.
On the Real Waring Rank of a Biharmonic Form
Hua-Lin Huang; Yiming Liu; Yilun Tang

We develop an effective method for determining the real Waring rank and the real border rank of biharmonic binary forms. By means of real apolarity, we convert both of these problems into membership questions for regions bounded by a hypocycloid and an epicycloid. We further provide a computable algebraic criterion for the relevant memberships, which involves only the signs of certain real-valued resultants.
Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning

In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.
The $\ell$-degree Turán densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies

Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Turán density $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $α\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=α$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>α$. This confirms the conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao on codegree Turán densities for every $k > 3$. As an immediate consequence, the set $Γ^{k,\ell}_{\infty}$ of $\ell$-degree Turán densities of nonempty $k$-graph families is $[0,1)$ whenever $k>\ell>2$, which answers a question of Lo and Markström from 2014.
Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations

An efficient shallow Ritz method was developed in [8, 9] for one-dimensional linear diffusion and diffusion-reaction problems. In this paper, the method is extended to a nonlinear diffusion-reaction equation with a cubic reaction term: (1) a basic error estimate of the shallow Ritz discretization is established and (2) a reduced block Newton (rBN) method for solving the resulting non-convex optimization problem is developed. Again, the computational cost of the rBN method is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ for one-dimensional problems, where $n$ is the number of neurons. Combining a convex splitting scheme for time discretization with the efficient shallow Ritz method, we develop a time-stepping neural network method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. The unconditional energy stability of the time discretization and an error estimate in the $L^2$ norm are established. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the neural network approach yields accurate solutions for singularly perturbed nonlinear diffusion-reaction equations and the Allen-Cahn equation. The method effectively resolves interior and boundary layers without oscillations and significantly outperforms the finite element method on fixed uniform meshes.
On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4

A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case. For connected rank-$4$ chain graphs, we derive four explicit equations in the cell parameters that are necessary and sufficient for generalized cospectrality. These equations reduce to a quadratic equation in a single parameter. As a consequence, every connected rank-$4$ chain graph has at most one generalized cospectral mate, and the possible mate can be reconstructed explicitly. We further obtain a simple sufficient condition for a rank-$4$ chain graph to be determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) and, in particular, prove that every double star graph is DGS. Finally, we construct an explicit infinite family of non-double-star rank-$4$ chain graphs that are DGS but not determined by their adjacency spectra, with both the graphs and their complements being connected.
Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection

We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{ω_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{ω_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.
Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra

We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.
Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes
Han Bao; Shinsaku Sakaue; Kazuki Watanabe

Safety verification of a Markov decision process (MDP) asks whether the probabilities of reaching several failure states jointly lie in a convex safe region under every scheduler. Watanabe and Unno (2026) prove safety by refining an outer approximation of the failure probabilities, where each query bounds a nonnegative weighted sum of the probabilities. Their rule selects weights by the largest Euclidean violation. We present a unified framework to measure violation in an explicitly chosen error unit: directions are scored by the support-function gap between the outer approximation and the safe region, normalized by the support function of the unit. We show that the maximal score, when positive, equals the smallest enlargement of the safe region in multiples of that unit that contains the outer approximation. The Euclidean unit recovers the earlier rule; two new rules are generated by the unit cube and the safe region itself. We experimentally evaluate how the choice of measurement rule affects the performance of safety verification for MDPs.
Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
Kangsheng Liu; Lihui Lu; Qiong Zhang

We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+χ_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,π)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(η-δ,η+δ)\times(0,π)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|η|\leqδ$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.
On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.
Chika Hayashida; Joe Kamimoto; Ninh Van Thu

In this paper, we introduce a new class of unbounded Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb C^n$ ($n\geq 2$),which we call horn domains. We study the dimensions of the Bergman spaces,the holomorphic sectional curvature of the Bergman metric, and the holomorphic equivalence problem for such horn Reinhardt domains.
Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
Li Guo; Yunzhou Xie; Yi Zhang

A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.

We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $γ\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $γ$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required. The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[ L_s=\left\{ g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n): \int_{\mathbb R^n} \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-Δ)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.
Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity

In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-δ}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+δ}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.
Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge--Ampère Problem

We prove that every nonnegative source \(f\in L^1(Ω)\) in the Monge--Ampère equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }Ω, \] on a bounded uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}\) domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq2\), is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the outward normal derivative and may equal \(+\infty\). For each \(ω\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), it suffices to know these slopes for the cylindrical Dirichlet data \[ \frac{t_k^ω}{2}|P_ωx|^2,\qquad t_k^ω\to\infty, \] along any sequence of amplitudes, where \(P_ω\) projects onto \(ω^\perp\). The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change-of-variables formula and a large-amplitude limit then recover the Euclidean X-ray transform of \(f\), yielding uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative \(L^\infty\) sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and coincide with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. The argument also extends to \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight \(\vartheta\) is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. Conditional on existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions, the same cylindrical boundary-slope data determine every nonnegative \(L^1\) source.
Orthogonality of Defect Ideals for Jordan Homomorphisms

Let $φ\colon A\to B$ be a Jordan homomorphism of associative algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic different from $2$, with defect ideals $V_φ$ and $W_φ$. If $A=\operatorname{Alg}([[A,A],[A,A]])$, then $V_φW_φ=W_φV_φ=0$ and $V_φ\cap W_φ\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{Alg}(φ(A)))$. Moreover, the induced map modulo $V_φ\cap W_φ$ is standard. The annihilator bound is sharp, even in finite dimension. As an application, when $A$ is unital and $A=K(A)$, every Jordan homomorphism defined on $A$ is splittable and standard. In this setting, the corresponding result of Brešar and Zelmanov holds without the surjectivity hypothesis.
Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
Nishant Chandgotia; Zemer Kosloff; Shrey Sanadhya

We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},μ,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.
Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation

We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=λ_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $τ_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+τ_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrhoτ_q/[2(\varrho+τ_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions.
