The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves $\log_2(e)-1$ bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to $2/e$.
Peter J. Cameron; Vinod Kumar P. B

Graphs defined on groups, such as power graphs, enhanced power graphs and commuting graphs, form a hierarchy under inclusion of edge sets. We develop an analogous theory for topological spaces. To a space X we attach five graphs on the vertex set X, all invariant under homeomorphisms: the specialization, inseparability, closure-meeting, Urysohn and functional graphs. They form a diamond-shaped hierarchy whose members are null exactly when X is T_1, Hausdorff, Urysohn or functionally Hausdorff. The Urysohn graph always contains the square of the inseparability graph, with equality for Alexandrov spaces, and the hierarchy is compatible with products via the strong product of graphs. Every countable graph, together with isolated vertices, is the inseparability graph of a second countable T_1 space. For finite spaces we characterize the graphs that occur as inseparability graphs (every edge lies in the closed neighbourhood of a simplicial vertex), determine all coincidences between members of the hierarchy, and show that the specialization graph determines the weak homotopy type but not the space itself. Using Dowker duality we prove that the complexes of inseparable and of closure-meeting families are always homotopy equivalent and, under an acyclicity hypothesis, recover the weak homotopy type. We show that if the closure-meeting graph is a cograph then it is chordal, an analogue of a recent result for enhanced power graphs; the same holds for the inseparability graph of an Alexandrov space but not in general. Finally, following Cameron's work on topologies preserved by permutation groups, we show that for a topology invariant under a primitive group each graph is null or connected, and that the neighbourhood filters of the five graphs reverse the hierarchy, giving spaces whose specialization graph contains the Rado graph as a spanning subgraph.
Decomposition of functions of bounded variation in Ahlfors-regular PI spaces
Paolo Bonicatto; Panu Lahti; Enrico Pasqualetto

We prove that, on a non-compact Ahlfors-regular PI space, every function of bounded variation $f$ can be decomposed as a countable sum $\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ of monotone functions of bounded variation $f_n$, in such a way that the total variation of $f$ is the sum of the total variations of the functions $f_n$. Our result extends a Euclidean result of Bianchini and Tonon to the metric setting.
Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
Qian Zhang; Xuejun Cheng; Jiaming Shi; Yufei Zhao; Rugui Yao; Ye Fan

Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
Valentin Leplat; Zeyu Dong; Junfeng Yin

We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.
A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices

In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(λ_1,λ_2,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and $λ_2$ real, then $(λ_1+t,λ_2\pm t,λ_3,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with eigenvalues $λ_1\ge\dots\geλ_n$ and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $λ_1+d_1,\dots,λ_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list Guo-extreme if none of Guo's moves can be reversed within the set of symmetrically realizable lists. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modelled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if $A$ is irreducible and every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and vanishes wherever $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every trace-preserving direction (in every direction, if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry) and remain symmetrically realizable; in particular it is not Guo-extreme.
Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests

We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.
Generic nondegeneracy of constant mean curvature radial graphs

Given a smooth domain $D\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$, $N\geq 3$, and a positive constant $H$, we study radial graphs over $D$ with constant mean curvature $H$ which meet orthogonally the boundary of the cone spanned by $D$. The corresponding problem is given by a quasilinear elliptic equation on $D$ with homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. We investigate the structure of the solution set under smooth perturbations of the domain which are parametrized by an open set of $C^{3,α}$-diffeomorphisms of the sphere. After pulling the equation back to a fixed reference domain, we apply a classical transversality theorem and prove that, in the class of domains for which $N-1$ does not belong to the Neumann spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, there is a residual set for which every solution is nondegenerate. A consequence of our result is that, for every such domain and every $R>0$, the set of solutions whose $C^{2,α}$-norm is bounded by $R$ is finite.
Bounds for (k,c) model functions over p-adic fields

Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $ρ$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $ρ$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $ρ$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.
Nontrivial domains for the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem with small constant vorticity

In this paper, we first apply the implicit function theorem to find nontrivial solutions to the following Bernoulli's overdetermined problem \begin{equation} -Δu=γ\,\, \text{in}\,\,Ω\setminus\overline{D}, \,\, u=1,\,\,\partial_\mathbf{n} u=Q\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partial D, \,\,u=0\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partialΩ\nonumber \end{equation} for a fixed boundary $\partialΩ$ and a free boundary $\partial D$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ with $N\geq2$, where $γ$ is a sufficiently small constant, the Bernoulli value $Q$ is determined by the construction, and $Ω\setminus\overline{D}$ is a bounded ring-shaped domain. In dimension $N=n+1$ with $n\geq2$, we further study the existence of a nontrivial unbounded domain $Ω\setminus\overline{D}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ such that the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem admits a solution. This unbounded domain we construct is periodic in one variable and radial in the other variables by bifurcation analysis.
Unique Determination of the Lamé Parameters in Three Dimensions

We prove that the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for static isotropic elasticity uniquely determines both smooth Lamé parameters in a bounded smooth domain of \(\mathbb R^3\) under strong convexity. The proof uses an exact four-component Laplace-type reduction, but its decisive identities are obtained from physical elastic solutions. The characteristic quotient of the reduced system has rank three, whereas the leading physical adjoint lift supplies only two directions. We construct the missing polarization from the first nonvanishing correction of a reduced amplitude in the kernel of that lift. Paired with fixed primal and adjoint quotient frames, the resulting complex geometrical optics solutions yield a complete family of holomorphically weighted \(3\times3\) matrix moments through the physical Betti identity. Cauchy--Plemelj factorization converts these moments into an invertible relative transport normalized in the common exterior. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction and transport rigidity then determine a material ratio and the shear modulus, hence both Lamé parameters. No smallness, symmetry, separability, or analyticity hypothesis is imposed.
Sharing a unit, measuring a length: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for fractions from Grade 1 to Grade 8

Fractions require learners to revise properties associated with whole numbers. This paper presents a design rationale and a critical analysis of an eight-level source progression for fractions (Grades 1-8, nominal ages 6-14), from which the French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. Its central hypothesis is a bridge from sharing to numerical measure: a share of one unit is represented by a bar, read as a length relative to a specified unit, and located on the number line. The reference unit is kept stable in the initial tasks to focus attention on fraction magnitude, equivalence and operations; changing the unit is deliberately postponed, without treating this as a mathematical requirement or an established reduction in cognitive load. Three principles organise the meanings: sharing one unit, coordinating bars and number lines, and establishing fractions as numbers before explicitly treating them as scalar operators. Two supporting principles concern valid local justifications before formal generalisation and chains of equalities, introduced in Grades 2-3, with written reasons in lessons from Grade 4. The analysis relates these choices to the research literature and selected curricula, examines task strategies and feedback, and distinguishes realised features from discrepancies and proposed revisions. The source documents and their curriculum projections do not establish the order actually experienced by pupils. No empirical evaluation is reported. Primary hypotheses address transfer between representations, coordination of units and the numerical status of fractions before operators; the audit also identifies limits to the reproducibility of its findings.
Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs

In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.
Stochastic Geometrically Exact Beams: Continuous-Time Geometric Principles and Variational Discretizations
Minghang Du; François Gay-Balmaz; Tianzhi Li; Donghua Shi

Geometrically exact beams naturally arise in physical phenomena and engineering practice for modeling flexible structures, such as soft robotic manipulators and DNA structures. To the best of our knowledge, there appear to be no geometric integrators for stochastic geometrically exact beams in a variational formulation. In this paper, we introduce variational principles for the dynamics of stochastic geometrically exact beams, in both continuous- and discrete-time settings. By introducing perturbations via stochastic potentials and stochastic kinematics, we derive the equations of motion from a variational viewpoint. The resulting stochastic geometric integrators simultaneously discretize time and space in a parallel manner, which provides a distributed computational framework for solving the stochastic dynamics of complex beam systems. In particular, the proposed integrators are shown to be a stochastic extension of the well-known deterministic staggered leapfrog scheme for the wave equation, and also a stochastic extension of Yee's scheme for spatially one-dimensional computational electromagnetism. Numerical results are shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

Let $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ be the maximum, over all $k$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs $F$, of the absolute difference between the number of induced copies of $F$ in $H$ and its expectation in the binomial random $r$-graph with the same number of vertices as $H$ and edge probability $p$. Let $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ be the minimum of $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ over all $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $D_r(n,p)$ be the distance from $p\binom nr$ to the nearest integer. For fixed $r\ge3$, $k\ge2r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the quantity $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ has order $\max\!\left\{D_r(n,p),p(1-p)\right\}n^{k-r}$ whenever $p(1-p)n^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor/(\binom{2r-2}{r}-1)}\ge\varepsilon$. Using local moment estimates and switchings in a sparse reservoir, we construct one hypergraph with the nearest-integer edge count that controls all induced orders simultaneously.
C*-algebras of Essentially Tracially Rank One

We introduce the notion of essential tracial rank at most one for simple $C^*$-algebras. We show that separable simple $C^*$-algebras with essential tracial rank at most one have several regularity properties, including stable rank one, strict comparison, and tracial approximate divisibility. A finite amenable simple $C^*$-algebras with this property is $\mathcal Z$-stable. We also prove the converse. Thus this property gives a new characterization of separable simple finite amenable $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras and shows that these algebras admit a one-dimensional tracial approximation. In the unital real-rank-zero case, this approximation can be strengthened to show that the algebra has tracial rank zero. This completes a long-standing project. As a byproduct, we prove that every tracial state on a unital separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra is quasidiagonal and that the algebra itself is quasidiagonal. Consequently, every separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra of finite nuclear dimension has finite decomposition rank. None of these results requires the UCT.
The price of a weak shadow variable: inference under nonignorable missingness as relevance vanishes

When an outcome is missing not at random, identification is commonly restored by a shadow variable: a covariate that predicts the outcome but is excluded from the response mechanism. The literature treats the first requirement, relevance, as a yes-or-no condition. We make it continuous, parametrizing it by a scalar that scales the shadow variable's entire contribution to the moment conditions, and ask what inference costs as that scalar vanishes. One functional of the inverse weight governs the answer. We characterize it exactly, show that it fixes the effective sample size, and use it to sharpen the rates of the estimator that avoids the weight. The characterization is concrete. Whether the functional saturates or diverges turns not on boundedness of the outcome but on whether the tilting variable has an atom at its essential supremum: a binary outcome saturates, a uniform one does not. It also bounds how far a scanned set reaches, and that reach grows only as the square root of the logarithm of the sample size, so a thousandfold increase buys one unit of tilt while the set to be scanned widens. A reanalyzed credit-scoring study shows the cost: a characteristic an optimizing selector uses cannot satisfy exclusion.
Diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices and $ϕ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices

In this article, we present the diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary equivalence. For a unit quaternion $ϕ$, we also obtain the diagonalization result of $ϕ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary $ϕ$-congruence, which generalizes the Autonne--Takagi factorization of symmetric complex matrices and $ϕ$-Hermitian quaternion matrices.
Sylow $2$-Subgroups of Finite Groups with a Single Conjugacy Class of Involutions

We solve Brauer's Problem 33 by determining the finite $2$-groups that occur as Sylow $2$-subgroups of finite groups with a single conjugacy class of involutions. Besides the Sylow $2$-subgroups arising from the relevant non-abelian simple groups in Table 1, these are precisely the homocyclic, generalized quaternion, and Suzuki $2$-groups. The classification of finite simple groups is used in this paper.
Pairwise Compatibility Graphs of Unweighted Caterpillars

In this paper we study pairwise compatibility graphs whose witness tree is required to be an unweighted caterpillar. This is a natural restriction of PCGs, in the same line of research as the study of star witnesses, which led to the class of double-threshold graphs. In the caterpillar case, we show that this restriction is equivalent to a one-dimensional difference-labelling problem: a graph admits such a representation if and only if its vertices can be assigned integer labels so that adjacency is determined exactly by whether the absolute difference of two labels belongs to a given interval. Using this characterization, we derive structural properties of the class, including bounded twin-width, and study its relation with familiar graph families. We show that the class contains cycles and two-dimensional grids, while it excludes natural obstructions such as the subdivided star $S_{2,2,2,2,2}$, the cube graph $Q_3$, the wheel $W_6$, and the complement of the $3$-sunlet. We also consider restricted representations, including centipede witnesses and representations with a given interval and we give a polynomial-time recognition algorithm when the interval is fixed.
Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
Van Hao Can; Naoki Kubota; Shuta Nakajima

We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $μ$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $ξ>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (μ(v)+ξ)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_dξ, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=π$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.
Development and operational deployment of a staff rostering system using mathematical optimisation in a municipal water utility
Takaaki Kobayashi; Satoshi Matsumura; Satoko Moriguchi

We developed a staff rostering system for complex employment and staffing requirements at a municipal water utility and deployed it in routine operations at the Water Purification Office of Suita City Waterworks Bureau, Japan, in May 2026. We estimated that preparing a monthly roster took approximately 2-3 h after deployment, compared with 12-18 h previously. The system represents roster states, effective staffing and office assignments using binary and auxiliary integer variables and optimises the entire planning horizon. When the normal model yields no feasible solution, a second stage attempts to generate a reference roster by penalising weekly day-off shortages while retaining the other hard constraints. Outputs identify shortages and meeting-date changes applied before solving. Computational experiments used operational inputs for 14 staff over 245 days. The baseline was solved to optimality in approximately 177 s; a modified meeting-day scenario produced a reference roster with five staff-days of shortage. Independent monthly solving without history produced 16 staff-week cases of excess days off across two month-boundary weeks. This case demonstrates the practical value of optimisation-based decision support for staff rostering in municipal water utilities by showing how mathematical optimisation can be integrated into roster preparation and checking workflows with reduced preparation time.
Stable and effective restarting of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing partial eigenpairs of Hermitian matrices

We consider stable and effective restarts of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing the eigenpairs of a large Hermitian matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with the $n_{ev}$ eigenvalues in a given interval. Taking the CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR methods for instance, we prove that the commonly used restart scheme and its orthonormalized variant, named the natural restart schemes, are not numerically stable, thereby lowering attainable accuracy of approximate eigenpairs and missing some of the $n_{ev}$ desired eigenpairs. We prove the remarkable mathematical and numerical superiority of the combination restart over the natural restarts, then present a hybrid restart scheme that fully exploits the advantages of the natural restart and combination restart, and finally develop CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR algorithms with the hybrid restart. Numerical experiments confirm that the new algorithms are numerically backward stable to the working precision and more efficient than the CJ--SS--RRR algorithm with the natural restart. The combination restart and hybrid restart schemes can be straightforwardly extended to the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for general standard and generalized eigenvalue problems.
Sharp decay estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear equations in thin domains
John Fabricius; Niklas L. P. Lundström

We reduce the problem of establishing pointwise upper decay estimates in thin domains for viscosity subsolutions of fully nonlinear partial differential equations to solving a one-dimensional differential inequality. The resulting estimates make explicit the interaction between the transverse geometry of the domain and the ellipticity of the equation, and are shown to be sharp. Our framework allows the ellipticity to degenerate at infinity and accommodates nonhomogeneous equations with lower-order terms. As an application, we obtain decay estimates for $p$-subharmonic functions when $1<p\leq 2$
Learning Optimal Robust-Pathwise Control of Elliptic Equations with Random Coefficients
Qi Sun; Yanhan Cui; Ling Guo; Lili Ju

Conventional control approaches to optimization problems under uncertainty entail a practical compromise: deterministic controls offer robustness at the expense of pathwise accuracy while stochastic controls can adapt to individual realizations but suffer from the curse of dimensionality. To achieve both robustness and adaptivity, a neural operator-based approach is proposed in this paper for distributed elliptic optimal control problems with high-dimensional random inputs. A data-driven training algorithm is first established to learn the mapping from coefficient realizations directly to their optimal pathwise controls. To bypass the burden of generating training data pairs, a physics-informed training algorithm is then proposed and recast as weakly supervised learning using pseudo label targets produced by standard adjoint-based control updates. Numerical experiments with rough coefficients are conducted to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our robust-pathwise controls, which outperforms the benchmark robust deterministic control on unseen coefficient realizations owing to the generalization capability and fast inference of trained models.
Euler Cutting Planes for Fractional CVaR Programming
Pranay Seshadri; Hubert Dzieciol; Zhe Feng; Alan Tua

We maximise expected reward per unit of marginal tail risk, a reward-to-CVaR ratio against a baseline. The standard Dinkelbach route re-solves a Rockafellar--Uryasev LP or QP with one auxiliary variable per tail scenario at each multiplier update. Our method eliminates the multiplier iteration and keeps scenario auxiliaries out of the master, while still evaluating tail risk to generate cuts. A Charnes--Cooper/Schaible homogenisation removes the reward/risk multiplier, and the remaining convex constraint is separated on demand: each cut coefficient is an Euler allocation vector, read off a ranking and an average. The result is a single convex program, finitely terminating at the global optimum, with size independent of S --- an LP in $M{+}1$ variables, or a second-order cone program in $M{+}2$ for a concave quadratic numerator. The method runs 20--100 times faster than the exact Dinkelbach formulation and only needs single-digit cut counts.
Liouville theorems for stable solutions to the mean curvature equation

We study stable solutions of the mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-1}u $$ in domains of $\mathbb R^n$. We establish Liouville-type results in three settings. First, for globally stable solutions in $\mathbb R^n$, we prove that $u\equiv0$ if $1<p<p_{JL}$, where $p_{JL}$ is the Joseph--Lundgren exponent. Second, for solutions in $\mathbb R^n$ that are stable outside a compact set, we show that if $n>2$ and $p=p_S$, where $p_S$ is the Sobolev critical exponent, then $u\equiv0$. Third, for solutions of the Dirichlet problem on connected unbounded domains with smooth boundary satisfying an epigraph-type geometric condition, we prove that if $n>2$, $1<p\le p_S$, and the solution is stable outside a compact set, then $u\equiv0$. The proofs are based on a gradient estimate for stable solutions, an integrability result, conservation laws and Pohozaev-type identities, and a unique continuation argument. These results extend Liouville-type theorems for stable solutions from the semilinear Lane--Emden equation to the mean curvature equation.
Occupation Times at a Moving Interface and Sharp Yosida Rates for MacKean-Vlasov BSDE with Jumps and Fuzzy Selections
Kayembe Tshiswaka Tcheick; Mabela Matendo Rostin; Kabengele Mpunga Yannick; Bosonga Bofeki Jean-Pierre

We study a forward-backward McKean-Vlasov system with jumps whose backward equation contains a source obtained by evaluating the minimal-norm selection of a maximal monotone operator along the forward state. This selection changes branch across an interface that moves with the state law, the control, and an imprecisely known parameter described by fuzzy cuts. Assuming normal non-degeneracy and finite-statistics dependence of the interface on the law, we prove that the first and second moments of the time spent within a given distance of the interface are bounded, respectively, by a constant times that distance and by a constant times its square. The second-moment estimate makes it possible to integrate the source error before squaring it, which yields a Yosida error of first order in the regularization parameter in the natural solution norm; a first-moment argument gives only order one half. An explicit example shows that the first-order rate is sharp. For compact classes of admissible selections, the corresponding solutions form the cuts of a fuzzy solution set. These cuts are compact, stable with respect to the fuzzy level and the data, and approximated at the same first-order rate in Hausdorff distance. All estimates are uniform over a non-dominated family of probability measures representing volatility uncertainty. The quantitative results are obtained for separable quadratic potentials with finitely many affine branches.
Optimal Receive Design on the Observation Axis for RSMA Satellite-UAV Downlinks

A receiver can change its observation state while the physical signal remains the same. In rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlinks, this distinction separates receive-beam design and phase-reference transport from the motion of the satellite--UAV line of sight. We formulate receive optimization within the physical--observation dual-axis (PODA) structure and obtain three complementary results. For a known line-of-sight response and positive-definite receiver-noise covariance, a noise-weighted matched combiner simultaneously maximizes every decoding SINR and the minimum user rate. Under directional uncertainty, the principal eigenvector of the conditional response covariance globally maximizes mean array gain; for a Gaussian directional model, an equal-amplitude receiver is optimized by steering towards the conditional mean. Mean rate requires a different objective. We prove that the RSMA common-rate water level is jointly concave in the users' receive gains and derive a semidefinite relaxation with a computable global upper bound. A feasible rank-one beam can therefore be compared directly with the optimum of the finite-scenario problem. We also derive a precision-weighted linear predictor that suppresses uncertain physical-velocity estimates after observation-frame transport. Paired dynamic simulations reduce direction-cosine RMSE by 51.29\% relative to unrestricted nine-point extrapolation. In a separate uncertainty experiment, direct rate optimization increases mean minimum spectral efficiency from 0.32425 to 0.41712 bit/s/Hz, an improvement of 28.64\%; the corresponding design objective is within $2.28\times10^{-4}$ bit/s/Hz of a global upper bound. The phase-transport equation fixes a coherent representative of each optimal beam without changing its gain.
The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite algebras over perfect fields

Let $k$ be a perfect field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional representation-finite $k$-algebra. We prove that finite global dimension implies that the integral Cartan determinant of $A$ is one, extending Enomoto's result from algebraically closed fields to perfect fields.
Adam Blažek; Lubomíra Dvořáková; Edita Pelantová

The reflection complexity of a sequence, introduced recently by Allouche, Campbell, Li, Shallit, and Stipulanti, counts the factors of a given length up to reversal. We generalize this notion considering a group $G$ generated by antimorphisms over a given alphabet $\mathcal A$. The $G$-complexity of a sequence over $\mathcal A$ counts the factors of a given length up to the action of $G$. For $G$ generated by the reflection alone, the $G$-complexity coincides with the reflection complexity. We characterize eventual periodicity in terms of the $G$-complexity. Then we focus on the binary alphabet and the group $H$ generated by reflection and the antimorphism exchanging letters. We provide a simple formula for the $H$-complexity in the case of $H$-rich sequences and determine the precise values for complementary symmetric Rote sequences and generalized binary Thue-Morse sequences. Finally, we describe the aperiodic recurrent sequences having the minimum $H$-complexity -- they are exactly the complementary symmetric Rote sequences, while the binary sequences with the minimum reflection complexity correspond to the Sturmian sequences.
Examples of Bessel Functions of Order Zero Related to the Functional Equation of the Riemann Zeta Function

In 2010, M. A. Chaudhry et al. introduced a class of functions Sigma satisfying an L^1-condition. They proved that every function phi in Sigma gives rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. They also provided an example of a function outside Sigma for which the functional equation still holds. In this paper, we present several examples of Bessel functions of order zero that do not belong to Sigma but nevertheless give rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, we show that J_0(a sqrt(x)), J_0(ax), and Y_0(x) exhibit this phenomenon.
Dimension-independent eigenvalue approximation for sparse matrices
Natalia Hajlasz; Christopher Musco; Jonathan Weare; Robert J. Webber

Many applications in science and engineering require solving sparse Hermitian eigenvalue problems that are so large that even algorithms whose runtime scales linearly with the matrix dimension are unacceptably slow. Responding to this challenge, there is a growing body of work on sparsified iterative methods and submatrix selection methods that often perform well in practice. However, theoretical understanding of these methods is limited. In this paper, we take a step toward better understanding sublinear-time eigenvalue computation by analyzing the sparsified power method. We prove that the method approximates a leading eigenpair to a prescribed accuracy in a number of iterations comparable to the standard power method. The required number of retained nonzeros depends explicitly on the target accuracy, the initial overlap with the leading eigenvector, the compressibility of the leading eigenvector, and the relative spectral gap. When these quantities and the column sparsity are independent of dimension, the runtime is independent of dimension. In contrast, we show that a comparable worst-case guarantee cannot hold for a prototypical sparsified submatrix selection method. Submatrix selection is the approach of choice in many quantum chemistry applications. However, we show that, even with substantial initial eigenvector overlap, a single iteration of the method can produce a vector that is orthogonal to the leading eigenvector, after which the method cannot recover. Nevertheless, experiments on matrices from the SuiteSparse matrix collection and quantum chemistry problems illustrate the practical effectiveness of submatrix selection methods in a variety of domains despite these worst-case limitations.
Poisson contingency tables, Gibbs permutations, and entropic optimal transport
Danny Duan; Hanbaek Lyu; William Powell

We study random contingency tables obtained by conditioning a matrix of independent Poisson entries on its row and column sums. We identify such a table with the block counts of a random permutation drawn from a Gibbs measure of Mallows type, an exact coupling whose normalizing constants recover Barvinok's permanent identity. We use this correspondence to study the table at three scales. For finite dimensions, a transference principle compares the table with a matrix of independent Poisson entries whose means form the static Schrödinger bridge, the solution of a discrete entropic optimal transport problem. As the dimensions grow and the margins and prior means converge, the normalized histogram of the table converges to a limiting Schrödinger bridge at a quantitative rate. The fluctuations of the table around the bridge are characterized in two complementary ways. Linear statistics satisfy a central limit theorem for bounded test functions, with limiting variance equal to the squared $L^2$-distance, under the bridge, of the test function to the subspace of additively separable functions; as a process they converge to white noise with intensity given by the bridge, conditioned to have vanishing marginals. Spectrally, the limiting spectral distribution of the centered table is governed by a Dyson equation whose variance profile is the density of the bridge. The key ingredient is an asymptotic formula for the partition function of the Gibbs measure in terms of a Fredholm determinant given by the canonical correlations of the bridge. For Mallows-type random permutations, our results prove Pal's conjecture on the limiting partition function and Mukherjee's conjecture on the central limit theorem for linear statistics, both in greater generality.
Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
Gal Arnon; Andrej Bogdanov; Paul Lou; Giulio Malavolta; Alon Rosen; Lorenzo Taschin

We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with scattering damping
Elliot Adamson; Jason Metcalfe; Chengbo Wang

The focus of this article is to establish the existence portion of the Strauss conjecture for wave equations with spatially dependent scattering damping. In the current setting, the damping is not sufficiently strong to alter the critical Strauss exponent. In a subsequent study, the authors will consider the case of damping coefficients with critical decay where a shift of the Strauss exponent is expected. While several recent studies of the Strauss conjecture have relied upon weighted Strichartz estimates, here, instead, an approach that is based only on integrated local energy estimates, in particular those with both $r^p$ and ghost weights, is developed. This technique also applies to the problem for the free equation. Space-time Klainerman-Sobolev estimates provide the necessary decay to close the argument.
On trace-zero norm forms of orders of rational quaternion algebras with applications
Yifan Luo; Tianze Wang; Haigang Zhou

In this paper, by normalizing the trace-zero norm forms according to the parity of orders of definite rational quaternion algebras, we give an explicit formulation to the even Clifford correspondence followed by the reciprocity of ternary forms. We obtain an exact identity between ternary representation numbers and the number of elements of an order with prescribed reduced norm and trace, which applies to all orders without squarefreeness constraint on the reduced discriminant. Applications include a criterion for realizing ternary forms as trace-zero norm forms, a formula for traces of Brandt matrices in terms of representation numbers, and explicit theta series relations associated with local reciprocity. We also describe reciprocal orders and order chains, and interpret the ternary forms occurring in the congruent number problem through their associated quaternion orders.
The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with critical damping
Elliot Adamson; Jason Metcalfe; Chengbo Wang

The Strauss conjecture concerns wave equations with power-type nonlinearities and seeks the optimal range of powers that admit global solutions for all sufficiently nice and sufficiently small initial data. In three spatial dimensions, it is well known that small data global existence is available provided that the power $p>p_c(3)=1+\sqrt{2}$, where $p_c(n)$ denotes the critical power in $n$-spatial dimensions. In the current article, the analogous problem is considered for damped wave equations where the damping coefficient is at the critical scaling. When $a$ denotes the constant multiple applied to the damping term, it is shown that the corresponding critical power is $p_c(3+a)$ provided that $a$ is sufficiently small.
Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.
A new convergence proof for an iterative scheme for elliptic Cauchy problems based on alternating orthogonal projections
Abhijit Guchhait; Adrian Muntean; Martin Lind

We consider an elliptic Cauchy problem for the Poisson equation in which both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on a portion of the boundary, while no boundary conditions are available on the remaining part of the boundary. Such problems are severely ill-posed. In this work, we study the convergence of an iterative method based on the alternating imposition of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We formulate the scheme within a Hilbert space framework, where a yet another alternation becomes apparent: each iteration can now be interpreted as an orthogonal projection onto an appropriate closed subspace. This perspective provides a transparent geometric interpretation of the algorithm and yields a concise convergence proof based on von Neumann's classical result on alternating (orthogonal) projections. In addition to elucidating the convergence of the method, this alternating projections perspective also offers a general rate of convergence in terms of the Friedrichs angle (between two closed subspaces). We point out by means of an example that such convergence rate estimate degenerates for the elliptic Cauchy problem under consideration.
Products of Berezin Transforms on Generalized Fock Spaces

We study products $B_{α,m}^{(d)}B_{β,m}^{(d)}$ of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^d$. We establish a result for $m\neq2$: if $B_{α,m}^{(d)}B_{β,m}^{(d)}$ coincides with another such product, then the weight parameters of the second product must be $(α,β)$. As consequences, we characterize when two Berezin transforms commute and when the product of two Berezin transforms is again a Berezin transform.
Spectral-Edge Continuation, Dimensional Crossover, and Endpoint Stability for Partially Confined Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations

We study the global geometry and endpoint dynamics of positive solutions of $-Δu+|y|^2u+λu=g(u)$, $(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, $m=N-d$. Despite the loss of coercivity at $λ=-d$, we construct a connected component of centered positive solutions with frequency projection $(-d,\infty)$, assuming subcritical asymptotics of $g$ at zero and infinity, a zero-mass Liouville condition, and a strict Hamiltonian sign condition. At the lower edge, $λ+d\rightarrow 0^+$, anisotropic rescaling selects the lowest confined harmonic mode coupled to an $m$-dimensional scalar ground state. As $λ\rightarrow\infty$, isotropic blow-up yields the $N$-dimensional scalar ground state, revealing a dimensional crossover. The endpoint profiles and mass laws hold for every sequence of centered positive solutions, not merely along this component. The proof combines Gaussian--exponential localization on compact frequency strips, Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, compact spectral perturbation, and Leray--Schauder continuation. At both ends, we establish uniqueness and differentiability of the centered branch, identify the Morse indices and symmetry kernels of the real and imaginary linearizations in the full energy space, and derive sharp mass-slope asymptotics. Under standard Hamiltonian-flow hypotheses, the resulting slope criterion classifies orbital stability and instability away from the mass-critical powers. The mass map on this component, combined with endpoint control on the full centered solution set, yields existence, nonexistence, and multiplicity for normalized standing waves, revealing the roles of both critical exponents $2+4/m$ and $2+4/N$.
Orbit stratifications and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds with rank-one nonabelian symmetry

We study closed simply connected six-manifolds with positive sectional curvature and an effective isometric action of $SO(3)$ or $SU(2)$. Starting from Liu's corrected orbit-space analysis, we refine the stratification and recover smooth topology in several previously unresolved cases. For a boundaryless $SO(3)$ quotient, singular isotropy is connected, the weighted nonprincipal graph belongs to nine necessary families, and every action with only cyclic exceptional isotropy is classified equivariantly. The remaining branching families admit explicit rational intersection and Pontryagin formulas. For a three-ball $SO(3)$ quotient, the uniform-boundary configurations give sphere bundles over $S^4$ and a completely distinguished odd-integer family of non-spin six-manifolds. A doubled-quotient argument excludes the configuration with two boundary fixed points and an interior singular orbit, while the configuration with one fixed point and an exceptional interval has underlying manifold $\mathbb{CP}^3$. For a boundaryless $SU(2)$ quotient, an adjoint-weight matching argument reduces the exceptional three-orbit case to a unique action on the Eschenburg flag and identifies every two-orbit candidate with a weighted action on $S^2\times S^4$. These classifications imply rational ellipticity throughout the stated symmetry class. We also establish restricted curvature obstructions for the two diagonal product actions, without asserting nonexistence for arbitrary invariant metrics. Abstract graph restrictions, smooth realizability, and positive-curvature realizability are kept distinct. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.
Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing
Weidong Liu; Qingqing Jiang; Yufu Liu; Ruiqing He; Jiandong Shang; Hengliang Guo; Qiang Chen

Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions $χ$ and $2χ$. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by $25.20\times$ and $16.89\times$ for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.
Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link

Within the topological concordance class of the Hopf link, we construct infinitely many classes under the equivalence relation generated by smooth $0$-shake concordance. Each contains infinitely many smooth concordance classes represented by links that are pairwise strongly $0$-shake concordant and whose second components have unbounded smooth slice genus.
Sharp projection inequalities for antichains in cone orders

We establish sharp projection inequalities for $k$-antichains under orders defined by open convex cones. For integers $n\geq2$ and $k\ge 1$, let $C\subsetneq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open convex cone. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is a $k$-antichain with respect to the order $x\prec_C y\iff y-x\in C$ if it contains no chain $x^1\prec_C\cdots\prec_C x^{k+1}$. For every such set $A$ and every $v\in C$, we prove \[ \mathcal H^{n-1}(A) \leq k\frac{\|v\|}{α_C(v)} \mathcal H^{n-1}(P_v(A)), \] where $P_v$ is the orthogonal projection onto $v^\perp$, $\mathcal H^{n-1}$ denotes normalized Hausdorff outer measure, and $α_C(v)$ is the minimum of $\langleξ,v\rangle$ over unit vectors in the dual cone $C^*$. In particular, every weak antichain $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq\mathcal H^{n-1}(Δ_i(A))$ for each $i$, where $Δ_i(x)=(x_j-x_i)_{j\ne i}$. This proves the skewed projection conjecture of Engel, Mitsis, Pelekis and Reiher. As an application, we recover the bound $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq kn$ for $k$-antichains in the unit cube under the coordinatewise order.
Quantitative Stability and Sample Complexity for Regularized Gromov-Wasserstein Distance

The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance provides a principled framework for comparing two probability distributions supported on different metric spaces by matching their individual intrinsic geometric structures. In practice, the GW distance is estimated from finite samples and often incorporates regularization for statistical and computational tractability. This motivates a quantitative understanding of the stability and estimation error of regularized GW distances. In this work, we study a general family of divergence regularized GW distances, including entropy and Tsallis regularizations over the full range of powers, from a nonasymptotic perspective. Specifically, we establish Lipschitz continuity of the value of regularized GW and H{ö}lder continuity of its optimal coupling under Wasserstein perturbations of the input probability measures. Moreover, we derive the parametric rate of convergence for the empirical regularized (2,2)-GW distance on compactly supported Euclidean spaces.
A Safeguarded Accelerated Proximal ADMM Algorithm for Solving Structured Cardinality Penalized Optimization Problems
Wei Bian; Hongyuan Tao; Fan Wu

This paper considers a class of structured cardinality penalized optimization problems with nonsmooth convex loss functions, for which the proximal mapping associated with the structured $\ell_0$ penalty is generally unavailable. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a chain of exact reformulations based on variable splitting, exact penalization, and continuous relaxation, and establish rigorous equivalence relationships among these resulting models. In particular, we define a class of strong local minimizers for the original problem and show that these minimizers are equivalent to weak $d$-stationary points of the relaxation problem. Further, we propose a safeguarded accelerated proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (SAP-ADMM). We prove that the sequence generated by SAP-ADMM converges to a weak $d$-stationary point of the relaxation problem. Depending on the parameter settings and algorithmic regime, we establish $O(1/k)$ or $o(1/k)$ convergence rates for both the objective function value gap and the KKT residual. Numerical experiments on signal and image denoising demonstrate the effectiveness of both the proposed models and SAP-ADMM in terms of reconstruction quality and computational efficiency.
Global Well-Posedness and Persistence of H2 Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Primitive Equations with Horizontal and Topography-Adapted Thermal Diffusion

We study the three-dimensional primitive equations with full viscosity and horizontal thermal diffusion in bounded domains. We establish global well-posedness for admissible $H^1$ initial data and persistence of $H^2$ regularity on the flat-bottom cylinder. The higher regularity analysis combines fractional hydrostatic Stokes regularity with anisotropic estimates of the vertical transport. We also consider variable-depth domains with positive $h\in C^3(\overline M)$ and a diffusion operator adapted to the topography compatible with layers $z/h(x,y)=\mathrm{constant}$. This operator reduces to $Δ_H$ at constant depth and generally differs from the Cartesian horizontal Laplacian over a varying bottom. Its weighted formulation yields global strong solutions for admissible $H^1$ data. Persistence of $H^2$ regularity is proved under the additional assumption $\partial_νh=0$ on $\partial M$, where $ν$ is the outward horizontal unit normal.
Rigidity of Immersed Gauss Curvature Shrinkers in Euclidean Space

For every $m\geq2$, we prove that any connected closed oriented smooth immersion $X:M^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ satisfying \[ K=\left\langle X,ν\right\rangle \] is an embedding onto the unit sphere. No convexity is assumed. At a point maximizing $|X|$, we find a strictly convex component of $\{K>0\}$. If this component does not coincide with $M$, its polar immersion bounds an unbounded convex set. A finite area lemma then extends the local surface area formula for the polar body to a global measure identity. Using the vanishing first moment of surface area measure, we show that the origin lies in the interior of the polar body, contradicting the existence of recession directions. Thus the hypersurface is strictly convex, and the classification of strictly convex shrinkers completes the proof.
Order-preserving maps of the Turing degrees: regularity and consistency strength

We formulate a proof of Part~I of Martin's conjecture for order-preserving maps directly on the quotient of the reals by Turing equivalence. The assumptions are countable choice for reals, the perfect-set property for sets of reals, and continuous uniformization on a comeager domain. The argument applies under $\mathsf{AD}+\mathsf{DC}_{\R}$ and inside the choiceless Solovay model. We then determine the exact consistency strength of the unrestricted order-preserving dichotomy as an axiom over $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{AC}_ω(\R)$: it is equiconsistent with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ plus a strongly inaccessible cardinal.
Simultaneous Unimodularity of Positive Integer Matrices and Their Entrywise Cubes
Xinyi Li; Shuochen Wang; Zimeng Ye; Alexandru Zaharescu

We solve an open problem posed by Richard Guy in his book Unsolved Problems in Number Theory. We prove that, for every integer $n\geq10$, there exist infinitely many $n\times n$ integer matrices $A$ such that every entry is $\ge2$ and $\det A=\det A^{[3]}=1$, where $A^{[3]}$ denotes the entrywise cube of $A$. The matrices may be chosen compatibly, so they can form the leading principal blocks of a single infinite positive integer array. The order-ten case is reduced to an inhomogeneous system consisting of one linear and one diagonal cubic equation. The circle method then provides infinitely many positive integral solutions. To pass from order $n$ to order $n+1$, we introduce a bordering construction that preserves the signed cofactor vectors of both the matrix and its entrywise cube. Iterating this construction yields the result in every order $n\geq10$.
DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
Bohao Wang; Tianen Yuan; William Yen; Zehua Jiang; Chongwen Huang; Li Wei; Chen Zhu; Jiguang He; Hang Zou; Lina Bariah; Brahim Mefgouda; Anis Bara; Yongliang Shen; Zhaoyang Zhang; Merouane Debbah

Large-scale multimodal data are a key enabler for integrating large generative artificial intelligence models into wireless networks. However, existing wireless datasets offer limited support for heterogeneous environments, particularly in terms of reusable high-fidelity scenes, scalable differentiable ray tracing, and synchronized multimodal data. These limitations are more pronounced in mobile and aerial scenarios with time-varying environments and channels. To address these limitations, we propose DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for networks involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.
Multiplicity One and van Dijk's Conjecture for Connected Complex Symmetric Spaces

We prove regularity for symmetric pairs of connected complex reductive groups by combining invariant theory with the analysis of Schwartz distributions. For the classical residual families, a Gaussian lifting argument reduces the required equivariant vanishing to invariant theory in quadratic moment quotients: contraction and supertrace identities settle DIII and balanced CII, while Gram-matrix invariants and volume tensors handle BDI/Spin. In the exceptional EVII case, transverse slices and explicit radial differential operators establish the vanishing of the full sign-equivariant Schwartz-distribution space. Together with the reduction to irreducible factors and finite-component assembly, these results establish regularity for all symmetric pairs of connected complex reductive groups. We further establish multiplicity one for irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations whenever the complex symmetric space is connected, allowing disconnected ambient groups. In particular, van Dijk's unitary Gelfand conjecture follows in this setting. Finally, we construct an invariant tempered distribution supported on an EVII nilpotent orbit closure whose Fourier transform also has nilpotent support, showing that the EVII isotropy representation is not special.
Volker Diekert; Anna E. Frid; Silas Natterer; Alexander Thumm

Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).

Let $P = \sum_ω a_ωx^ω$ be a degree $d$ homogeneous polynomial in $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with real coefficients. Pólya showed that, if $P$ is strictly positive on the standard $n$-simplex, then $(x_0 + \cdots + x_n)^M P$ has strictly positive coefficients for all $M \gg 0$. The least such $M$ is known as the \emph{Pólya exponent} of $P$. de Klerk-Laurent-Parrilo showed that the Pólya exponent is $O(d^2) P^{(0)}_{\max}/λ(P)$, where $P^{(0)}_{\max} := \max_ωa_ω/\binom{d}ω$ and $λ(P)$ is the infimum of $P$ on the standard simplex. By applying known estimates of this approximation from probability theory, we obtain a different $O_n(d) L(P)/λ(P)$ upper bound of the Pólya exponent, where $L(P) := \max |a_ω|/\binom{d}ω$. An example shows that $O_n(d)$ is tight.

Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $α\mapsto E(α)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $α\mapsto E(α)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(α)$ for all $α\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $α\mapsto \dim_H(E(α))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $α$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.
Domain dependence of Sobolev-curl constants and structure of critical curl-curl solutions
Yong Liu; Jun Wang; Xuan Wang; Wen Yang

This paper investigates intrinsic critical Sobolev-curl constants on bounded domains and the structure of finite-energy solutions to the critical curl-curl equation in R^3. First, for 1< p < 3, we prove that the intrinsic critical p-curl constant on (0, a)\times D is bounded above by a^{p/3} times a Sobolev quotient on D. The proof uses an aligned test field whose optimal curl-free correction vanishes. Consequently, these constants tend to zero along thin convex boxes. For p = 2, we construct explicit convex and nonconvex domains with intrinsic constant below the sharp scalar Sobolev constant. The nonconvex example gives an affirmative answer to the domain-existence question in Problem 5 of Mederski and Szulkin(Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 241 (2021), 1815-1842), while the convex example disproves the lower bound stated there for convex domains. Concerning their Problem 2, we obtain an implicit Newtonian representation of finite-energy solutions and exclude two special forms of solutions. These structural results do not yet provide an explicit ground state or an unconditional ground-state decay rate as asked in Problem 2.
Consumption adjustment with mean-reverting risk premia: A singular stochastic control approach
Gugyum Ha; Junkee Jeon; Jehan Oh

We study a two-sided singular stochastic control problem in which changes in consumption carry utility costs and the risk premium follows the mean-reverting Kim-Omberg model. Optimal consumption is reflected between two moving barriers given by thresholds that depend on the current risk premium. These thresholds are the stopping boundaries of a Dynkin game for a two-dimensional diffusion driven by a single Brownian motion. A sharp occupation estimate shows that they are Lipschitz in logarithmic scale, uniformly in the cost of reducing consumption, and that smooth fit holds along the diffusion direction at every contact point. Outside a bounded interval of risk premia and at most two further points, the thresholds are infinitely differentiable. As the reduction cost grows, optimal consumption converges to the ratcheting policy.
UAV SAR Imaging via Diffusion Posterior Sampling under Non-Ideal Motion in ISAC Systems

Unmanned aerial vehicle-enabled synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers significant potential for providing communication services to ground users while sensing the surrounding environment in low-altitude integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. However, its practical deployment is challenged by known non-ULM trajectories and unknown position errors, which violate conventional SAR assumptions and cause severe image defocusing. Based on this formulation, we develop a diffusion posterior sampling (DPS)-based super-resolution SAR framework, where a pre-trained diffusion model provides a data-driven image prior and the exact physical model enforces measurement consistency during posterior inference. The inference process is further accelerated for practical implementation. For unknown position errors, we develop a joint iterative DPS and motion compensation (MoCo) optimization algorithm with discrete cosine transform reparameterization and coarse-to-fine spectral scheduling. Simulations demonstrate that our framework achieves high-accuracy reconstruction across diverse trajectories and remarkable super-resolution, maintaining greater than 21.3 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) even under half physical resolution truncation.
