Almost tight asymptotic enumeration of finite $p$-groups: Almost all finite groups are $2$-groups of class $2$

Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. We prove, uniformly over all primes $p$, that \[ \log_p f(p^m)=\frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac49m^2+O(m), \] with an absolute implied constant. This improves the classical upper bounds of Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965) and Newman--Seeley and matches Higman's lower bound (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) through the quadratic term. We also prove that \emph{the proportion of $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ among all groups of order at most $n$, counted up to isomorphism, tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$.} These results answer questions~22.3 and~22.19 of Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman (\emph{Enumeration of Finite Groups}, 2007). Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalization by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-Ω(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bläser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term. The same presentation estimates give fixed-quotient extension bounds which, together with Pyber's prescribed-Sylow theorem and the concentration result, establish domination by $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$.
Characterization of $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of small rank
C-Y. Jean Chan; Thomas Hagedorn; Joel Louwsma; Michael Wijaya

The $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a polynomial map is a quadratic enrichment of the classical Milnor number, defined as the local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree of the gradient. We study which elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms arise as $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers. Over fields of characteristic not $2$, $3$, or $5$, we show that every element of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $7$ that is a local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree is also an $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number. Unlike for local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees, however, in general not all $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers can be obtained from two-variable polynomials. Over an arbitrary field of characteristic not $2$, $3$, $5$, or $7$, we characterize the elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $8$ that are $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of two-variable polynomials. Over subfields of $\mathbb{R}$, this implies that there are local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees of ranks $4$, $6$, and $8$ that are not the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a two-variable polynomial. We also prove that under a mild hypothesis one can reduce the number of variables of a polynomial while preserving the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number up to multiplication by a unit.
A sharp bound for the least signless Laplacian eigenvalue of triangle-free graphs
Dongxiu Cai; Zhengbo Chen; Xiao-Dong Zhang

We prove that every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ on $n\geq1$ vertices satisfies $q_{\min}(G)\leq7n/50$, where $q_{\min}(G)$ is the least eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian matrix $Q_G=D_G+A_G$, with $D_G$ the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A_G$ the adjacency matrix. The constant is sharp, since the Higman--Sims graph and its balanced blow-ups attain equality, as shown by de Lima, Nikiforov and Oliveira (2016). This proves the bound conjectured by Balogh, Clemen, Lidický, Norin and Volec (2023). The proof uses five test column vectors associated with an ordered edge to obtain a matrix Rayleigh inequality. Our use of local Rayleigh inequalities together with flag-algebra semidefinite programming is inspired by Zhou (2026). We use semidefinite programming and rational approximation to find the required positive semidefinite matrices, and complete the proof by exact correction and verification.

We define a $d$-cube in a graph $G$ to be monophobic in $G$ if, whenever it supports a $d$-face of a discrete singular $d+1$-cube, it must also support another face. In many cases, the presence of such cubes implies the nontriviality of discrete cubical homology and homotopy groups associated with $G$. We describe several large classes of examples and characterize the property completely when $d=2$.
Copula Active Subspaces II: Error Decomposition, A Posteriori Estimation, and Sharpness of the Bounds
Joshua Chen; Peter Jan van Leeuwen

The Copula Active Subspaces (CAS) method of Part I estimates a non-Gaussian observation-noise density $π_{\boldsymbol{n}}$ from residual samples. Its KL divergence $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(π_{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\|\,\widehatπ_{\boldsymbol{n}})$ admits an exact decomposition into marginal, projection and reduced-density terms and bounds the posterior KL divergence averaged over the true predictive distribution. We derive a priori bounds for these terms, together with estimates or bounds from residual samples. Weighted nearest-neighbour entropy estimates are used for the marginal and reduced-density terms, with asymptotic standard errors in exact rank coordinates. For the projection error, the score is fitted on one subsample, and its mean squared magnitude outside the retained subspace is estimated on the other. Corrections for score and rank-transform errors then give a theoretical upper bound with probability at least $1-δ$. Tests on three known noise laws in dimension $d=20$ use the estimated rank transform. In $11$ of $12$ combinations of example and sample size, the sum of the two estimated terms and the trace bound exceeds the reference divergence after averaging over the estimated models. In these tests, score-estimation error is the largest contribution to looseness. The overestimate from the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality alone is at most a factor of $1.98$.
When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?

For a subset $A$ of a finite abelian group $G$, let $Σ_k(A)$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$, and let $Σ(A)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}Σ_k(A)$. The problem of determining when $Σ(A)=G$ goes back to Erdős and Heilbronn. Nguyen and Vu later formulated the corresponding fixed-length question: for a prescribed $k$, when does $Σ_k(A)=G$? For groups of odd order, we prove the sharp large-order threshold $|A|>|G|/3+1$, which forces $Σ_k(A)=G$ throughout the entire middle range $4\le k\le |A|-4$. This determines the limiting thresholds posed by Girard, Griffiths and Hamidoune. If $p$ is the least prime divisor of $|G|$, then, for fixed odd $p$ and sufficiently large $|G|$, the exact threshold $|A|\ge |G|/p+p-1$ forces covering throughout the middle range beginning at $2p-2$. Thus, throughout this range, prescribing the number of summands does not change the sharp covering threshold. For $3\le k\le2p-3$, the restricted and ordinary $k$-fold covering problems have the same asymptotic threshold. As an application to MDS elliptic codes on an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$, we sharpen the half-scale conjecture of Li, Wan and Zhang, obtaining the sharp $1/3$-scale bound when $|E(\F_q)|$ is odd and, more generally, the exact bound determined by the least prime divisor of $|E(\F_q)|$.
The canonical class and Chern character operators on Hilbert schemes of points

Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex surface. We obtain explicit formulas for the Chern character operators on the Hilbert schemes of points $X^{[n]}$ in terms of Nakajima operators, determining in particular the coefficients of the terms involving the canonical class $K_X$ and its square. Consequently, the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme is determined. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the action of the affine Yangian $Y_{t_1,t_2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$ on the cohomological Fock space $\mathbb{H}_X = \bigoplus_{n\geq 0} H^*(X^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})$.
Local Antimagic Chromatic Number of Middle Graph and Direct Product of Graphs
Huimin Xu; Gee-Choon Lau; Ruixue Zhang

An edge labeling of a connected graph $G=(V, E)$ is called a local antimagic labeling if it is a bijection $f: E\rightarrow \{1, 2, \cdots, \left | E \right | \}$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, $f^{+}(u)\neq f^{+}(v)$ where $f^{+}(x)=\sum f(e)$, with $e$ ranging over all the edges incident to $x$. The local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $χ_{la}(G)$, is the minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels across all possible local antimagic labelings of $G$. This paper investigates two families of graphs $G(m^{[n]})$ (a graph class constructed by augmenting a bipartite structure $B(m^{[n]})$ with cyclic edges) and $K_{1,s}\times C_n$ (the direct product of a star $K_{1,s}$ and a cycle $C_n$). Under the conditions odd integer $m\ge 1$ and even integer $n\ge 4$, we establish the exact values of $χ_{la}(G(m^{[n]}))$ and $χ_{la}(K_{1,s}\times C_n)$ for various $s$. Furthermore, we characterize several graph families achieving $χ_{la}(G)=2$ or $3$.
Localization of Lagrangian Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
Erkao Bao; Tyler Lawson; Cheuk Yu Mak

For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises

We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
Memory-Augmented Phase-Field Modeling: Onsager Formulation, Internal-Variable Lifting, and Structure-Preserving Computation
Peng Ding; Qingxia Liu; Zhiping Mao; Zhen Zhang

In this work, we develop a general memory-augmented phase-field (MAPF) framework based on Onsager's variational principle, in which memory effects are incorporated through a general relaxation kernel while preserving the thermodynamic consistency of the underlying system. Rather than treating fractional models as fundamental formulations, we show that they can be interpreted as reduced descriptions associated with specific power-law memory kernels. The proposed MAPF equations provide a unified modeling framework for non-Markovian phase-field dynamics. To facilitate analysis and computation, we further introduce an equivalent internal-variable representation that transforms the original nonlocal-in-time dynamics into an extended Markovian gradient system. This formulation preserves key structural properties, including energy dissipation and mass conservation, and enables the development of efficient structure-preserving numerical schemes. In particular, we construct an energy-stable scalar auxiliary variable approach combined with a fast rank-one implementation that exploits the relaxation-spectrum-induced coupling structure, resulting in a computationally efficient algorithm with reduced storage requirements. The proposed framework establishes a systematic connection between memory-dependent phase-field modeling, internal-variable thermodynamics, and structure-preserving numerical computation. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, stability, and efficiency of the proposed methods for phase-field dynamics with long-time memory effects.
Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO

We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.
The strong Ramanujan bound for Drinfeld modular forms

The Ramanujan bound states that the degree of the trace of the $\mathfrak{p}$-Hecke operator on a space of weight $k$ Drinfeld cusp forms is at most $d(k-2)/2$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is a prime of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$. We prove the strong Ramanujan bound, which states that at level 1, this bound can be improved to $d(k-(q+1))/2$. In addition, we classify when the strong Ramanujan bound is sharp; surprisingly, this turns out to depend on $\mathfrak{p}$ only through the parity of its degree. We also prove results related to the smallest slope of the Atkin operator and mod $p$ distributions of Frobenius polynomials of Drinfeld modules over finite fields.
Convergence of Least Squares Methods for PDEs on R^d with Shallow ReLU^k Networks
Tong Mao; Lei Shi; Hanfei Zhou

We establish inverse inequalities in Gaussian Sobolev norms for shallow $\mathrm{ReLU}^k$ trial spaces. The estimates identify the sharp regularity threshold and quantify the dependence on parameter separation and bias magnitude. Based on these estimates, we prove convergence of weighted least squares discretizations of linear PDEs on $\mathbb R^d$ using shallow networks with prescribed inner parameters and finitely many residual samples in an expanding ball. Under suitable stability and regularity assumptions, we obtain an error bound of order $h^{k+(d+1)/2-r}δ_\pm^{-(S-r)}$ in the Gaussian Sobolev norm of order $S$, up to logarithmic factors, where $r$ is the PDE order, $h$ is the parameter fill distance, and $δ_\pm$ is the antipodal separation. The convergence results cover deterministic and random sampling and extend to fixed bounded regions by restriction. We construct parameter sets with $δ_\pm\asymp h$, yielding a convergence rate in terms of the network width that matches a lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and provide practical guidance on balancing accuracy and stability.
Global existence and convergence of a density heat flow for strictly subcritical Liouville systems
Zetao Cheng; Haoyu Li; Woongbae Park; Lei Zhang

We study a density heat flow associated with normalized Liouville systems on a closed connected Riemannian surface, and we show that this flow leads to the existence of solutions for the corresponding subcritical Liouville systems. The coupling matrix is symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, with no invertibility, irreducibility or inverse-matrix sign assumption. Under the strict subcriticality conditions $8π\sum_{i\in J}ρ_i>\sum_{i,j\in J}a_{ij}ρ_iρ_j$ for every nonempty set of components $J$, every smooth positive initial density of masses $ρ_i>0$ generates a unique global smooth positive solution converging in every $C^m$ norm to a stationary density. The limiting potentials solve the stationary Liouville system. Our proof uses entropy coercivity and a gradient inequality in the density variables, which also yields algebraic or exponential convergence rates.
Signed Quantities and Quadrilaterals: Geometry without Cases

Ordinary angles and unsigned areas discard orientation, and much of the case analysis in plane geometry is the price of that loss. Signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas and directed distances) keep the signs and so let one argument serve for every configuration. We illustrate this with results that hold uniformly for convex, concave and crossed quadrilaterals: the diagonal area formula, an identity expressing one diagonal in terms of the sides and the other diagonal, a test for a pair of parallel sides, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals (such a quadrilateral has a pair of equal opposite sides if and only if it has a pair of parallel opposite sides), and a single ratio of directed distances that decides whether the vertices lie on an ellipse, only on hyperbolas, or on a circle.
On the generalization of Christol's theorem to domains of finite type over finite fields

We generalize Christol's theorem---which characterizes algebraic power series over a finite field in terms of automatic coefficient sequences---to completions of domains of finite type over a finite field~$\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Let $A$ be such a domain of dimension~$d$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of depth~$d$. In the $\mathfrak{a}$-adic completion $\hat{A}$, choose an $\hat{A}$-regular sequence $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{d}\}\subset\hat{\mathfrak{a}}$ and a set of representatives $E$ of $\hat{A}/(\boldsymbol{x})$ that is an $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-vector subspace consisting of algebraic elements. Every element $y\in\hat{A}$ then admits a unique expansion $y=\sum_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}a_{u}x^{u}$ with coefficients $a_{u}\in E$. We prove that $y$ is algebraic over $A$ if and only if the coefficient sequence $\{a_{u}\}_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}$ is $q$-automatic. The proof relies on a careful study of henselizations, which are shown to coincide with the algebraic closures inside the completions under certain conditions. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the automaticity of $β$-expansions for formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, answering questions posed by Hbaib--Mkaouar and Scheicher--Sirvent.
Symmetric two-level preconditioning for the method of reflections

We develop and analyze a symmetric two-level preconditioner for the method of reflections for Laplace problems in perforated domains. Using constant boundary modes, we define a coarse correction through a symmetric coercive dual formulation. Combining this coarse correction with parallel reflection corrections gives a symmetric positive definite preconditioner for solving the dual system by the conjugate gradient method. Under a geometric separation condition, we prove a condition number bound independent of the number and sizes of the holes and the diameter of the ambient domain. We also derive geometry-dependent convergence estimates for the one-level methods that explain the need for a coarse correction.
Compact localization and co-sobriety of Smyth power spaces

We establish a compact-localization theorem for finite iterates of the Smyth power space. Successive union maps assign to every finite-level Smyth object a canonical least compact saturated carrier in the original space, and co-sobriety at each positive finite level is equivalent to co-sobriety of the corresponding iterates over all compact saturated carriers. Consequently, if every compact saturated subspace of a $T_0$-space $X$ is stably compact---in particular, if every such subspace is Hausdorff---then $\PS^n(X)$ is co-sober for every finite $n\geq 1$. This applies to every $k_1$-Hausdorff space and hence to every Hausdorff or metrizable space. For the first iterate, we also give a direct full-Vietoris argument, independent of stable compactness, which shows that each $k$-irreducible compact saturated family is generated by its union.
Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight

We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $γ=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
Jiawei He; Zihan Zhang; Xiaoqiang Wang; Zhao Lin

Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.
Products of co-sober spaces need not be co-sober

We answer negatively the question whether the product of two co-sober spaces must be co-sober. For a nonempty closed subset $A$ of a $T_1$-space $(X,τ)$, we consider the topology consisting of the co-finite open sets together with the $τ$-open sets disjoint from $A$. We determine its $k$-irreducible compact subsets and derive a criterion that produces two compact co-sober spaces whose product contains a non-singleton $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of the diagonal. Applying the criterion to a specific Kovář--van Douwen space gives two countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober spaces whose product is not co-sober. A further construction yields a countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober space whose square is not co-sober. The failure of product closure also gives an alternative proof of the known non-reflectivity of co-sober spaces in the category of $T_0$-spaces.
Minimax Wasserstein Testing under Differential Privacy
Bonwoo Lee; Ilmun Kim; Cheolwoo Park

We study Wasserstein-$p$ goodness-of-fit and two-sample testing under differential privacy. For general compact metric spaces, we establish upper and lower bounds on the minimax separation radii in terms of covering numbers, matching up to logarithmic factors. On the hypercube $[0,1]^d$, these bounds match up to constant factors for two-sample testing in all dimensions and for goodness-of-fit testing whenever $d\neq 4p$, thereby closing logarithmic gaps in existing non-private results. At the critical case $(d,p)=(4,1)$, we further show that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable by establishing matching minimax bounds for non-private Wasserstein-$1$ goodness-of-fit testing under a bounded-density assumption. Finally, for unbounded domains, we establish minimax-optimal separation rates up to logarithmic factors under an exponential tail condition.

In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.
A framework for spanning forest identities

Identities of spanning forest polynomials can come from determinantal identities such as the classical Dodgson identity. They can also be useful in quantum field theory calculations, particularly the quadratic ones. To better understand the structure of spanning forest polynomial identities, we look at when identities on a given graph are generic for all graphs, we ask about dimensions of spaces of spanning forest identities indexed by certain parameters, and we set up a framework that we hope will be helpful for further progress in these directions. As part of this framework, we identify a family of maps naturally given by the all-minors matrix-tree theorem, and we show that their ranks are counted by the Narayana numbers via explicit construction of bases.
Flat and Ghost dimensions in tensor triangulated categories with a compact tilting generator

Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tensor triangulated category with a compact tilting generator $M$ and abelian heart $\mathcal{H}_M = M^{\bot_{\neq0}}$. We define a triangulated flat dimension $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X$ for $X\in\mathcal{T}$, and give criteria in terms of tensor vanishing and resolutions by the class of pure quotients of $\mathrm{Add}(M)$. We further introduce $M$-ghost length and $M$-ghost dimension, and show that the global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ controls the $M$-ghost length of all objects in $\mathcal{T}$, and that the $M$-ghost dimension of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the weak global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ and the supremum of $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X+\mathrm{inf}X$ of bounded objects, and the relative triangulated dimension of $\mathcal{T}^c$ with respect to $\mathrm{add}(M)$. This extends the classical Hovey-Lockridge theorem, which is recovered for derived categories of rings.
Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework

This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincaré-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.
A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
Pablo Cubides Kovacsics; Sebastián Uribe Rincón

Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $γ(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $Λ_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notinΛ_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}ω_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $ω_{i}$ in the ring $Λ_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.
Error Bounds and a Smoothing Penalty Method for Binary Orthogonal Optimization

Binary orthogonal optimization arises in semantic hashing, orthogonal binary projection, and Hadamard matrix design. Existing methods often handle binarity and orthogonality separately, so their outputs need not satisfy both constraints simultaneously and generally come without a residual-based guarantee of exact feasibility. Using an exact box-constrained reformulation, we establish local and global Lipschitz error bounds and prove that the Lipschitz exponent is optimal. In particular, when the binary orthogonal feasible set is nonempty, any box-constrained matrix whose orthogonality residual is below $1$ admits a feasible sign rounding, and the rounding distance is bounded by this residual. These bounds also yield a globally exact nonsmooth orthogonality-residual penalty over the box and a uniformly sharp local penalty threshold. We further develop a smoothing penalty method for binary orthogonal optimization (SPBO). We prove that every accumulation point is stationary for the limiting nonsmooth penalty problem. Numerical experiments on orthogonal binary projection, supervised hashing, and Hadamard completion show that SPBO substantially reduces orthogonality violations while retaining competitive objective values or retrieval accuracy.
Prior-Informed Generalizable Low-Rank Representation Learning via Regularized Adversarial Reweighting
Keyao Zhan; Junwei Lu; Tianxi Cai

Modern learning problems increasingly leverage data from heterogeneous sources to improve robustness and generalizability under distribution shift, often with high-dimensional parameters admitting low-rank structure. Existing group distributionally robust optimization (group-DRO) approaches optimize against adverse source mixtures, but extending this principle to low-rank matrix estimation with a broad class of losses leads to a challenging nonconvex-concave problem for which methods and theory remain limited. We propose Prior-Informed generalizable Low-rank representation Learning via Adversarial Reweighting (PILLAR), which smooths the group-DRO objective by regularizing adversarial source weights toward a user-specified reference distribution while learning a shared low-rank representation. By tempering extreme adversarial reweighting, PILLAR improves estimation stability and reduces the potential conservativeness of group-DRO. Using Burer-Monteiro factorization, we optimize the nonconvex-concave objective by bifactored gradient descent with mirror ascent. We establish linear convergence to a statistical neighborhood of the population saddle point and derive an error bound that separates low-rank estimation from adversarial reweighting. We further show that PILLAR improves on vanilla group DRO when the latter's excess conservativeness dominates source heterogeneity and prior misspecification. Simulations and an electronic health record study of suicide-attempt risk demonstrate improved worst-source and transported predictive accuracy.
Persistence of conormal analyticity for the Euler equations in the half-space
Benjamin Ingimarson; Igor Kukavica; Marco Sammartino

We prove the persistence of conormal analyticity through the $H^r$ norm, with $r \geq 4$, for the 3D incompressible Euler equations in the half-space $Ω= \mathbb{R}_+^3$. We also establish a lower bound on the radius of conormal analyticity which depends on $\|u\|_{H^r}$ and initial data. In particular, persistence is established in both of the spaces $X_τ^{\rm co}$ and $A_τ^{\rm co}$, the former being based on the conormal operator $Z_k = ϕ^k \partial_3^k$ and the latter being based on $L^k = (ϕ\partial_3)^k$. Finally, we show that the norms $\|\cdot \|_{X_τ^{\rm co}}$ and $\|\cdot \|_{A_τ^{\rm co}}$ are equivalent up to a small loss in radius, the proof of which uses explicit identities relating the two conormal operators.
Harmonic numbers and Lerch functions behind falling factorial generating functions
Hemen Dutta; Gradimir V. Milovanovic; Yilmaz Simsek

We study a family of special numbers and polynomials introduced by Simsek whose exponential generating function has as denominator a falling factorial in the exponential variable. Using the partial fraction decomposition of this denominator, each member of the family is expressed by a single finite sum involving Bernoulli polynomials, Apostol Bernoulli polynomials and two variable Fubini polynomials evaluated at reciprocals of integers. We consider the future of mathematics as a profession in a world where artificial intelligence may surpass human mathematicians in essentially every technical task. Through an informal dialogue, we explore why human mathematical expertise might nevertheless remain valuable, what kinds of expertise universities should cultivate, and how graduate education might adapt. We also discuss the institutional and economic uncertainties that threaten the continued existence of a thriving mathematical profession, even if the value of human mathematical understanding endures.
Juncheng Wei; Zetian Yan; Zikai Ye

In both cases, the Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. The even case resolves a conjecture of Dolbeault (2021).

We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. This allows us to obtain Hölder regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. We construct a random walk that jumps between neighboring cells of the optimal partition and use it to describe how the matching cost responds to changes in the sample. Estimates for this walk control the effect of replacing one sample point and the interaction between two replacements. These bounds yield the variance estimates and allow us to apply a martingale central limit theorem.

For quasi-metric spaces, taken $T_1$ throughout ($d(x,y) = 0$ implies $x = y$), this fails: Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether bijectivity restores rigidity; a recent example, the toll spiral, shows that it does not. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity cannot be dropped: a compact, hereditarily precompact quasi-metric on the natural numbers makes the shift non-contractive and not an isometry. Under $R_0$ the two-sided case reduces to the metric theorem, both topologies being sequentially compact exactly when the symmetrized distance is compact; the one-sided theorems do not reduce to it, and plasticity does not pass to the symmetrization even for compact spaces. This paper treats a system that performs back-to-back tasks. Each new task has a random matrix of parameters and can be processed in various processing modes. The processing mode determines the task duration and a vector of rewards (penalties are viewed as negative rewards). The reward vector can include quality, profit, or $-1$ times a penalty such as cost or energy. In wireless applications, tasks correspond to data transmissions and rewards/penalties correspond to throughput and distortion. Prior work treats the problem of maximizing the time average of a reward process subject to constraints. This paper seeks to maximize a concave function of the time average reward vector. This is difficult because it involves a multi-variable function of ratios of averages. We develop a single algorithm that does not know the probability distribution of the random task matrices. The algorithm is adaptive, meaning it responds efficiently (with optimal adaptation time) when probabilities change.

Optimization can be expensive when evaluating the objective and its gradient requires a large dataset or a costly simulation. A cheaper approximation (i.e., a surrogate) can provide a useful initial point, but the work spent on that surrogate must be justified by the saving on the original problem. We study how many iterations to perform on each surrogate before switching to a more accurate objective. For a given sequence of smooth, strongly convex objectives, we use convergence bounds and distances between minimizers to construct a model of the total iteration cost. We derive closed-form two-level budgets for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and a convex reformulation for multiple levels. We also develop an online switching rule that updates the cost comparison using the gradient at the current point. We test the techniques on a logistic-regression problem using HIGGS data. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $δ(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $Δ(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. Instead of prescribing the boundary values and imposing a junction condition, we compute the solution on each branch from its outer vertex toward the junction and determine the boundary values for which these branchwise solutions agree at the junction. Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications

Let $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.
Explicit Solutions in a Probabilistic Cellular Automaton Model for Self-Assembled Monolayer Degradation
Wes Caldwell; Ryan Evans; Jacob Majikes; Anthony Kearsley

Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), formed by the adsorption of a monomolecular layer of adsorbate onto a surface, have emerged as leading candidates for plat- forms for electrochemical biosensors. In order to characterize the working age of a SAM-based biosensor, it is necessary to understand the long-term degradation of the monolayer, with particular emphasis on the intermolecular forces present in the self-assembly process. In this work, discrete- and continuous-time proba- bilistic cellular automaton (PCA) models for the degradation of SAMs involving adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are proposed in which adsorbate molecules desorb at a rate dependent only on the number of adsorbed neighbors. Impor- tantly, we make no assumptions on the relationship between degradation rate and adsorbed neighbors. Using techniques from generating function theory and complex analysis, the expected degradation curve is solved for explicitly in one dimension and shown to be a sigmoid curve related to the Gompertz function.
A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)

The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by Gł{\k a}b and Prus-Wiśniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irréductibles de dénominateur $n$ ou de dénominateur au plus égal à $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{ϕ(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $ϕ$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. Eva Bayer-Fluckiger; Stevell Muller; Matthias Schütt
We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperkähler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $Δ$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(Δ-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole. This article presents an introductory study of $p$-differential forms in spinor variables defined on the Minkowskian (or Lorentzian) manifold. Starting from the algebraic and geometric foundations of spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, we establish the correspondence between Minkowski spacetime and Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates. Within this framework, we construct differential 1-forms and 2-forms expressed in spinor notation, and formulate the Dirac operator in terms of exterior calculus. A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane.
