The results extend to noise without finite support, to backward passes on a sample average approximation, and to stationary and periodic infinite-horizon SDDP with geometric pass lengths.
Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings

We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.
Pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products

We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise Hölder continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise Hölder continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.
Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
Zeru Zhu; Marco Gamarra; Ji Liu

This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.
Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields

This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(nφ)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.
Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three

We prove that every finite ordered set of width at most three and cardinality at least four is reconstructible from its deck. This settles the width-three part of an open problem posed by Schröder in Ordered Sets; the separate question concerning ordered sets of height one is not addressed here. The new ingredient is a criterion for recovering the marked maximal deck of an ordered set with exactly three maximal elements from its unmarked maximal deck and the isomorphism type of the suborder obtained by deleting all maximal elements. We express the criterion as an orbital balance condition on the attachment ideals in this common base. Necessity follows by double counting; sufficiency uses the structure of automorphism actions in width at most three. The full-deck theorem then follows from reconstruction results of Schröder concerning maximal cards and marked maximal cards. A local reattachment argument correcting one intermediate step in the two-maximal-element case is included in an appendix.
An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
Averkios Averkiou; Manuel del Pino; Monica Musso

We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.
Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
Daniel Álvarez; Andrew Clarke; Eduardo González

Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wiśniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.
A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations

The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.
The square function estimate for the cone in four dimensions

We obtain the $L^3$ reverse square function estimate for the light cone in four dimensions from the critical local-smoothing and round-cone propagation statements in the September 2026 OpenAI manuscript. We state these inputs, together with the plate maximal theorem of Di Plinio and Parissis, in a preliminaries section. The proof passes from geometric concentration of packet coefficients to regularity of the analyzed wave, and then from free waves to arbitrary functions supported near the cone. As a consequence, we obtain the corresponding $L^3$ estimate for the sphere and elliptic paraboloids in three dimensions.
Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent

We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.
Steven V Sam; Keller VandeBogert; Jerzy Weyman

In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincaré series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gröbner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.
Could four-dimensional $ϕ^4$ theory exist beyond the usual triviality arguments?

Do lattice triviality, suspected Borel non-summability and the perturbative Landau pole exclude an interacting four-dimensional theory satisfying the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms and reproducing every renormalized coefficient of positive-coupling $O(N)$ $ϕ^4$ theory? An example involving one real function separates vanishing cutoff limits along its allowed bare trajectories from a nonzero result obtained by renormalizing the coefficients first; an exponentially small correction preserves its expansion and removes the pole in its running coupling. For the massless two-point expansion of the singlet composite $Φ_aΦ_a$ at leading order in $1/N$, ordinary Borel summation fails even for Gaussian smearing. The arithmetic mean of two Borel integrals along opposite imaginary rays defines a real distribution on every four-dimensional Schwartz momentum or position test, with finite-order remainder bounds uniform on bounded test sets. Two alternative covariances with nonnegative mass spectral weights remove the Euclidean pole and construct generalized free fields. After a fixed contact subtraction, their Euclidean extensions preserve every coefficient of the collective correlations obtained by Wick pairing. The interacting finite-$N$ family remains open. We also state a conditional interacting route through the physical scalar correlations of a larger theory (the parent) with heavy particles. A concrete $N=1$ gauge--Higgs--fermion candidate has a tuned one-loop trajectory on which all interaction couplings tend to zero in the ultraviolet, and a stable tree vacuum with additional masses comparable to the heavy scale. Constructing the parent and its corrected ultraviolet trajectory, and proving coefficient decoupling and the exact remainder bounds as the quartic coupling tends to zero and the family's heavy masses grow, remain open.
On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming

The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.
Stochastic Modelling of Telomere Length Dynamics During Hematopoiesis
Sophie Baland; Simon Toupance; Denis Villemonais

We introduce a new stochastic model of telomere length dynamics during hematopoiesis. The numerous cell divisions occurring in this setting makes telomere length dynamics, and in particular their attrition, a crucial aspect of hematopoiesis. After recalling the main aspect of the biological setting, we describe an individual based model of hematopoietic population cells. We then study its behaviour in the large population limit, as well as its fluctuations.
Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
Nhat Trung Nguyen; Ivan Dorofeev; Irina Podlipnova; Yuriy Dorn; Alexander Gasnikov

We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.
Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis

The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a one-time symbolic phase, the runtime bus-type projection overhead is entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The framework is realized in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 24.4-30.1x faster than the MATPOWER- style baseline and 6.0-7.8x faster than the Schafer-Braun optimized assembly. End-to-end, the grid-level solve time is 11.7x-154.3x faster than pandapower 3.5.4 with Numba, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. Compared with the native C++ LightSim2Grid 1.0.0, grid-level performance is comparable on IEEE 39 and 1.3x-1.8x faster on IEEE 118 and the PEGASE systems. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.
Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
Michael Borinsky; Jury Radkovski; Suriyah Rajalingam Kannagi

A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in $D=2$ and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the $β$-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.
Median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for nested integration
Arved Bartuska; Yang Liu; Raúl Tempone

Nested integrals $\int f\left(\int g(\boldsymbol{y},\boldsymbol{x})\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{x}\right)\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{y}$ where $\boldsymbol{y}\in[0,1]^{d_1}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\in[0,1]^{d_2}$ frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate $α+3/2-ε$ for any $ε>0$ can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where $α\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.
Optimal Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities under different relaxations of bounded variance assumption
Kirill Novoselov; Yuriy Dorn; Darina Dvinskikh; Alexander Gasnikov

We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with $m$ workers, $K$ oracle calls per worker per round, and $N$ rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from $(KN)^{-1/2}$ to $(KN)^{-1}$ with local steps and from $(mKN)^{-1/2}$ to $(mKN)^{-1}$ with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in $m$. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over $KN$ sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all $mKN$ samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an $N^{-2}$ gradient term, a $(KN)^{-1}$ monotone term, and a $(mKN)^{-1}$ sampling term, without assuming SGC.
Frugal coloring in planar graphs with maximum degree 4 and 5
Boštjan Brešar; Přemysl Holub; Marko Jakovac; Petra Melicharová

A proper coloring of vertices of a graph $G$ is called $t$-frugal if no color appears more than $t$ times in the neighborhood of any vertex of $G$. While $1$-frugal coloring coincides with $2$-distance coloring, we study $2$-frugal colorings of planar graphs with maximum degree $4$ and $5$, respectively. We prove that every planar graph with maximum degree $4$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $7$ colors, while a planar graph with maximum degree $5$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $10$ colors. The results present variations of parts of the famous Wegner's conjecture, which for planar graphs with maximum degree $Δ\in\{4,\ldots,7\}$ states that their $2$-distance chromatic number is at most $Δ+5$.
The first homology of square-section braid groups
Minh Pham; Nicholas Wawrykow; Jacob Zweiback

We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.
Equality Cases in the Tu-Deng Conjecture Bound

The Tu-Deng Conjecture, made in 2011, asserts that for $k\geq2$ and $1\leq t<2^k-1$, the set \[ S_{t,k}=\left\{(a,b)\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^k-2\}^2: a+b\equiv t\pmod{2^k-1},\quad \wt(a)+\wt(b)<k\right\} \] satisfies \[ |S_{t,k}|\leq 2^{k-1}. \] Proofs of the conjecture were given independently by the author and by Liu, Luo and Xie in arXiv in 2026. Let $r=\wt(t)$, and let $z=k-r$ be the number of zeros in the $k$-bit expansion of $t$. We prove that equality holds in the Tu-Deng Conjecture if and only if every cyclic distance between consecutive zeros is at least $z$. We give several other simple necessary and sufficient conditions, including a forbidden-pattern condition, a packing condition for the zero positions, a composition condition for the gaps, and equivalent conditions involving the coefficients of the polynomial $H_W(u,v)$ in the proof of the Tu-Deng conjecture. We also count the equality words having a prescribed number of zeros.
Pointed Gromov-Hausdorff Distance between $l^p$-Wedge Sums and Isometric Embeddings of $l^\infty$

The paper studies $l^p$-wedge sums of metric spaces and provides a two-sided estimate for the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff distance between them. Using an upper bound for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, the existence of an isometric embedding of $l^\infty$ into the Gromov-Hausdorff space of all non-empty metric spaces is proved.
Removing Boundary Smoothness from the Hot-Spots Conclusion in the Simple-Eigenvalue Case

We give a reduction from a smooth-domain theorem excluding interior critical points of first positive Neumann eigenfunctions to a non-strict hot-spots conclusion on arbitrary bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple first positive eigenvalue. The main analytic step is spectral convergence under exhaustion by conformal images of concentric disks. A reflection extension, conformal invariance of Dirichlet energy, and compactness of the Sobolev embedding give a direct proof. A truncation argument justifies square integrability of the transferred extensions without any boundary regularity. The smooth-domain theorem proved by OpenAI is an external input; the approximation argument is proved here in full. The paper was generated by ChatGPT with prompts from the listed author.
A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
Nihar Gargava; Matthias Gröbner; Michael Simkin

For a positive integer $d$, let $Δ_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $Δ_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.
Mesh-Native Tokenisation: Retrofitting Foundation Models to Unstructured Data
Georg Maierhofer; Miles Cranmer; Payel Mukhopadhyay

Physics foundation models are an increasingly popular approach for building versatile emulators for spatiotemporal systems. They require tokenisation layers that lift physical field data into a latent representation suitable for dynamic processing. A typical choice for this layer is a convolutional encoder, which lifts field information in a locality-aware way and can be trained very efficiently. However, this choice cannot be applied to a large class of scientific computing problems where data are represented on unstructured meshes, for example simulations on domains with curved boundaries. Such data typically require graph neural network architectures, which are more expensive to train and, in the form currently used, encode information differently from their CNN counterparts, thus limiting the portability of physics emulators between these data regimes. In this work we introduce Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC), a locality-aware tokenisation layer that encodes unstructured mesh-based data in a way that is analogous to CNNs. This approach leads to models that can be trained once on mesh data and then deployed to arbitrary unstructured meshes, even if these are irregular, with minimal retraining. We show that this tokenisation approach can be used to retrofit grid-pretrained foundation models efficiently on unstructured meshes and provide theoretical results to confirm the consistency of this approach with classical CNN encoders. We demonstrate the favourable performance of this retrofitting approach, which in many cases reaches acceptable accuracy even in zero-shot deployment, and outperforms existing baselines after only a few epochs of fine-tuning, thus providing an efficient bridge between the two data regimes.
Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs

The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $π$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |π(u) - π(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.

We completely resolve Question~5.3 of Kania's paper \cite{Kania} and establish a more general realization theorem. We show that for infinite cardinals $μ\leqslantν<κ<λ$, a space with \[ \pc(X)=μ,\qquad\pcl(X)=ν,\qquad \pcc(X)=κ,\qquad\pcd(X)=λ\] exists if and only if $κ\leqslant2^μ$. The witnesses may be zero-dimensional and Tychonoff spaces, of the least possible cardinality $λ$. They may have the least possible number of non-isolated points, or alternatively be crowded. The main ingredient is an exact computation of the centered local $π$-character of star filter spaces in terms of ultrafilter character, obtained from a finite selection lemma for filter pushforwards. We also construct a single space with countable $r$-linked local $π$-bases for every finite $r$, centered value $ω_1$, and any prescribed decreasing value greater than $ω_1$.
Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
William Chen; Lior Silberman; Ury Segal; Chen Greif

We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.
Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety

We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta-Iovita-Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard-Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao-Liu.

We prove that a tubular group is linear if and only if it is residually finite, equivalently virtually primitive. Every such group embeds in $\SL_n(\Z[u])$. For a primitive tubular decomposition with at most $m$ edge slopes at each vertex, our representation has dimension $2\max\{2,m\}$. In particular, Gersten's group embeds in $\SL_6(\Z[u])$, and this dimension is minimal.
Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles

Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_δ$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.
Global obstruction property and its applications

We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite. For each Artin algebra $A$, we construct an algebra $\mathcal{G}(A)$ satisfying GOP by using triangular matrix extensions. We show that $\text{fin.dim}\mathcal{G}(A)=\text{fin.dim} A+2$ and that $A$ and $\mathcal{G}(A)$ are singularly equivalent. Finally, we give a pair of derived equivalent finite-dimensional algebras for which GOP holds on only one side.
A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem

In this note we show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. Combined with an announced result of Auroux, Bai and Pomerleano, this shows that for some $4 \le n \le 8$ there is a complex affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative.

We prove that every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph which is quasi-isometric to a graph excluding a countable clique as a minor is quasi-isometric to a planar graph. Consequently, every finitely generated group with such a quasi-isometry is virtually planar, meaning that some finite-index subgroup admits a planar Cayley graph. We also show that a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph admitting a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding some finite minor admits a regular map into a bounded-degree planar graph. If the source is accessible, the target need only exclude a countable clique. Combined with work of Mackay, Spriano, and the present author, this shows that a finitely presented group admits a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding a countable clique if and only if it is virtually planar.
A higher-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate along families of bi-Lipschitz curves

Let $Θ\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 1$ be compact with upper Minkowski dimension $β$, and let $γ(x,t,θ)$ be a family of curves which is bi-Lipschitz in the first variable and Lipschitz in the last two. We prove the maximal estimate $$\left\|\sup_{(τ,θ)\in[0,1)\timesΘ}\left|e^{iτΔ}f(γ(\,\cdot\,,τ,θ))\right|\right\|_{L^2(B^n_1)}\lesssim_s\|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb{R}^n)},$$ for every $s>\tfrac{n(β+1)}{2(n+1)}$, in the range $0\leβ\le n-1$. In the range $n-1<β\leq n$ we prove the threshold $s>\min\big\lbrace\fracβ2 + \frac 1{2(n+1)},\frac n2\big\rbrace$. The proof relies on a fractal $L^2$ estimate of Du--Zhang. We also use the temporal localization of Lee, the locally constant property, and a counting argument allowed by the Lipschitz properties of the curve.
Triality rotation of connections and Dirac operators on SU(3)

We show how triality, the symmetry permuting the three 8-dimensional representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$, can also appear as a symmetry of geometric objects such as connections and Dirac operators. Take any Riemannian metric $g$ on the manifold $M = \mathrm{SU}(3)$ and let $
abla$ be a metric connection on $TM$. Using an explicit model of Clifford multiplication by deformed Okubo products, we combine spinorial lifts with isometries $TM \simeq S^+ \simeq S^-$ to show that $
abla$ can be rotated into two new metric connections on $TM$. So there is a canonical $\mathbb{Z}_3$-orbit of metric connections determined by $(g, 
abla)$, with no other choices. The three connections coincide when $g$ is bi-invariant and $
abla$ belongs to the Cartan-Schouten line, but in general they are different. The rotations of $
abla$ preserve the norm of the curvature, so they define a new $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetry of the moduli space of Yang-Mills connections on $TM$. They also preserve the Chern-Simons 3-form and adjoint Yang-Mills-Higgs functionals. After choosing an orientation on $M$, the rotated connections define three self-adjoint, Dirac-type operators on the spinor bundle. We prove that these operators are natural, in the sense that they commute with the Kosmann derivatives of spinors along all invariant Killing vector fields that preserve $
abla$. We also show that they are not isospectral, in general. This is verified by computing the simplest eigenvalue for the Levi-Civita connection and observing that it splits among the three operators as the bi-invariant metric on $M$ is deformed to one with isometry group $(\mathrm{SU}(3) 	imes \mathrm{SU}(2) 	imes \mathrm{U}(1)) / \mathbb{Z}_6$. Finally, we outline how the constructions in the paper may extend to general 8-manifolds with a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)$-structure.
Transformer-Based Masked Diffusion Models Provably Learn Distributions with Latent Structure

Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate discrete data by iteratively unmasking multiple tokens in parallel using a learned mask predictor. Their output carries two errors: parallelization error due to parallel sampling, and estimation error from the mask predictor learned with finite samples. Existing theory treats these errors separately, and the available statistical bounds typically scale with the number $V^L$ of length-$L$ sequences over a vocabulary of size $V$, suffering from the curse of dimensionality. In this work, we establish end-to-end statistical guarantees showing that transformer-based MDMs learn structured distributions with a sample complexity governed by their latent structure. Specifically, we model this structure through mixtures of hidden Markov trees, which capture latent dependencies within components and heterogeneity across components. When the data distribution is well approximated by such a mixture, a transformer-based MDM with parallel unmasking schedules achieves $\varepsilon$-accurate sampling in KL divergence with $\widetilde{O}(LK_{\mathrm{par}}/\varepsilon)$ training samples, where $K_{\mathrm{par}}$ is polynomial in $L$, $V$, the number of hidden states, and the number of mixture components. The transformer network and sampling procedure require no knowledge of the tree topologies or component parameters, thereby adapting to the unknown latent structure automatically. Overall, our results provide theoretical justification for the empirical effectiveness of MDMs on real-world data.
We prove asymptotic formulas for the number of $m$-full ideals of bounded norm in a given ideal class and for the number of $m$-full algebraic integers of bounded Weil height.
Quaternion Gaussian Probes for Tensor Frobenius-Norm Estimation
Yannan Chen; Hailin Sun; Min Xi

Large-scale tensors arising in science and engineering are often too large to form or store explicitly. Their multilinear contractions, however, can frequently be evaluated efficiently, which makes randomized Frobenius-norm estimation a practical alternative to exact computation. In this paper, we study estimation of the squared Frobenius norm of a real order-$d$ tensor from such contractions using independent real, complex, or quaternion Gaussian probes. For a rank-one tensor, one normalized sample is a product of $d-1$ independent Gamma variables. This gives exact relative-variance factors $3^{d-1}-1$, $2^{d-1}-1$, and $(3/2)^{d-1}-1$, respectively. Under the same budget of underlying real Gaussian vectors, the quaternion probe has smaller rank-one variance than four independent real probes for $d\ge3$; a real-channel representation identifies the gain as modewise pooling. For orthogonal CP tensors, the exact relative variance equals the corresponding rank-one factor divided by the participation-ratio effective rank and the number of samples. For arbitrary real tensors, we prove sharp uniform moment bounds, attained at rank one, and obtain Chebyshev guarantees. A classical block-median construction then gives two-sided exponential confidence for the modified estimator. Numerical examples test the rank-one and effective-rank formulas. An implicit infinite-series kernel tensor illustrates contraction-based norm evaluation; EEG maps provide a qualitative spatial interpolation illustration.
Lusztig Parameters and Factorizations of Determinantial Modules

We give an explicit formula for the Lusztig parameters of determinantial modules over symmetric quiver Hecke algebras. The formula applies to every Bruhat pair and every fixed reduced expression of the upper Weyl group element. In finite types $A$, $D$, and $E$, we identify the parameters of the modules in Ménard's seed using Demazure weaves. We then factor prefix determinantial modules into these seed modules, with multiplicities given by Lusztig cycles. We also give a criterion for recognizing monomials in this fixed seed and an explicit formula recovering their multiplicities from Lusztig parameters.
Fix What's Wrong, Keep What's Right: Hallucination Repair for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
Jiageng Wu; Chao Shen; Zihan Guo; Junyan Shao; Zongyan Zhang; Jie Song; Zhong Li; Mingyang Sun

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored to automate operations research modeling, reduce modeling time and lower the expertise barrier to optimization based decision support. However, this process often introduces inconsistencies between generated artifacts and the original problem, which we refer to as optimization modeling hallucinations. Despite progress in general-purpose hallucination mitigation, optimization modeling poses a distinct repair challenge: restoring fidelity to the original problem through coordinated model-code updates. We introduce OPT-Kraken, a training-free hallucination repair framework. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first post-hoc framework for repairing hallucinations in LLM-based optimization modeling artifacts. It extracts problem requirements and instance data, localizes errors by checking problem-model fidelity, model-code consistency, and data grounding, and selects repair granularity by the affected scope. For local repair, category rules and instance evidence are compiled into contracts specifying permitted edits, expected effects, and protected content. Experiments on established optimization modeling benchmarks show positive gains across automatic modeling frameworks and fine-tuned models. On zero-shot artifacts from multiple base models, OPT-Kraken effectively repairs optimization modeling hallucinations while preserving initially correct artifacts. These results demonstrate effective and controlled repair for LLM-based optimization modeling artifacts.
Infinite light rays and infinite clusters with infinitely many pivots

It is conjectured that in the Lorentz mirror model on $\Z^2$ all trajectories are finite. Quas showed that, almost surely, the two halves of any infinite trajectory, cut at an edge, meet at infinitely many vertices, each of which is pivotal: changing its state can make the trajectory finite. We construct plane graphs on which infinite trajectories exist, and all of them have this property. Given $p\in(0,1)$, we replace each edge of a random one-ended subtree of $\Z^2$ by a number of parallel edges, depending on $p$, that is at most logarithmic in the height of the corresponding descendant tree. The medial graph of the resulting plane multigraph is a factor of the tree, and for the uniform spanning tree it has finite vertex intensity. In the mirror model on this medial graph, with probability $p$ for mirrors along primal edges and any probability $r\in(0,1-p]$ for mirrors along dual edges, infinite trajectories exist, and the two halves of each of them meet infinitely often. The construction rests on Bernoulli percolation: every random one-ended locally finite tree can be decorated in this way such that bond percolation with parameter $p$ is critical and percolates, and every vertex of the infinite cluster has infinitely many pivotal edges. We characterize this property for bond and site percolation and for mirrors.

For $Δ\ge2$ and $q\ge11Δ/6$, we prove that the antiferromagnetic $q$-state Potts partition function on finite simple graphs of maximum degree at most $Δ$ has no Fisher zeros in a graph-uniform complex neighbourhood of $[0,1]$. For $q>11Δ/6$, the proof establishes coupling independence throughout $[0,1]$ using a soft version of Vigoda's flip dynamics. Our main tool is a separator-shell transfer theorem for the Potts model on induced-subgraph closed classes of graphs of maximum degree at most $Δ$, with $q\geΔ+1$. It yields a graph-uniform zero-free neighbourhood of $[0,1]$ from Hamming coupling independence at $0$ and a uniform coupling-independence bound on each interval $[δ,1]$, $δ\in(0,1]$. We also obtain zero-free Lee-Yang polydiscs around the uniform field for vertex- and edge-colour fields. For Boolean Holant problems on bounded-degree graphs whose signatures come from a fixed finite family of log-concave symmetric signatures $f$ with $f(0)>0$, such as $b$-matchings, we obtain graph-uniform zero-free polytubes around every bounded box of nonnegative activities; their union is an open zero-free neighbourhood of the nonnegative orthant. An appendix summarizes further coupling-independence inputs and the zero-free regions they yield.
Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds

We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.
Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
Ivan O. Shevchenko; Jun Liu; Xinzhi Liu

We study the decision problem of global asymptotic stability (GAS) of the origin for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients. In the first part of the paper we give, for every fixed dimension $n$ and odd degree $2k+1$, a computable map which sends a homogeneous vector field of degree $2k+1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ to a homogeneous cubic vector field on $\mathbb{R}^m$, $m=\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, and preserves both GAS and Lyapunov stability. The map passes to new variables $y_α=x^α$ (one for each monomial $x^α$ of degree $k$), in which the vector field becomes cubic, and adds a cubic penalty term transverse to the set of points of the form $(x^α)_{|α|=k}$; the main point is that this controls every initial state of the new system. As a consequence, the GAS problems for all degrees, for each fixed odd degree $d\ge3$, and for degree three are pairwise many-one equivalent. In the second part we prove that there are a fixed dimension $N_*$ and a fixed odd degree $d_*$ such that the set of homogeneous vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^{N_*}$ of degree $d_*$ whose origin is GAS is many-one complete. The reduction encodes an undecidable family of polynomial equations in integer unknowns into the constant term of a product of Jacobi theta series, realizes these series as outputs of a polynomial differential system with rational coefficients, and turns the existence of an integer solution into the sign of a maximal invariant average, which homogeneous GAS detects. Combining the two parts shows that GAS of rational homogeneous vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^N$ of degree $d$ is many-one complete for every odd $d\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $N$; in particular it is undecidable for cubic vector fields in a fixed dimension. Building on recent work, some analogous results are proven for Lyapunov stability of homogeneous vector fields.

The Hilton-Milner theorem is a classical theorem in extremal set theory which determines the maximum size of a nontrivial $k$-uniform intersecting family. In this paper, we prove an exact version of the Hilton-Milner theorem in the $\ell_2$-norm. Our method also gives an asymptotic version of the Hilton-Milner theorem in the $(j, p)$-norm.
Estimates on Fully Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unrectifiable Exceptional Gradient Sets

We study fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations that are imposed only when the gradients of solutions lie outside a closed ball and a closed purely one-unrectifiable set that can be unbounded. We prove Harnack inequalities and Hölder regularity estimates for viscosity solutions, with constants independent of the exceptional set. The proofs use the geometry of the contact sets in the cusp and barrier arguments to exclude exceptional gradients. We also provide examples and counterexamples showing the role of pure one-unrectifiability. Materials and proofs are presented in detail to ensure the paper is fully self-contained and accessible to a broad audience.
On Large Drift Enhancement for the Relaxation Time of Averages

In this note we prove in a broad analytic set-up a general result characterizing the asymptotic vanishing of the $L^2$-relaxation time of averages in the presence of a large incompressible drift-like term. The broad analytic set-up is analogous to that of Constantin-Kiselev-Ryzhik-Zlatos '08 or of Coti Zelati-Delgadino-Elgindi '20. A crucial role is played by the singular value gap method of Chatterjee '25, further developed by Eberle-Lörler '26.
Commitment over Gaussian channels with deterministic identification codes
Pau Colomer; Christian Deppe; Holge Boche; Andreas Winter

We establish a previously unnoticed connection between commitment (BC), a fundamental cryptographic primitive, and deterministic identification (DI), a post-Shannon communication setting. Specifically, for additive white Gaussian noise channels $\mathcal{G}$ we show that a reliable commitment protocol can be obtained from deterministic identification codes in both the honest but curious and fully dishonest security settings. This viewpoint allows BC schemes to inherit the asymptotic performance of DI codes. Indeed, we show that commitment is naturally achievable in the linearithmic regime, i.e., with message sets of size $N_n=\exp [Θ(n\log n)]$, and we establish a lower bound on the linearithmic-scale BC capacity of $\dot C_{\text{hBC}}(\mathcal G)\geq\frac12$ in the honest but curious case and $\dot C_{\text{BC}}(\mathcal G)\geq\frac14$ in the fully dishonest picture. This refines the best previously known characterisation of the commitment capacity over $\mathcal{G}$, which established only an infinite linear-scale capacity.
A neural characteristic mapping method: Lagrangian PINNs based on flow maps for transport-dominated problems
Martin Campos Pinto; Victor Fournet; Emmanuel Franck; Philipp Krah; Victor Michel-Dansac

We propose a novel numerical method for transport-dominated problems using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). In such problems, the solution can develop large gradients and fine structures over time. This is particularly challenging for classical PINNs, which represent the solution itself. In our approach, rather than the solution, we choose to approximate the flow map of the equation. The solution is then recovered by pulling back the exact initial condition, so that its fine structures are produced by the map rather than represented by the network. Our method is constructed by approximating the flow map of the equation with multiple PINNs, one per time subinterval, and composing them using the semigroup property of the flow, so that each network only has to represent a map close to the identity. To highlight the advantages of our method compared to classical PINNs or classical numerical schemes, we present numerical results on the linear advection equation, the incompressible Euler equation in vorticity formulation, the Vlasov-Poisson equation, and finally a drift-kinetic equation.
Tiling 3D by Translates of a Single Polycube is Undecidable

We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
Endpoint Compactness and Finite-Energy Weak Solutions for the 2D Isothermal Compressible Navier-Stokes

We prove global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the 2D isothermal compressible Navier--Stokes equations in bounded $C^2$ domains with no-slip boundary conditions. The initial data are arbitrary in the natural energy class, allowing vacuum and unbounded density. This resolves the isothermal endpoint $γ=1$ of the classical 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory for power-law pressures. We develop a new endpoint compactness argument based on a truncation-independent integrable bound for centered density oscillations. This argument yields strong $L^1$ compactness of the approximating densities at the natural energy level.
Platonic self-dual solitons in a (1+1)-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model

We construct a family of self-dual $(1+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^1$ sigma models whose potentials $V$ are determined from pre-potentials $U$ by Platonic geometry. Using the round metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\simeq\mathbb{CP}^1$ and the generalized self-duality formalism, we build symmetry-invariant pre-potentials $U$ from the unit vertices of each Platonic solid intersecting the unit circumsphere. The regular-lattice sites associated with vertex, face-center, and edge-midpoint directions are critical points of $U$ and degenerate vacua of the scalar potential $V$. Dual solids share the same regular lattice but generate different pre-potentials, charges, potentials, and metric-gradient flows. Numerical integration reveals distinct self-dual trajectories and energy-density profiles, including multi-peak structures for paths passing near saddle points, while solutions with the same endpoint difference $ΔU$ have the same total energy. The positive maxima of $V$ are also organized into symmetry orbits. This construction provides a geometric prescription for controlling the vacuum structure and self-dual sectors of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ models with a potential.
Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves

Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geomet- ric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently estab- lished Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.
Differential $T_2$-Duality and Spans of Principal 3-Bundles with Connections
Gianni Gagliardo; Christian Saemann; Roberto Tellez-Dominguez

We present a generalization of T-duality, called $T_2$-duality, that captures certain aspects of U-duality in M-theory. In particular, it features backgrounds that contain a 2-gerbe over a principal torus bundle, structures familiar from eleven-dimensional supergravity backgrounds. In special cases, it also incorporates S-duality in a precise sense. Our main result is a theorem characterizing $T_2$-dual pairs through spans of categorified principal bundles with connections, giving explicit rules for constructing a $T_2$-dual for a given background. A number of explicit examples illustrate how the various characteristic classes are mapped between the left and right backgrounds. For two-dimensional torus fibers, we also relate our construction to the combination of dimensional reduction and T-duality that links eleven-dimensional supergravity to type IIB supergravity. Finally, we discuss how $T_2$-duality arises from a Buscher-like span of 3d sigma models.
FeatureZ: A General Framework for Feature-Preserving Compression via Pointwise Bounds and Star Classification
Nathaniel Gorski; Xin Liang; Hanqi Guo; Bei Wang

Geometric and topological features, such as isosurfaces, quantiles, merge trees, and Morse-Smale complexes, are central to the analysis and visualization of scientific data across diverse domains, including medical imaging, climate science, materials science, and astronomy. However, most lossy compressors for scientific data provide only pointwise error guarantees and do not preserve derived features. Existing feature-preserving compressors are often difficult to develop and typically tailored to a single feature. In this paper, we introduce FeatureZ, a lossy compression framework for structured volumetric scalar fields that can preserve a wide class of geometric and topological features. In particular, FeatureZ frames feature-preserving compression as preserving pointwise upper and lower bounds together with a consistent classification of each point's star (i.e., its incident cells) in the underlying structured mesh. Although not all notions of feature preservation fit this framework, many features and topological descriptors targeted by existing compressors do. FeatureZ provides an efficient implementation of feature-preserving compression under this formulation. In particular, FeatureZ operates as an augmentation layer that refines the output of an existing lossy compressor. It first applies quantization to enforce pointwise bounds, and then employs an iterative procedure to ensure consistent star classification. We demonstrate that FeatureZ preserves diverse features during compression with minimal overhead, achieving compression ratios comparable to or better than methods specialized for individual features.
Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
Joel-Pascal Ntwali N'konzi; Feliks Nüske; Stefan Klus

Koopman operator theory provides a linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems and has become a major tool for data-driven modeling. A central challenge, however, is that finite-dimensional approximations computed by methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) require the dictionary to be specified a priori. Recent machine-learning approaches address this limitation by learning the dictionary from data, predominantly using artificial neural network (ANN) autoencoder architectures. Although kernel methods offer an alternative with greater interpretability and tractability for theoretical analysis, they have received little attention in this setting. We introduce extended dynamic mode decomposition with kernel-based dictionary learning (EDMD-kDL), a kernel-based method for learning finite-dimensional Koopman embeddings directly from data. The method combines ideas from collocation methods and bilevel optimization to simultaneously learn a kernel dictionary and the corresponding Koopman approximation. We evaluate EDMD-kDL against state-of-the-art ANN-based approaches on a range of numerical experiments, including global sea-surface-temperature forecasting and learning directly from video data. Across all tested settings, EDMD-kDL achieves performance comparable to or better than the ANN-based methods. Moreover, in contrast to standard kernel methods, the proposed approach is scalable to large datasets by design since the size of the required kernel matrices depends on the number of collocation points rather than the size of the training dataset.
Directed fractal percolation and non-Lipschitz variants
Shirshendu Ganguly; Victor Ginsburg; Kaihao Jing

While models of undirected and directed geometry in random i.i.d. disorder with rapidly decaying tails are expected to behave similarly and exhibit features of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang universality class, the scenario when the background noise is fractal is expected to be significantly different. A canonical example of the latter is Liouville Quantum Gravity, where the planar Gaussian free field forms the fractal background. A toy model capturing some of the essential features is given by Mandelbrot's fractal percolation, a random Cantor set. In the simplest setting, dyadic cubes of different scales are retained independently with probability $p$ (a parameter of the model), and the intersection of all retained cubes forms the set of open sites. Connectivity properties of such sets have been intensely studied. Across [CCD88, Cha95], a surprising result was proven. Namely, while there is a phase transition for connectivity of the fractal percolation set (like in usual bond percolation), directed percolation never occurs. Results of a similar spirit have been obtained in geometric measure theory as well. As a step towards understanding last passage percolation (LPP) driven by the Gaussian free field (initiated in [GGN24]), we study the problem of quantifying LPP in fractal percolation. Developing a multi-scale framework, we show an almost polynomial gap from linear growth of the passage time. The obstruction to high LPP values is the Lipschitz nature of directed paths. Along these lines, [Cha96] showed that any connected subset of fractal percolation must have Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than one. We show that one can construct directed paths passing through open sites in fractal percolation provided they move exponentially fast in the spatial direction---a model we introduce and term as unrectifiable directed percolation.
The moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled
Using in a novel way non-abelian Brill-Noether theory, we show that the moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled. This is the highest genus for which such a result is known.
Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube

We study Gaussian regression under squared population $L_2$ loss in a known $m$-dimensional subspace of degree-at-most-$k$ functions on the $d$-dimensional Boolean cube. Random inputs can undersample regions essential for prediction, delaying the parametric rate even when the model is known. For fixed $q_0<1/2$, $1\le k\le q_0d$, and sufficiently large fixed $A$, the worst-subspace sample threshold for minimax error $Aσ^2(m+t)/n$ with confidence $1-e^{-t}$, $t\ge\log4$, is \[ N=(m+t)\exp\{E_{d,k}+O(k^{1/3})\}, \quad E_{d,k}=dΨ(k/d), \] where $Ψ(q)=\log2-\mathsf H(\tfrac12-\sqrt{q(1-q)})$ and $\mathsf H$ is binary entropy with natural logarithms. The upper bound holds for every feasible $m$; the matching lower bound holds when $m\le\binom d{\lfloor k^{1/3}\rfloor}$ or $t\ge m$. We sharpen the Polyanskiy--Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle in two respects. First, for fixed leakage $ρ\in(0,1)$, the smallest set carrying a fraction $1-ρ$ of a nonzero degree-at-most-$k$ polynomial's energy has probability $\exp\{-E_{d,k}+O_{ρ,q_0}(k^{1/3})\}$. An Airy-kernel construction proves that the remainder cannot be $o(k^{1/3})$ in general. Second, we construct a subspace of dimension $\binom d{\lfloor k^{1/3}\rfloor}$ such that every function in the subspace has at least a fraction $1-ρ$ of its energy on the same set, whose probability is at most $\exp\{-E_{d,k}+C_{ρ,q_0}k^{1/3}\}$. For sufficiently large $k$, this set is a Hamming ball. A striking consequence is an exponential cost of noise: the parametric rate can require $(m+t)4^k\exp\{-O(k^{1/3})\}$ samples, whereas $O((m+t)2^k)$ suffice for noiseless identification. As $k\to\infty$ with $k/d\to0$, the noisy threshold is $(m+t)\exp\{2k+o(k)\}$.
Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection

We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI). Both problems concern polynomials $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, over a prime-order finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$. In LLR for Shamir secret sharing, one asks how much one can learn about $Q(0)$ given a few bits leaked from each of $Q(α_1), \ldots, Q(α_n)$, for distinct non-zero evaluation points $α_i \in \mathbb{F}_p$. In OPI, one is given input list $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subset \mathbb{F}_p$, and wants to find a polynomial $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$ so that $Q(α_i) \in S_i$ for as many $i$ as possible. Leveraging recent connection between these two problems due to (Sun, Wootters 2026), we improve the state-of-the-art for both problems. For LLR, we show that there is some constant $δ> 0$ so that, as long as $R := k/n \geq 1/2 - δ$, Shamir secret-sharing is one-bit locally leakage resilient (meaning that one can learn only a negligible amount about $Q(0)$). This is the first result to break the so-called "one-half barrier" for LLR, and improves over the previous best known result, requiring $R \geq 0.668$ (Kasser, 2025). For OPI, we give a quantum algorithm that finds a polynomial $Q(X)$ that agrees with at least a $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ(R)-\varepsilon$ fraction of the lists in expectation, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ$ is the \emph{semicircle law} of (Jordan et al., 2025). This improves previous algorithmic (and existential) results of (Jo, 2026) and (Horinaga, Yamakawa, 2026). We also give further improved existential results. We also adapt the hardness result of (Yamakawa, Zhandry, 2024) to apply to OPI (rather than a folded version); over large fields, this gives an unconditional separation between the quantum and classical hardness of OPI relative to a membership oracle.
Brownian motion with drift conditioned to have restricted $L^2$-norm
Frank Aurzada; Yuvraj Dutta; Max Wiegand

We study the long-time behaviour of Brownian motion with drift under a rare-event conditioning of the quadratic additive functional $Z_T=\int_0^T W_s^2ds$, where $(W_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a Brownian motion with drift $μ$. More precisely, we consider the conditional law of $W$ given the event $Z_T\le θT$, as $T\to\infty$, allowing the drift $μ$ to depend on $T$. We derive sharp, uniform small-deviation asymptotics for $Z_T$, including the exact prefactor, and use them to show that the conditioned process converges weakly to an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. Remarkably, the limiting dynamics are independent of the original drift.
Asymptotically Vanishing Excitation Without Loss of Parameter Convergence

Parameter convergence in recursive identification requires persistent excitation, which is typically enforced with a probing signal that degrades performance if retained indefinitely. Regulating the probing amplitude with the one-step prediction error is insufficient, since a small prediction error does not imply parameter convergence. This paper proposes a self-regulating excitation law that scales the probing amplitude with the associated covariance matrix, so that the excitation vanishes only as fast as the estimator's own measure of remaining parameter uncertainty allows. The key idea is that the excitation amplitude must decay more slowly than the covariance measure, the largest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix in this work, for parameter convergence to be preserved. Under the proposed excitation law, the excitation amplitude and the covariance measure are shown to jointly converge to zero while the parameter estimate converges to the true parameter, with the excitation vanishing more slowly than the covariance measure throughout. A scalar exponent in the law trades the rate of covariance decay against the amount of excitation retained. Numerical results confirm both properties.
The Colored Jones Function does not determine any colored Links--Gould polynomial

We prove that there is no uniform description of $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}$ in terms of colored Jones polynomials for all knots, even when allowing infinitely many colors and arbitrary operations. We prove the $n=1$ case, using an existing cabling formula and the separation of the Conway and Kinoshita--Terasaka knots by $\mathrm{LG}^{(2)}$. We develop an odd cabling formula and use a Vandermonde argument to show that for each $n\geq 2$ some satellite of each of these knots is distinguished by $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}$.
Prevalence of sparsity for negatively curved metrics

Let $M$ be a closed manifold of arbitrary dimension. The length spectrum of a negatively curved metric $g$ on $M$ is the set of lengths of all possible closed geodesics of $g$. We prove that metrics whose length spectrum is exponentially sparse, i.e., the gaps between distinct lengths are bounded below by a quantity decaying exponentially in the length, are prevalent, and hence dense, among $C^k$-smooth negatively curved metrics on $M$ for sufficiently large $k$. Moreover, unlike in all known constructions, the exponent in our bound grows only sublinearly in the regularity $k$. This work is motivated by our recent result on prevalent unmarked length spectral rigidity for expanding circle maps and a very recent result by DeWitt, Durham, Reber, and O'Hare that $C^k$-smooth negatively curved metrics with exponentially sparse spectra are locally rigid.
Edgar A. Bering IV; Samantha Ford; Aarav Ghai; Maxwell Lyon; Om Shah

The curve graph of a surface is the graph whose vertices are isotopy classes of essential, closed curves on the surface. Edges join vertices with disjoint representatives. The curve graph plays a central role in the theory of mapping class groups of surfaces. Gaster, Greene, and Vlamis have shown that the subgraph of the curve graph induced by curves in a single primitive homology class is uniquely and finitely colorable. In the analogy between the theory of mapping class groups of surfaces and outer automorphisms of free groups, the sphere graph of $M_r$, a connect sum of $r$ copies of $S_1 \times S_2$ plays an analogous role in the theory. Motivated by Gaster, Green, and Vlamis' result, we investigate $\mathcal{S}_v(M_r)$, the subgraph of the sphere graph of $M_r$ induced by spheres representing a single primitive homology class $[v] \in H_2(M_r;\mathbb{Z})$. We show that this graph is uniquely $r-1$ colorable. As a corollary, with $r\ge 3$ we obtain a nontrivial homomorphism from the Torelli subgroup $IO_r \le \operatorname{Out}(F_r)$ to the symmetric group on $r-1$ symbols; this parallels Gaster, Greene, and Vlamis' connection between their coloring and the Chillingworth homomorphism. In the course of our proof we find new smaller generating sets for mapping class groups of $M_r$ with spheres deleted.
Volume Sampling and Spectral Equalization in Randomized Alternating Projections
Alireza Entezari; Arunava Banerjee; Leila Kalantari

We study a family of randomized alternating projection methods that alternate among subspaces spanned by subsets of \(n\) vectors from a prescribed set. We derive an explicit characterization of performance bounds when these subspaces are sampled with probabilities proportional to the volumes subtended by the vectors in their corresponding subsets. For each \(n\), the bound is obtained through an explicit nonlinear transformation of the spectrum of an associated matrix. Our analysis reveals an explicit spectral equalization mechanism that drives the spectrum toward improved conditioning as $n$ increases, establishing an unexpected connection between volume sampling and the Cayley-Hamilton theorem. Furthermore, we introduce a computationally efficient uniform sampling scheme that achieves comparable theoretical guarantees through a specific relaxation strategy. Empirical results show that this relaxation method achieves convergence rates comparable to, and often better than, volume sampling, while avoiding the infeasibility of volume sampling at large scale. Besides the randomized Kaczmarz, these results also directly apply to randomized Gauss-Seidel and coordinate descent methods.
Geometrically Abelian Sections on Higher-Dimensional Varieties

We investigate how much arithmetic information about a variety can be detected by sections of the geometrically abelian fundamental groups of sufficiently small open subvarieties. Over a \(p\)-adic field, such a section determines a rational point on the Albanese torsor, and, under a conjectural assumption, this point is represented by a \(0\)-cycle of degree \(1\) on the original variety if the variety has index \(1\). For curves, the latter statement holds unconditionally. Over finitely generated fields, such sections still force the relative Brauer group to vanish away from the characteristic. The key input is an identification of the Chern class obstruction attached to a section with the obstruction arising from local Tate duality. As a byproduct, we give a new proof of an open-subvariety strengthening of a theorem of Esnault and Wittenberg.
Constraint Enforcement via Reference Governor in Dynamic Mode Adaptive Control

This paper integrates reference governance with Dynamic Mode Adaptive Control (DMAC) to enforce constraints without a prior plant model. DMAC identifies and updates a discrete-time model online from measured state and input data, and the reference governor (RG) uses this identified model, rather than the true plant dynamics, to predict constrained closed-loop behavior. Because the prediction model changes as DMAC adapts, a governed reference that was previously feasible may become infeasible, and the classical interpolation-based RG may be unable to move the reference in the direction required to recover predicted constraint satisfaction. The proposed DMAC-RG framework instead searches directly over the governed reference rather than over an interpolation factor. When feasible references exist, the governed reference is selected to track the desired command, with an optional penalty on deviation from the previously applied reference. When the finite-horizon feasible set is empty, the reference is selected to minimize predicted constraint violation while retaining the same tracking preference. This work is a numerical investigation and does not provide theoretical guarantees of recursive feasibility, constraint satisfaction, or closed- loop stability. Numerical examples on a linear system, a nonlinear Van der Pol oscillator, and a high-dimensional Burgers equation under partial-state measurement demonstrate that the proposed RG enforces constraints using only the model identified online by DMAC, without access to the true plant dynamics or the complete system state.
asdex: Automatic Sparse Differentiation in JAX

Many tasks in scientific computing and machine learning require the Jacobian or Hessian matrix of a function. Automatic differentiation (AD) computes these derivatives to machine precision, but materializing a dense $m \times n$ Jacobian requires $n$ forward-mode or $m$ reverse-mode AD passes, one per column or row. For a large class of functions, each output depends on only a few inputs, making the derivative matrix sparse. Automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) exploits this structure in four steps: detection of the input-agnostic sparsity pattern, coloring of a graph to group columns or rows that can share an AD pass, compressed differentiation to compute a compressed derivative matrix with one AD pass per color, and finally decompression into the original sparsity pattern. The number of colors, and hence of AD passes, is often independent of the problem dimension: a banded Jacobian with $b$ contiguous bands, for instance, only ever requires $b$ colors, regardless of its size. asdex offers the first standalone ASD toolkit in the popular JAX ecosystem. With $\texttt{asdex.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{asdex.hessian}$, it provides sparse drop-in replacements for $\texttt{jax.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{jax.hessian}$.
Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential
Scott Armstrong; Ahmed Bou-Rabee; Tuomo Kuusi

We study a Brownian particle in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\geq2$, with drift given by the gradient of a log-correlated Gaussian potential. At weak disorder, we prove convergence to a scaling limit whose law is singular with respect to Brownian motion and whose invariant measure is given by Gaussian multiplicative chaos. The proof uses a renormalization group induction: at each scale, the elliptic operator is well approximated by a Laplacian with effective diffusivity decaying as a power of scale. We compute this exponent exactly in dimension two.

In this paper, we study the nature of wave packets and their decay behavior in the $κ$-Minkowski space. We employ techniques from singularity theory throughout our analysis. Specifically, we use methods from the theory of Lagrangian singularities and caustics to study the topology of the energy-level manifold. The Newton polyhedron method from the theory of oscillatory integrals is applied to analyze the decay behavior of wave packets. We find that for a generic Hamiltonian in the $κ$-Minkowski space, the associated wave packets exhibit different decay rates depending on the control parameter of the system. When the control parameter takes values on the cusp, the system exhibits decay of order $t^{-1/4}$; otherwise, it exhibits decay of order $t^{-1/2}$. This distinctive behavior of wave packets in the $κ$-Minkowski makes it fundamentally different from commutative spacetime.
Characteristic cycles and the Gevrey filtration of irregularity in hypergeometric families

We show that the characteristic cycle multiplicities of $A$-hypergeometric systems are upper semicontinuous in the parameter for every rational projective weight, thereby proving a conjecture of Schulze and Walther [Duke Math. J. 142 (2008), 465--509].
